akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ﴾, i.e. by reckoning, and He implied the khabar (predicate). I think — and Allah knows best — that He meant "they run by reckoning".

akhfash:11-11.t: And He said ﴿ذَاتُ ٱلأَكْمَامِ﴾: its singular is "الكِمُّ" (sheath).

akhfash:48-48.t: And He said ﴿ذَوَاتَآ أَفْنَانٍ﴾: its singular is "الفَنَنُ" (branch).

akhfash:64-64.t: And He said ﴿مُدْهَآمَّتَانِ﴾, as you say "اِزْوَرَّ" and "اِزْوارَّ" (to turn aside).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَالنَّجْمُ﴾ plants that have no stem, ﴿وَالشَّجَرُ﴾ what has a stem, ﴿يَسْجُدَانِ﴾ submit to what is willed of them;

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَالسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ﴾ He established justice,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا﴾ that is, so that you do not act unjustly ﴿فِي الْمِيزَانِ﴾ that with which things are weighed;

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice, ﴿وَلَا تُخْسِرُوا الْمِيزَانَ﴾ do not diminish what is weighed.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا﴾ He set it firm ﴿لِلْأَنَامِ﴾ for creatures: humans, jinn and others;

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَالنَّخْلُ﴾ the familiar one, ﴿ذَاتُ الْأَكْمَامِ﴾ the sheaths of its spathes,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَالْحَبُّ﴾ such as wheat and barley, ﴿ذُو الْعَصْفِ﴾ straw, ﴿وَالرَّيْحَانُ﴾ the leaves, or the fragrant plant.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ﴾ the blessings of ﴿رَبِّكُمَا﴾ O humans and jinn, ﴿تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ It is mentioned thirty-one times, and the interrogative in it is for affirmation (taqrīr), because of what al-Ḥākim narrated from Jābir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Sūrat al-Raḥmān to us until he finished it, then said: Why do I see you silent? The jinn were better than you in response: I never recited to them this verse {فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ} but they said: Nor do we deny any of Your blessings, our Lord; to You belongs the praise."

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ﴾ Adam ﴿مِنْ صَلْصَالٍ﴾ dry clay that gives out a ṣalṣala, that is, a sound, when tapped, ﴿كَالْفَخَّارِ﴾ which is what is baked of clay,

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ﴾ the father of the jinn, and he is Iblīs, ﴿مِنْ مَارِجٍ مِنْ نَارٍ﴾ it is its flame free of smoke.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾ the rising place of winter and the rising place of summer ﴿وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ﴾ likewise.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿مَرَجَ﴾ He let loose ﴿الْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾ the sweet and the salt, ﴿يَلْتَقِيَانِ﴾ to the sight of the eye;

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ﴾ a barrier, of His, Exalted is He, power; ﴿لَا يَبْغِيَانِ﴾ neither of them encroaches on the other so as to mix with it.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿يُخْرَجُ﴾ in the passive and the active voice [يَخْرُجُ], ﴿مِنْهُمَا﴾ from the two together, which holds true of one of them, namely the salt, ﴿اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ﴾ red beads, or small pearls.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَلَهُ الْجَوَارِ﴾ the ships, ﴿الْمُنْشَآتُ﴾ the ones brought into being, ﴿فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ﴾ like mountains in size and height.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا﴾ that is, the earth, of living beings ﴿فَانٍ﴾ perishing; مَنْ is used giving precedence (taghlīb) to rational beings.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَيَبْقَى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ﴾ His essence, ﴿ذُو الْجَلَالِ﴾ majesty ﴿وَالْإِكْرَامِ﴾ to the believers, by His blessings upon them.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ that is, by speech or by their state, what they need: strength for worship, provision, forgiveness and other things; ﴿كُلَّ يَوْمٍ﴾ time ﴿هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ﴾ a matter that He brings forth in accordance with what He decreed from pre-eternity: giving life and death, exalting and abasing, enriching and impoverishing, answering the one who calls, giving to the one who asks, and other things.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ﴾ We will turn to your reckoning, ﴿أَيُّهَا الثَّقَلَانِ﴾ that is, humans and jinn.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا﴾ to get out ﴿مِنْ أَقْطَارِ﴾ the regions of ﴿السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا﴾ a command expressing [their] incapacity; ﴿لَا تَنْفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطَانٍ﴾ by power, and you have no power for that.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُمَا شُوَاظٌ مِنْ نَارٍ﴾ it is its flame free of smoke, or with it, ﴿وَنُحَاسٌ﴾ that is, smoke without flame; ﴿فَلَا تَنْتَصِرَانِ﴾ you will not protect yourselves from that; rather it will drive you to the place of gathering.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ﴾ opens up into gates for the angels to descend, ﴿فَكَانَتْ وَرْدَةً﴾ that is, like it, reddened, ﴿كَالدِّهَانِ﴾ like red leather, contrary to what is familiar of it; and the apodosis (jawāb) of إِذَا is: how great the terror then!

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُسْأَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إِنْسٌ وَلَا جَانٌّ﴾ about his sin; and they will be asked at another time: {فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَسْأَلَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ}. الْجَانُّ here and in what is to come means the jinn, and الْإِنْسُ means the human being.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿يُعْرَفُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيمَاهُمْ﴾ that is, the blackness of the faces and the blueness of the eyes, ﴿فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّوَاصِي وَالْأَقْدَامِ﴾

celaleyn:42-42.t:
﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ That is, the forelock of each of them is bound to his feet, from behind or in front, and he is thrown into the Fire; and it is said to them:
[Translator's note: this gloss explains the previous ayah (55:41); it is given here as it stands in the source.]

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿هَذِهِ جَهَنَّمُ الَّتِي يُكَذِّبُ بِهَا الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿يَطُوفُونَ﴾ they go back and forth ﴿بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ﴾ hot water ﴿آنٍ﴾ intensely hot, which they are given to drink when they cry for help from the heat of the Fire; it is a manqūṣ noun (ending in a weak yāʾ), like قَاضٍ.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَلِمَنْ خَافَ﴾ that is, for each of them, or for them collectively, ﴿مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ﴾ his standing before Him for the reckoning, and so abandoned disobedience to Him, ﴿جَنَّتَانِ﴾

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿ذَوَاتَا﴾ dual of ذَوَاتٍ in its original form, and its final radical (lām) is a yāʾ; ﴿أَفْنَانٍ﴾ branches, plural of فَنَنٍ, like طَلَلٍ.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿فِيهِمَا مِنْ كُلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ﴾ in this world, or everything that is enjoyed as fruit, ﴿زَوْجَانِ﴾ two kinds, fresh and dried; and the bitter of them in this world, such as colocynth, is sweet [there].

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) whose governing word (ʿāmil) is omitted, that is, they enjoy bliss ﴿عَلَى فُرُشٍ بَطَائِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾ the thick and coarse kind of brocade, while the outer sides are of fine silk (sundus); ﴿وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ﴾ their fruit ﴿دَانٍ﴾ near, reached by the one standing, the one sitting and the one lying down.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ in the two gardens and the upper chambers and palaces they contain, ﴿قَاصِرَاتُ الطَّرْفِ﴾ restraining their eyes to their husbands who recline, of humans and jinn; ﴿لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ﴾ deflowered them — and they are of the ḥūr, or of the women of this world, created anew — ﴿إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلَا جَانٌّ﴾

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿كَأَنَّهُنَّ الْيَاقُوتُ﴾ in purity ﴿وَالْمَرْجَانُ﴾ that is, pearls, in whiteness.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾ (meaning: not) ﴿جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ﴾ through obedience ﴿إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ﴾ through bliss.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿وَمِنْ دُونِهِمَا﴾ that is, the two gardens mentioned, ﴿جَنَّتَانِ﴾ also, for the one who fears the standing before his Lord.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿مُدْهَامَّتَانِ﴾ black from the intensity of their green.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ نَضَّاخَتَانِ﴾ gushing with water, never ceasing.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿فِيهِمَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ﴾ they [the palms and pomegranates] are part of it [fruit]; and it is said: not part of it.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ that is, the two gardens and what is in them, ﴿خَيْرَاتٌ﴾ in character, ﴿حِسَانٌ﴾ in face.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿حُورٌ﴾ with intensely black and intensely white eyes, ﴿مَقْصُورَاتٌ﴾ veiled ﴿فِي الْخِيَامِ﴾ of hollowed pearl, attached to the palaces, resembling curtained chambers.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ before their husbands ﴿وَلَا جَانٌّ﴾

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ that is, their husbands; and its i'rab is as before; ﴿عَلَى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ﴾ plural of رَفْرَفَةٍ, that is, carpets or cushions, ﴿وَعَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسَانٍ﴾ plural of عَبْقَرِيَّةٍ, that is, rugs.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿تَبَارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ﴾ This has been explained before; and the word اسْمٍ is redundant (zāʾid).

daas-irab:68-68.t: ﴿فِيهِما﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿فاكِهَةٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ﴾ both conjoined to what precedes them; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:70-70.t: ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿خَيْراتٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حِسانٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of خيرات; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:72-72.t: ﴿حُورٌ﴾ a badal (substitute) from خيرات. ﴿مَقْصُوراتٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of حور. ﴿فِي الْخِيامِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) مقصورات; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:76-76.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عَلى رَفْرَفٍ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them. ﴿خُضْرٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of رفرف. ﴿وَعَبْقَرِيٍّ﴾ conjoined to رفرف. ﴿حِسانٍ﴾ a ṣifa of عبقري.

daas-irab:78-78.t: ﴿تَبارَكَ اسْمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ذِي﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of ربك, and it is muḍāf. ﴿الْجَلالِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْإِكْرامِ﴾ conjoined to الجلال; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿الرَّحْمنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿خَلَقَ الْإِنْسانَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is a second khabar. ﴿عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيانَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; البيان is its second mafʿūl; the clause is a third khabar.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿الشَّمْسُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَالْقَمَرُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿بِحُسْبانٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وَالنَّجْمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَالشَّجَرُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿يَسْجُدانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَالسَّماءَ﴾ a conjunction, and mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned. ﴿رَفَعَها﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) and has no grammatical position, and the implied clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزانَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿أَلَّا﴾ an is a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative, and lā is negating. ﴿تَطْغَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿فِي الْمِيزانِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by an implied preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to وضع.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْوَزْنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا تُخْسِرُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الْمِيزانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned; the implied clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَضَعَها﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لِلْأَنامِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فِيها﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿فاكِهَةٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَالنَّخْلُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فاكهة. ﴿ذاتُ﴾ an adjective. ﴿الْأَكْمامِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَالْحَبُّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فاكهة. ﴿ذُو﴾ an adjective. ﴿الْعَصْفِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالرَّيْحانُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and بأي: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تكذبان. ﴿آلاءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿رَبِّكُما﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تُكَذِّبانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿خَلَقَ الْإِنْسانَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ صَلْصالٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿كَالْفَخَّارِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of صلصال.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ مِنْ مارِجٍ﴾ its i'rab is like the preceding one. ﴿مِنْ نارٍ﴾ an adjective of مارج; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿رَبُّ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to المشرقين. ﴿الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَلْتَقِيانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿بَيْنَهُما بَرْزَخٌ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate) and a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿لا﴾ negating; and ﴿يَبْغِيانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿يَخْرُجُ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْهُمَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿اللُّؤْلُؤُ﴾ fāʿil (agent), nominative. ﴿وَالْمَرْجانُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to اللؤلؤ; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿الْجَوارِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿الْمُنْشَآتُ﴾ an adjective of الجوار. ﴿فِي الْبَحْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) المنشئات. ﴿كَالْأَعْلامِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿كُلُّ مَنْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) annexed to the relative noun, and the relative noun is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿فانٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, it being a defective noun (ism manqūṣ); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿وَيَبْقى وَجْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ذُو﴾ an adjective of وجه, in construct (muḍāf). ﴿الْجَلالِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْإِكْرامِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الجلال; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿يَسْئَلُهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿مَنْ﴾ its fāʿil (agent). ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السموات; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ an adverb, in construct (muḍāf). ﴿يَوْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي شَأْنٍ﴾ khabar (predicate).

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿سَنَفْرُغُ﴾ the sīn is for futurity, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَيُّهَ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda). ﴿الثَّقَلانِ﴾ badal (substitute); the vocative clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿يا مَعْشَرَ﴾ a vocative (munādā) in construct. ﴿الْجِنِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْإِنْسِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ in is a conditional particle, and a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of استطعتم. ﴿مِنْ أَقْطارِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات. ﴿فَانْفُذُوا﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿تَنْفُذُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بِسُلْطانٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb.

daas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿يُرْسَلُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْكُما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿شُواظٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ نارٍ﴾ an adjective of شواظ. ﴿وَنُحاسٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to شواظ. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and lā is negating. ﴿تَنْتَصِرانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿فَإِذَا﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and إذا is an adverbial conditional particle not governing the jussive. ﴿انْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فَكانَتْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir). ﴿وَرْدَةً﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَالدِّهانِ﴾ an adjective of وردة.

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and يومئذ is an adverb of time annexed to idh. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُسْئَلُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿إِنْسٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is the apodosis. ﴿وَلا جَانٌّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to إنس.

daas-irab:41-41.t: ﴿يُعْرَفُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِسِيماهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فَيُؤْخَذُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿بِالنَّواصِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun standing in the place of the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿وَالْأَقْدامِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to النواصي; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿هذِهِ جَهَنَّمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted saying. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective of جهنم. ﴿يُكَذِّبُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿بِهَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:44-44.t: ﴿يَطُوفُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بَيْنَها﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿وَبَيْنَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بينها. ﴿حَمِيمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿آنٍ﴾ an adjective of حميم, genitive (majrūr) by the implied (muqaddar) kasra on the omitted yāʾ.

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وَلِمَنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿خافَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مَقامَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿جَنَّتانِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of man, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:48-48.t: ﴿ذَواتا﴾ an adjective of جنتان. ﴿أَفْنانٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:50-50.t: ﴿فِيهِما﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿عَيْنانِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause has no grammatical position. ﴿تَجْرِيانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is an adjective of عينان.

daas-irab:51-51.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ﴾ its i'rab has preceded.

daas-irab:52-52.t: ﴿فِيهِما﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فاكِهَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿زَوْجانِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:54-54.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿عَلى فُرُشٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them. ﴿بَطائِنُها﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is an adjective of فرش. ﴿وَجَنَى﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ in construct (muḍāf). ﴿الْجَنَّتَيْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿دانٍ﴾ khabar; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:56-56.t: ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿قاصِراتُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), in construct (muḍāf). ﴿الطَّرْفِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl (object). ﴿إِنْسٌ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿وَلا جَانٌّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to إنس.

daas-irab:58-58.t: ﴿كَأَنَّهُنَّ﴾ كأن and its noun. ﴿الْياقُوتُ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿وَالْمَرْجانُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الياقوت; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:60-60.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾ a particle of interrogation. ﴿جَزاءُ الْإِحْسانِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) annexed to الإحسان. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الْإِحْسانِ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source vowels the khabar with kasra (الْإِحْسانِ); as khabar the Quranic word is الْإِحْسانُ.]

daas-irab:62-62.t: ﴿وَمِنْ دُونِهِما﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿جَنَّتانِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:66-66.t: [Translator's note: the source text of this entry is garbled: the quotation brackets and first letters of the Quranic words are lost (it reads «ِيهِما», «يْنانِ», «ضَّاخَتانِ»). The words are restored below from the verse, ﴿فِيهِما عَيْنانِ نَضَّاخَتانِ﴾.] ﴿فِيهِما﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿عَيْنانِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿نَضَّاخَتانِ﴾ an adjective of عينان; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:1-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْبَيانَ): linguistically, eloquent speech that expresses clearly what is in the mind. Technically, it is one of the three disciplines of rhetoric (balāgha); it examines simile (tashbīh), metaphor (istiʿāra), figurative usage (majāz) and allusion (kināya). Examples of these have preceded in this book.
(بِحُسْبانٍ): ḥusbān is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of "ḥasabtuhu aḥsubuhu ḥisāban wa-ḥusbānan" (I reckoned it). It is also said to be the plural of ḥisāb, like shihāb / shuhbān and raghīf / rughfān.
(النَّجْمُ): among plants, that which does not stand on a stem, such as grass and herbs, while "shajar" (trees) is that which stands on a stem. Its root meaning is rising/appearing; one says "najama al-qarnu wa-l-nabātu" when the horn and the plant come out. From this the star of the sky (najm) was named. It is also said that it is the star of the sky, singular, and that by it all the stars are meant.
(القسط): justice — "they only did it straight, with justice." [Translator's note: so in the source, «إنما فعلوه مستقيما بالعدل»; compare the I'rab below: «افعلوه مستقيما بالعدل».] Abū ʿUbayda said: "Setting upright (iqāma) is with the hand, and qisṭ is with the heart."
(الْأَكْمامِ): plural of kimm, which is the sheath of the blossom. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "al-kimm, with kasra, and al-kimāma are the sheath of the spathe and the cover of the blossom; the plural is kimām, akimma, akmām and also akāmīm. Al-kimām, with kasra, and al-kimāma are also that with which a camel's mouth is muzzled so that it does not bite; from it one says 'baʿīrun makmūm', i.e. muzzled (maḥjūm). 'Takammamtu al-shayʾa' means I covered the thing. Al-kamm is what conceals and covers something; from it comes 'kumm al-qamīṣ' (the sleeve of the shirt), with ḍamma, plural kimām and kimama. Al-kumma is the round cap, because it covers the head."
(الْعَصْفِ): that part of the crop which is blown about (yuʿṣaf) and eaten. It is also said: al-ʿaṣf is the leaves of everything from which grain comes out.
(الرَّيْحانُ): in al-Mukhtār: "al-rayḥān is a well-known plant, and it is also provision (rizq); al-ʿaṣf is the stalk of the crop and al-rayḥān its leaves, according to al-Farrāʾ." It is also said: al-ʿaṣf is straw. In al-Asās: "They became like the ʿaṣf of the crop, which is the broken and fine bits of straw."
(آلاءِ): favours; its singular is ilā; and ilā [also takes the forms] alā, like maʿā and ḥaṣā, and ilā and ilī — four forms. [Translator's note: the source has «أربع نعات», evidently for «أربع لغات» (four dialectal forms).]

* I'rab:
(الرَّحْمنُ، عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ): (الرحمن) is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (علم القرآن) is the khabar (predicate). The predicates are multiple in the verbs that come without a conjunction, in the manner of enumeration and of establishing the proof against the unbelievers. This is according to those who do not consider (الرحمن) a verse. Those who count it as a verse parse (الرحمن) as the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "Allah is the Most Merciful", or as a subject whose predicate is omitted, i.e. "the Most Merciful is our Lord". [Translator's note: the source has «أعرف», evidently for «أعرب» (parsed).] (علّم) is doubly transitive; its first object has been omitted for the sake of its comprehensiveness, i.e. He taught whoever learns. This is better than restricting the omitted first object to a single specific person.
(خَلَقَ الْإِنْسانَ عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيانَ): a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (علّمه البيان) is a past verb, a latent agent and its two objects. The alif and lām in (الإنسان) are generic.
(الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبانٍ): (الشمس) is a subject, (القمر) is conjoined to it, and (بحسبان) is the predicate of (الشمس).
(وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدانِ): conjoined to what preceded, and the clause (يسجدان) is the predicate of (النجم).
(وَالسَّماءَ رَفَعَها وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزانَ): the wāw is conjunctive; (السماء) is the direct object of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned, and the clause (رفعها) is explicative, with no grammatical position; (وضع الميزان) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object.
(أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزانِ): (أن) is maṣdarī (infinitival) and (لا) negating; (تطغوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the infinitival (أن); (أن) and what follows it are in the position of the genitive by an implied lām of cause, and the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It is also permissible for (أن) to be explicative (mufassira) and (لا) prohibitive, with (تطغوا) jussive (majzūm) by (لا). If it is said that a condition of the explicative [أن] is that it be preceded by a clause containing the meaning of saying without its letters, we say: setting up the balance calls for speech, namely the command to be just in it.
(وَأَقِيمُوا الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ وَلا تُخْسِرُوا الْمِيزانَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أقيموا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its agent; (الوزن) is a direct object; (بالقسط) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. do it straight, with justice. The wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تخسروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا), and the wāw is its agent; (الميزان) is a direct object.
(وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَها لِلْأَنامِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (الأرض) is the direct object of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned, and the clause (وضعها) is explicative, with no grammatical position; (للأنام) is attached to (وضعها), i.e. He made it level and spread it out for the creatures.
(فِيها فاكِهَةٌ وَالنَّخْلُ ذاتُ الْأَكْمامِ): (فيها) is a fronted predicate and (فاكهة) a delayed subject; (النخل) is conjoined to (فاكهة); (ذات الأكمام) is a naʿt (adjective) of (النخل); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of (الأرض).
(وَالْحَبُّ ذُو الْعَصْفِ وَالرَّيْحانُ): conjoined to what preceded; in the reading of the majority the three are conjoined to (فاكهة), and in the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir the three are in the accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "He created".
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition); (بأي) is attached to (تكذبان); (آلاء) is a muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct); (ربكما) is annexed to (آلاء) [Translator's note: so in the source, «مضاف لآلاء»; i.e. it is the second term of the construct with (آلاء)]; (تكذبان) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is its agent. The address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), humankind and jinn, and this will be stated explicitly. This verse is repeated thirty-one times, and the secret of its repetition will come in the Rhetoric section.

* Rhetoric:
1- Repetition (al-takrīr): in His words (فبأيّ آلاء ربكما تكذبان) there is a sweet repetition; what was said about it has preceded. The secret in repeating the verse after verses enumerating the wonders of Allah's creation and the marvels of His making, and after verses mentioning the Fire and its terrors, is that among the favours are the lifting of affliction and the deferral of punishment, [together with] eliciting acknowledgement (taqrīr) of the enumerated favours and emphasis in reminding of all of them; and because this kind of repetition is one of the signs of intense emotion. Laylā al-Akhyaliyya said, lamenting Tawba ibn al-Ḥumayyir:
لنعم الفتى يا توب كنت ولم تكن ... لتسبق يوما كنت فيه تحاول
ونعم الفتى يا توب كنت لخائف ... أتاك لكي تحمي ونعم المجامل
ونعم الفتى يا توب كنت إذا التقت ... صدور المعالي واستثال الأسافل
ونعم الفتى يا توب جارا وصاحبا ... ونعم الفتى يا توب حين تناضل لعمري لأنت المرء أبكي لفقده ... ولو لام فيه ناقص الرأي
جاهل لعمري لأنت المرء أبكي لفقده ... إذا كثرت بالملجمين ال
تلاتل أبى لك ذم الناس يا توب كلما ... ذكرت أمورا محكمات
كوامل أبى لك ذم الناس يا توب كلما ... ذكرت سماح حين تأوي الأ
رامل فلا يبعدنك الله يا توب إنما ... كذاك المنايا عاجلات
وآجل فلا يبعدنك الله يا توب إنما ... لقيت حمام الموت والموت عاجل
(What an excellent young man you were, O Tawba, never outstripped on a day you strove for something; excellent to one in fear who came to you for protection, and excellent in courtesy; excellent when the leading men met in glory; excellent as neighbour and companion, and when you contended. By my life, you are the man whose loss I weep, even if one of deficient judgement and ignorant blames me for it, when the bridled riders are beset by hardships. Your nature refused people's censure, O Tawba, whenever perfect, well-made deeds were mentioned, and generosity when the widows seek shelter. May Allah not take you far, O Tawba; so are the fates, swift and delayed; you have only met the decree of death, and death is swift.) [Translator's note: the line layout of these verses is disordered in the source — hemistichs run together and words are split across lines (e.g. «ال / تلاتل», «الأ / رامل»); they are reproduced as printed.]
So in these verses she went from repetition to repetition because of the differing meanings she enumerated. Examples of repetition are too many to count; the interrogative in it is for eliciting acknowledgement (taqrīr).
2- Ellipsis (al-ḥadhf): in His words (علّم القرآن) there is ellipsis: the first object has been omitted because the meaning indicates it, since the favour lies in the teaching, not in teaching one person rather than another — just as one says "So-and-so feeds people (yuṭʿimu al-ṭaʿām)", indicating his generosity without specifying whom he fed.
3- In His words (والشمس والقمر بحسبان والنجم والشجر يسجدان) there is the device of tawhīm (creating a false impression). Reference to it has preceded: it consists of the speaker bringing a word such that the rest of the speech, before or after it, makes [the hearer] imagine that the speaker intended it to share its wording with another word, or intended a misreading of its dots (taṣḥīf), or an alteration (taḥrīf), or a different i'rab, or a different meaning, or some other kind of variation, whereas the matter is the opposite. For the mention of the sun and the moon makes the hearer imagine that (النجم) is one of the stars of the sky, whereas what is meant is the plant that has no stem. Of this kind is the saying of Abū Tammām:
من كل أبيض يجلو منه سائله ... خدا أسيلا به خد من الأسل
(Every white [blade] whose flowing [blood] reveals a smooth cheek, in which there is a gash from the spears.)
For the mention of the smooth cheek — i.e. soft and radiant — makes one imagine that by "khadd min al-asal" something like it is meant, from spears, whereas what is meant is the wound. Among it is the false impression of taṣḥīf; its example is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib:
وإن الفئام التي حوله ... لتحسد أرجلها الأرؤس
(The throngs around him — their heads envy their feet.)
For the word "feet" made the hearer imagine that al-Mutanabbī meant "al-qiyām" (those standing), whereas he meant "al-fiʾām", with the single-dotted fāʾ, i.e. the multitudes; because "al-qiyām" applies to the minimum of a plural, and so the hyperbole would be lost.
4- In His words (والأرض وضعها للأنام) to the end of the verses in which He, glory be to Him, enumerated His favours, there is evidence that harshness and taking the hardest path, which is burdensome for the responsible person, are not praiseworthy, because the Law did not aim at tormenting the soul. It is narrated from al-Rabīʿ ibn Ziyād al-Ḥārithī that he said to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him: "Help me against my brother ʿĀṣim." He said: "What is the matter with him?" He said: "He has put on the cloak (ʿabāʾa), intending asceticism." ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Bring him to me." He was brought, wrapped in one cloak as a waist-wrapper and wearing another as an upper garment, his head and beard dishevelled. ʿAlī frowned at him and said:
"Woe to you! Are you not ashamed before your family? Have you no mercy for your children? Do you think that Allah made good things lawful for you while disliking that you take any of them? Rather, you are too insignificant to Allah for that. Have you not heard Allah say in His Book: (والأرض وضعها للأنام) up to His words (يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان)? Do you think Allah made these lawful for His servants for any reason other than that they use them and praise Allah for them, so that He rewards them for it? Your putting Allah's favours to use in deed is better than doing so in word." ʿĀṣim said: "Then what about you, with your coarse food and coarse clothing?" He said: "Woe to you! Allah has obliged the rightful leaders to measure themselves by the condition of the people."
Moreover, the Prophet ﷺ used to eat good food when he found it; he loved sweets and honey, he liked the meat of the foreleg, and sweet water was sought for him. So where is harshness in this? Hence, confining oneself to unpleasant food without excuse is extremism.

dervis-irab:14-30.t:
* Vocabulary:
(صَلْصالٍ): ṣalṣāl is dry clay that has a ṣalṣala, i.e. a sound, when it is tapped.
(الفخار): clay baked by fire, i.e. earthenware.
(الْجَانَّ): the father of the jinn; the al- in it is generic.
(مارِجٍ): al-mārij is the pure flame that has no smoke. It is also said to be that which is mixed with the blackness of the fire, from "maraja al-shayʾu" when a thing is agitated and mixed.
(مَرَجَ): He mixed. The meaning of (مرج البحرين) is: He mixed the two seas, the sweet and the salty, to the sight of the eye, and yet neither encroaches upon the other. The root meaning of al-marj is leaving loose, as an animal roams freely (tamruju) in the pasture. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-marj is land with vegetation and pasture; the plural is murūj, like fals / fulūs. 'Marajat al-dābba tamruju marjan', of the pattern qatala: it grazed in the marj; 'marajtuhā marjan': I sent it to graze in the marj. It is used both transitively and intransitively."
(بَرْزَخٌ): al-barzakh is the barrier between two things; its plural is barāzikh.
(اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ): pearls (al-durr); and al-marjān is this red bead [i.e. coral]. Al-Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā said: "It is a kind of pearl like rods, and al-marjān is a foreign noun that has been Arabised." Ibn Durayd said: "I have not heard a conjugated form (naql mutaṣarrif) of it." Al-Aʿshā said:
من كل مرجانة في البحر أحرزها ... تيارها ووقاها طينها الصدف
(Of every pearl in the sea, which its current has guarded and whose shell has protected it from its mud.)
It is also said: [they are] red veins that grow out of the sea like the fingers of the hand.
(الجواري): ships; plural of jāriya. Al-Tirmidhī said: "First [it is called] fulk, then safīna, then jāriya; it was so named because it runs (tajrī) in the water."
(كَالْأَعْلامِ): al-aʿlām is the plural of ʿalam, which is a mountain. Al-Khansāʾ said:
وإن صخرا لتأتم الهداة به ... كأنه علم في رأسه نار
(Indeed Ṣakhr — the guides take him as their leader, as though he were a mountain with a fire on its top.)

* I'rab:
(خَلَقَ الْإِنْسانَ مِنْ صَلْصالٍ كَالْفَخَّارِ): resumptive speech, set forth to rebuke them for neglecting the duty of thanking the Bestower for His bestowal. (خلق) is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah the Exalted; (الإنسان) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من صلصال) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خلق); (كالفخار) is a naʿt (adjective) of (صلصال).
(وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ مِنْ مارِجٍ مِنْ نارٍ): conjoined to what preceded; (من مارج) is attached to (خلق), and (من) is for the beginning of the extent; (من نار) is an adjective of (مارج), and (من) is explicative or partitive.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ): (رب المشرقين) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is the Lord of the two easts", and (رب المغربين) is conjoined to it. What is meant is the summer rising-place and the winter rising-place, and the summer setting-place and the winter setting-place. It is also said that by the two easts is meant the rising-place of the sun and the moon, and by the two wests the setting-place of the sun and the moon. He, glory be to Him, has made clear His power to direct the sun and the moon, and whoever has power over that has power over everything. It is also said that it is a subject whose predicate is the clause (مرج البحرين); the first is better.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيانِ): (مرج البحرين) is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; the clause (يلتقيان) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is close to the anticipated ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muqaddara), and it may also be a concomitant one (muqārina).
(بَيْنَهُما بَرْزَخٌ لا يَبْغِيانِ): the adverb is attached to an omitted fronted predicate, and (برزخ) is a delayed subject; (لا) is negating and (يبغيان) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the clause is an adjective of (برزخ). The whole clause is resumptive, or a ḥāl of the pronoun in (يلتقيان). The meaning of (لا يبغيان) is that neither of them oversteps its bounds: the sweet one is singular in its sweetness and the salty one singular in its saltiness.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ): the clause is resumptive, or a second ḥāl of the pronoun in (يلتقيان); (منهما) is attached to (يخرج); (اللؤلؤ) is the agent of (يخرج), and (المرجان) is conjoined to (اللؤلؤ).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(وَلَهُ الْجَوارِ الْمُنْشَآتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلامِ): the wāw is resumptive; (له) is a fronted predicate and (الجوار) a delayed subject. The yāʾ was dropped in the script because it is one of the supernumerary yāʾs (yāʾāt al-zawāʾid). (المنشآت) is an adjective of (الجوار); (في البحر) is attached to (المنشآت); (كالأعلام) is a ḥāl of (الجوار) or of the pronoun in (المنشآت), and the meaning is the same.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْها فانٍ): (كل) is a subject; (من) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by annexation to (كل); (عليها) is attached to an omitted [verb] which has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); (فان) is the predicate of (كل), and the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
(وَيَبْقى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلالِ وَالْإِكْرامِ): the wāw is conjunctive; (يبقى) is an imperfect verb, nominative; (وجه ربك) is its agent; (ذو الجلال) is an adjective of (وجه), and (الإكرام) is conjoined to (الجلال).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(يَسْئَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ): resumptive speech, beginning the enumeration of further favours of His, glory be to Him. You may also make the clause a ḥāl of (وجه), with (يبقى) governing it, i.e. it remains in the state of being asked by the people of the heavens and the earth. (يسأله) is an imperfect verb, and its implied object — what is asked for — is omitted [Translator's note: the source reads «ومفعوله المقدّم السؤال محذوف»]: the people of the heavens ask Him for forgiveness, and the people of the earth ask Him for forgiveness and provision. (كل يوم) is an adverb attached to the [notion of] being-located (al-istiqrār) to which the predicate of (هو) is attached; (هو) is a subject and (في شأن) the predicate.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words (يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان) there is the device of ittisāʿ (latitude of expression), which has been discussed in detail before. Coming out has been ascribed to the pearls and coral, because if that is brought out, it has come out. And He said "from both of them" and not "from one of them", because when they met and became like a single thing, it was acceptable to say "from both of them". Its like has been discussed before, namely His words (لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم), where only one of the two towns is meant; and as you say, "So-and-so is from the people of the lands of Syria," while his town is only one of them.
2- In His words (وله الجوار المنشآت في البحر كالأعلام) there is a mursal simile (tashbīh mursal, with the particle of comparison stated): He likened the ships, as they cleave the surging sea coming and going, to mountains. This simile captivated the poets, who borrowed it. Ibn al-Rūmī said:
أين فلك فيها وفلك إليها ... منشآت في البحر كالأعلام
(Where are ships [sailing] in it and ships [sailing] to it, raised up in the sea like mountains?)
3- In His words (كل من عليها فان ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام) there is a charming device, the device of iftinān (combining two modes). Its definition is that the speaker displays versatility, bringing in his speech two modes, either opposite, different or concordant. He, glory be to Him, has combined consolation and self-glorification: He consoled all creatures, and praised Himself for being alone in remaining after the perishing of all existing things, while describing Himself, after His being alone in remaining, with majesty and honour. Among its examples in poetry is combining love poetry (ghazal) and martial poetry (ḥamāsa) — love poetry being softness and tenderness, and martial poetry harshness and strength — like the saying of Abū Dulaf or ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir, the historians differing:
أحبك يا ظلوم وأنت عندي ... مكان الروح من جسد الجبان
ولو أني أقول مكان روحي ... خشيت عليك بادرة الطعان
(I love you, O unjust one, and you are to me as the soul is to the coward's body; had I said "as my own soul", I would fear for you the sudden thrust of spears.)
So he combined love poetry and martial poetry in the most elegant expression and the most eloquent allusion. ʿAntara reached the summit in it when he said:
إن تغدفي دوني القناع فإنني ... طب يأخذ الفارس المستلئم
(If you let your veil fall before me, I am skilled at seizing the mail-clad horseman.)
He described ʿAbla as covering her face from him with the veil, until what was between his sight and her face became like the dark, curtained night that comes between eyes and what they see. Then he said: "I am skilled at seizing (bi-akhdh) the mail-clad horseman" [Translator's note: the verse as quoted has «يأخذ», while the explanation has «بأخذ»], i.e. if you veil yourself from me, I am — through my experience of war — expert at seizing the horseman whose armour covers him and stands between me and facing him. So he presented earnestness in the guise of jest, and in his verse, along with iftinān, came a charming witticism (tandīr) and the expression of the meaning in noble wording.

dervis-irab:31-45.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَنَفْرُغُ): al-Zajjāj said: "Being free (al-farāgh) in the language is of two kinds: one is being free from occupation, and the other is directing oneself to a thing and turning towards it, as here — and it is a threat and warning. You say 'I have finished (faraghtu) with what I was engaged in', i.e. my occupation with it has ended; and you say 'I shall attend (sa-afrughu) to so-and-so', i.e. I shall make him my aim. So it is by way of figurative representation (tamthīl): His management, the Exalted, of the affair of the Hereafter — undertaking the recompense and delivering reward and punishment to those held responsible — after His management, the Exalted, of the affair of this world by command and prohibition, causing death and giving life, withholding and giving — while no matter distracts Him from another — has been likened to the state of one who, when engaged in an occupation that distracts him from another occupation, starts on the other once he has finished with that one."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is borrowed from a man's saying to someone he threatens: 'I shall make myself free for you (sa-afrughu laka)', meaning: I shall strip myself of everything that occupies me away from you in order to fall upon you, so that I have no occupation other than that. What is meant is devoting oneself fully to harming him and taking vengeance on him. It may also be meant: the world will come to an end and reach its last point, and at that the affairs of creation will end, which He meant by His words (كل يوم هو في شأن), so that only one affair remains, namely your recompense; and that was made 'becoming free' by way of a figurative expression."
It is concluded from the foregoing that being free (farāgh) is among the attributes of bodies in which accidents inhere and occupy them, away from their contraries, in that state; that is why it must be figurative (majāz) in describing the Eternal, the Exalted.
(الثَّقَلانِ): its origin is from al-thiql (weight); anything that has weight and worth is a thaqal. From it the ostrich's egg is called thaqal. [The poet] said:
فتذكرا ثقلا رتيدا بعد ما ... ألقت ذكاء يمينها في كافر
(The two [ostriches] remembered a carefully laid egg, after the sun had cast its right hand into the night.)
Humankind and jinn were called the two thaqals only because of their great importance and the majesty of their station in relation to the animals on earth, and because of the heaviness of their weight through reason and discernment. From it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "I am leaving among you the two weighty things (al-thaqalayn): the Book of Allah and my family (ʿitratī)." He called them two thaqals because of their great importance and the majesty of their worth. It is also said that the jinn and humankind were called two thaqals because of their weight upon the earth while living [Translator's note: the source has «إحياء»; evidently «أحياء» (living)]. From it are the words of Allah the Exalted (وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها), i.e. it brought out the dead that are in it. The Arabs make the brave chief a weight (thiql) upon the earth. Al-Khansāʾ said:
أبعد ابن عمرو من آل الشريد ... حلّت به الأرض أثقالها
(After Ibn ʿAmr of the family of al-Sharīd, the earth has cast off its burdens through him.)
The meaning is: when he died, a weight was lifted from it by his death, because of his lordship and glory. It is also said that the meaning is: it adorned its dead, from taḥliya (adornment).
(أَقْطارِ): al-aqṭār is the plural of al-quṭr, which is the side. One says "ṭaʿanahu fa-qaṭṭarahu" when he struck him and threw him onto one of his two sides (quṭrayhi), i.e. his flanks.
(بِسُلْطانٍ): with power, domination and mastery.
(شُواظٌ): al-shuwāẓ, with ḍamma or kasra on the shīn. Abū ʿUbayda said: it is flame without smoke. Ruʾba said:
إنّ لهم من حربنا إيقاظا ... ونار حرب تسعر الشواظا
(For them our war holds an awakening, and a fire of war that kindles the smokeless flame.)
(وَنُحاسٌ): al-nuḥās is smoke. He recited, from al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī:
تضيء كضوء سراج السلي ... ط لم يجعل الله فيه نحاسا
(She shines like the light of a lamp of [sesame] oil, in which Allah has put no smoke.)
It is also said: [it is] molten brass poured upon their heads.
(كَالدِّهانِ): about al-dihān there are two views. One is that it is the plural of duhn (oil), like qurṭ / qirāṭ and rumḥ / rimāḥ, and it is in the meaning of His words (يوم تكون السماء كالمهل), al-muhl being the dregs of oil. The second is that it is a singular noun. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "a noun for that with which one anoints, like al-ḥizām and al-idām." [Translator's note: the source prints «كالجزام», evidently for «كالحزام».] It is also said that it is red leather.
(بِسِيماهُمْ): al-sīmā is derived from al-sawm, which is raising the price above its measure; and the mark is raised by being displayed so that recognition occurs by it.
(بِالنَّواصِي): plural of nāṣiya, which is the hair of the front of the head; its root meaning is connection, for the forelock is connected to the head.
(حَمِيمٍ): hot water.
(آنٍ): intensely hot; its verb is "anā yaʾnī anyan".

* I'rab:
(سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ الثَّقَلانِ): resumptive speech, set forth for threat and warning. The sīn is a particle of the future; (نفرغ) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu" (We); (لكم) is attached to (نفرغ); (أيّه الثقلان) is a vocative of the intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda) from which the vocative particle has been omitted, and (الثقلان) is a badal (substitute) of (أيّه).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(يا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا مِنْ أَقْطارِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا): (يا) is the vocative particle and (معشر الجن) the one addressed, in a genitive construct (muḍāf); (الإنس) is conjoined to (الجن). (إن) is conditional; (استطعتم) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (أن) is an infinitival particle that puts in the accusative, and (تنفذوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (أن); (أن) and what falls in its scope are in the position of the accusative as the object of (استطعتم); (من أقطار السموات والأرض) is attached to (تنفذوا). (فانفذوا): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because the apodosis is a request; (انفذوا) is an imperative verb and the wāw its agent. What is meant by the command here is to show their inability (taʿjīz).
(لا تَنْفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطانٍ): (لا) is negating; (تنفذون) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw its agent; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (بسلطان) is attached to (تنفذون).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُما شُواظٌ مِنْ نارٍ وَنُحاسٌ فَلا تَنْتَصِرانِ): the clause is resumptive. (يرسل) is an imperfect verb, passive; (عليكما) is attached to (يرسل); (شواظ) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (من نار) is a naʿt (adjective) of (شواظ); (نحاس) is conjoined to (شواظ). It was also read in the genitive, conjoined to (نار). Al-Qurṭubī's wording: "Ibn Kathīr, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Mujāhid and Abū ʿAmr read (ونحاس) in the genitive, conjoined to (النار). Al-Mahdawī said: for whoever says that al-shuwāẓ is fire and smoke together, the genitive of (نحاس) here is an explication. But the genitive according to the view of whoever makes al-shuwāẓ the flame without smoke is far-fetched, admissible only by supposing an omitted qualified noun, as though He said: 'There will be sent upon you a flame of fire and something of nuḥās', so 'something' is conjoined to (شواظ), and 'of nuḥās' is a preposition and its genitive noun as an adjective of 'something'; (من) was omitted because it was mentioned before in (من نار), so (نحاس) on this view is genitive by the omitted (من)." The fāʾ is conjunctive; (لا) is negating; (تنتصران) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the alif is its agent, i.e. you will not be able to ward that off nor find any escape from it.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَالدِّهانِ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (إذا) is an adverb of future time; (انشقت السماء) is a verb and its agent, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (فكانت) is conjoined to (انشقت); the noun of (كانت) is latent, referring to (السماء); (وردة) is its predicate; (كالدهان) is an adjective of (وردة), or a second predicate of (كانت), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the noun of (كانت). Further discussion of this simile will come in the Rhetoric section.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُسْئَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إِنْسٌ وَلا جَانٌّ): the fāʾ links the answer of (إذا). It is also said that the answer of (إذا) is omitted, i.e. "when the sky is split you will see a tremendous matter", and the fāʾ is conjunctive onto it — but there is no call for this strained interpretation. (يومئذ) is an adverb attached to (يسأل); (إذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, and the nunation in it is compensation for a clause, i.e. "on the day when the sky is split". (لا) is negating; (يسأل) is an imperfect verb, passive; (عن ذنبه) is attached to (يسأل); (إنس) is the deputy agent, and (ولا جان) is conjoined to (إنس). (الجان) and (الإنس) are each a generic noun distinguished from its singular by the yāʾ, like zanj / zanjī.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(يُعْرَفُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيماهُمْ فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّواصِي وَالْأَقْدامِ): (يعرف) is an imperfect verb, passive; (المجرمون) is the deputy agent; (بسيماهم) is attached to (يعرف). The fāʾ is conjunctive; (يؤخذ) is an imperfect verb, passive, and (بالنواصي) is its deputy agent. (يؤخذ) is transitive, and yet it has been made transitive with the bāʾ because it has been made to include (ḍummina) the meaning of "yusḥabu" (is dragged), as Abū Ḥayyān said. But "yusḥabu" is made transitive only with (على); the Exalted said (يوم يسحبون في النار على وجوههم). So it is better to say that it includes the meaning of "yudfaʿu", i.e. they are pushed. The meaning is: the angels seize them by their forelocks — i.e. by their hair at the front of their heads — and their feet, and hurl them into the Fire. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "His forelock and his feet are brought together in a chain from behind his back." And from him: the man is seized by his two feet, which are brought together with his forelock until his back breaks, then he is thrown into the Fire.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(هذِهِ جَهَنَّمُ الَّتِي يُكَذِّبُ بِهَا الْمُجْرِمُونَ): (هذه) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (جهنم) the khabar (predicate); (التي) is an adjective, and the clause (يكذب بها المجرمون) is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
(يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَها وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ): the clause is a ḥāl of (المجرمين) or resumptive. (يطوفون) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw its agent; the adverb is attached to (يطوفون); (بين) is conjoined to the first adverb; (آن) is an adjective of (حميم); it is a manqūṣ noun (ending in yāʾ), so the kasra is implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ, which was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
In His words (فإذا انشقت السماء فكانت وردة كالدهان) there is a representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī). By "warda" He meant the plant [i.e. the rose]. The rose in spring is inclined to yellow; when the cold intensifies it is a red rose; and when it is after that, it is a rose inclined to dusty grey. So the colouring of the sky in the state of its splitting was likened to the rose, and the rose in the variation of its colours was likened to oil and the variation of its colours.
So the simile, as you see, is representational, composed of two parts or two successive images: the image of the sky split open and the image of the rose, then the image of the oil. The two latter images are for clarifying [Translator's note: the source prints «لتوضيع», evidently for «لتوضيح»] the point of similarity, namely the states of its colouring: in spring it is yellow, in winter red, then a dark dusty grey when it withers. This gradual colouring, from a bright colour to a dark colour, also resembles the colour of oil when fire has worked upon it, so that it blazes with a yellow colour, then its tongues appear reddish as it heralds its going out, then it turns into dark ash.
The heretics said: What is the point of similarity in (فكانت وردة كالدّهان)? And [what is the point of] repeating (فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان) after the mention of punishment, such as (يرسل عليكما شواظ من نار ونحاس), when it properly should be mentioned after enumerating favours? The answer to the first is that it has been said: its meaning is that the sky changes colour from the Greatest Terror just as the various oils change colour, and that al-dihān is the plural of duhn, so it is like the words of the Exalted (يوم تكون السماء كالمهل), according to whoever said that al-muhl is boiling oil. It is also said that al-dihān is red leather. As for the answer to the second: whoever warns you and makes you fear the consequence of what you are heading towards has bestowed a favour on you. Do you not see that He, glory be to Him, has said (وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة للعالمين)? And we know that he was sent as a bearer of good tidings to whoever believes and a warner to whoever disbelieves; so He made warning a mercy just as He made giving good tidings [a mercy]. Likewise (كل من عليها فان) and (فإذا انشقّت السماء) contain a favour to creation, in that He informed them of what they did not know and warned them of what they are heading towards. He, glory be to Him, made warning a kindness in His words (ويحذركم الله نفسه والله رءوف بالعباد).

dervis-irab:46-61.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَفْنانٍ): branches, plural of fanan; or they are the slender branches that "tatafarragh" from the boughs of the trees [Translator's note: so in the source, «تتفرغ»; evidently «تتفرع» (branch off)]. They were singled out for mention because they put forth leaves, bear fruit and extend shade.
(إِسْتَبْرَقٍ): thick brocade. Al-biṭān is the plural of biṭāna, which is the inner side of the outer covering (al-ẓihāra). It is also said that the outer covering is of sundus, which is the fine kind of brocade.
(جَنَى): al-janā is the fruit that has ripened on the tree.
(دانٍ): near; the one standing, sitting and lying down can reach it.
(قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ): al-maqṣūra is the one kept secluded; one also says qaṣīra and qaṣūra, i.e. kept behind the curtain. Kuthayyir said:
وأنت التي حبّبت كل قصيرة ... إليّ ولم تشعر بذاك القصائر
عنيت قصيرات الحجال ولم أرد ... قصار الخطا شر النساء البحاتر
(You are the one who made every secluded woman dear to me, though the secluded ones did not know it. I meant those kept within the curtained alcoves; I did not mean the short-stepped — the worst of women are the dumpy ones.)
Imruʾ al-Qays said:
من القاصرات الطرف لو دبّ محول ... من الذر فوق الأتب منها لأثرا
(One of those who restrain their glance; were a year-old ant to creep over her shift, it would leave a mark.)
Al-ṭarf (the glance) is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and that is why it is singular. The apparent sense is that they are the ones who restrict their eyes to their husbands and do not look at others. It is also said that al-ṭarf is the glance of others, i.e. they restrict the eyes of whoever looks at them from looking at anyone else.
(لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ): has not deflowered them; they are of the ḥūr, or of the women of this world newly created. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "ṭamatha al-rajulu imraʾatahu ṭamthan, of the patterns ḍaraba and qatala: he deflowered her. Ṭamth is not intercourse except with the causing of blood; to this refers the saying of the Exalted (لم يطمثهنّ)."
(الْياقُوتُ): a precious gem, red in colour; it is said that fire does not affect it. [The poet] said:
ألقني في لظى فإن غيّرتني ... فتيقن أن لست بالياقوت
(Throw me into the blaze; if it changes me, then be certain that I am no ruby.)
Among its properties is that it cuts all stones except the diamond, which cuts it, because of its hardness, the scarcity of its water, the intensity of its rays, its weight and its endurance of fire. Someone said about a handsome youth named Yāqūt:
ياقوت ياقوت قلب المستهام به ... من المروءة أن لا يمنع القوت
سكنت قلبي وما تخشى تلهبه ... وكيف يخشى لهيب النار ياقوت
(O Yāqūt, Yāqūt is the nourishment of the heart of the one infatuated with him; it is part of chivalry not to withhold nourishment. You dwell in my heart and do not fear its blaze — and how should a ruby fear the flame of fire?)
Al-marjān is small pearls, which are whiter; it is also applied to the other [i.e. coral]. More on the secret of this simile will come in the Rhetoric section.

* I'rab:
(وَلِمَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتانِ): the wāw is conjunctive; (لمن) is a fronted khabar (predicate); the clause (خاف) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من); (مقام ربه) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It may be a noun of place, or a mīmī maṣdar, in which case it bears two meanings: the first, that it means Allah's, the Mighty and Majestic, standing over creatures; the second, that it means the creatures' standing before Him, the Exalted. (جنتان) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). What is meant is a single garden, and it was made dual only out of regard for the verse endings. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "If you say: why did He say 'two gardens'? I say: the address is to the two weighty races, so it is as if it were said: for every two fearing ones of you there are two gardens — a garden for the fearing human and a garden for the fearing jinn. It may also be said: a garden for doing acts of obedience and a garden for abandoning acts of disobedience."
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(ذَواتا أَفْنانٍ): (ذواتا) is a naʿt (adjective) of (جنتان) and (أفنان) a muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct). The branches were singled out for mention because they are what flourish and put forth leaves, and from them shade extends and fruits are gathered. It is also said that al-afnān are the kinds and varieties of bliss that souls desire and eyes delight in. [The poet] said:
ومن كل أفنان اللذاذة والصبا ... لهوت به والعيش أخضر ناضر
(With every variety of pleasure and youth I amused myself, while life was green and fresh.)
(ذات) is the feminine of (ذو), meaning "possessor", and it occurs only annexed.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(فِيهِما عَيْنانِ تَجْرِيانِ): (فيهما) is a fronted predicate and (عينان) a delayed subject; the clause (تجريان) is an adjective of (عينان), i.e. in the high places and the low places. The views about the two springs are many, and perhaps what we have cited is the closest to reason.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(فِيهِما مِنْ كُلِّ فاكِهَةٍ زَوْجانِ): (فيهما) is a fronted predicate; (من كل فاكهة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of (زوجان) and was brought forward; (زوجان) is a delayed subject, i.e. two kinds, both delightful and sweet.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى فُرُشٍ بَطائِنُها مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ دانٍ): (متكئين) is accusative by way of praise, by an omitted verb; or a ḥāl from His words (ولمن خاف), because (من) has the meaning of a plural. It is also said that the governor is omitted, i.e. "they enjoy bliss, reclining". (على فرش) is attached to (متكئين); (بطائنها) is a subject and (من إستبرق) a predicate, and the clause is an adjective of (فرش). The wāw is circumstantial or conjunctive; (جنى) is a subject, (الجنتين) a muḍāf ilayhi, and (دان) the predicate; the sign of its nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ, which was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(فِيهِنَّ قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلا جَانٌّ): (فيهنّ) is a fronted predicate; the pronoun refers to the two gardens and the palaces and chambers they contain, or to the gardens indicated by His words (ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان) — since if each one of those who fear has two gardens, then it is right that they are many gardens. (قاصرات الطرف) is a delayed subject; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive; (يطمثهنّ) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); and the clause is an adjective of (قاصرات الطرف), because the annexation is verbal (lafẓiyya) and so it does not become definite. It may also be circumstantial, because the indefinite noun has been specified by annexation. (إنس) is the fāʿil (agent); (قبلهم) is an adverb of time attached to (يطمثهنّ); (ولا جان) is conjoined to (إنس).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(كَأَنَّهُنَّ الْياقُوتُ وَالْمَرْجانُ): the clause is an adjective of (قاصرات الطرف) or a ḥāl of it. (كأن) and its noun; (الياقوت) is its predicate, and (المرجان) is conjoined to (الياقوت).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(هَلْ جَزاءُ الْإِحْسانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسانُ): (هل) is an interrogative particle whose meaning is denial and negation; (جزاء) is a subject and (الإحسان) a muḍāf ilayhi; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and (الإحسان) is the predicate of (جزاء).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words (فيهنّ قاصرات الطرف) there is the device of irdāf (expression by a consequent). It has preceded that it is when the speaker intends a meaning and does not express it by the word coined for it, but by a word that is the consequent (ridf) of the particular meaning and follows it, close to the word of the particular meaning as the one riding behind is close to the rider. The meaning in the verse — as we said — is: in them are chaste women whose chastity has restricted their glance to their husbands. He turned from the particular meaning to the word of irdāf because everyone who is chaste lowers the glance from aspiring; for a person's gaze may stretch to something his soul desires, and he refrains from it, while able to have it, for some other reason. A woman's restricting her glance to her husband, or restricting her glance out of modesty and bashfulness, or restricting the eyes of those who look at them from looking at others, is something beyond chastity; because she whose glance does not aspire to anyone other than her husband, or does not aspire out of modesty and bashfulness, is necessarily chaste. So every woman who restrains her glance is chaste, but not every chaste woman restrains her glance; that is why He turned from the particular word to the word of irdāf.
2- In His words (كأنهنّ الياقوت والمرجان) there is a mursal mujmal simile (tashbīh mursal mujmal) — [mursal] because of the presence of the particle [of comparison]. As for the point of similarity, it is clarity. From Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "A woman of the women of the people of Paradise — the whiteness of her shin is seen from behind seventy garments, so that its marrow is seen. That is because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says (كأنهنّ الياقوت والمرجان). As for the ruby, it is a stone into which, were you to insert a thread and then make it clear, you would see [the thread] from behind it."
From Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His words (كأنهنّ الياقوت والمرجان): he said: "He looks at his face in her cheek, which is clearer than a mirror; the least pearl on her would light up what is between the east and the west; and she will have on her seventy garments which his sight penetrates, so that he sees the marrow of her shin from behind that." More description of the women of Paradise will come in Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa.

* Benefits:
(هَلْ) occurs in speech in four ways:
1- It means "qad" (indeed), as in His words (هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا).
2- It means the interrogative, as in His words (فهل وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقا).
3- It means the command, as in His words (فهل أنتم منتهون).
4- It means denial, as in His words (هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان).

dervis-irab:62-78.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُدْهامَّتانِ): in al-Mukhtār: "'dahimahum al-amru': the matter overcame them; its pattern is that of fahima; likewise 'dahimathum al-khayl' (the horses fell upon them); 'dahamahum', with fatḥa on the hāʾ, is a dialectal form. Al-duhma is blackness; one says 'faras adham' (a black horse), 'baʿīr adham' and 'nāqa dahmāʾ'; 'idhāmma idhīmāman', i.e. it became black. Allah the Exalted said (مدهامتان), i.e. two black ones from the intensity of their greenness through being well watered. The Arabs call every green thing black, and the villages of Iraq were called 'al-Sawād' (the Black) because of the abundance of their greenery. The 'dahmāʾ' sheep is the pure red one, and a shackle is called 'adham'." In al-Qāmūs: "A 'dahmāʾ' and 'mudhāmma' garden is a green one verging on black, through luxuriance and irrigation; from it comes (مدهامتان)."
(نَضَّاخَتانِ): two [springs] gushing with water, never ceasing. [Translator's note: the opening of this heading is damaged in the source text, «َضَّاخَتانِ)».] Al-naḍkh is more than al-naḍḥ, because al-naḍḥ, with the undotted ḥāʾ, is sprinkling, and with the dotted khāʾ it is like broaching; al-naḍḍākha is the gushing [spring] that throws water upwards.
(مَقْصُوراتٌ): they are kept secluded in their curtained chambers; one says "imraʾa qaṣīra", "qaṣūra" and "maqṣūra", i.e. kept behind the curtain.
(الْخِيامِ): in al-Qāmūs: "Al-khayma is a hillock above Abānān; and any round dwelling, or three or four poles over which thumām grass is thrown and in whose shade one takes shelter in the heat; or any dwelling built of tree branches. The plural is khaymāt, khiyām, khiyam and khaym — with fatḥa — and like ʿinab. 'Akhāmahā' and 'akhyamahā': he built it. 'Khayyamū': they entered it; [khayyamū] in a place: they stayed; [khayyama] a thing: he covered it with something so that it would become fragrant. 'Khāma ʿanhu yakhīmu khayman, khaymānan, khuyūman, khuyūmatan, khaymūmatan and khiyāman': he drew back and was cowardly; and he plotted a plot and it rebounded on him." In al-Qurṭubī: "ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the tent is a hollow pearl."
(رَفْرَفٍ): plural of rafrafa, i.e. carpets or cushions; so it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) or a collective generic noun (ism jins jamʿī). In al-Qāmūs: "Al-rafraf: green cloths from which maḥābis (covers) are made and which are spread out; the lower edge of the tent; the sides of the coat of mail and what hangs down from it; what droops of the branches of the thicket; the surplus of covers and bedding and everything left over and folded; bedding; a sea fish; a tree that grows in Yemen; the balcony (rawshan); the cushion; the clitoris; soft, trailing trees; meadows; carpets; a strip of cloth sewn at the bottom of the pavilion and the large tent; and the fine kind of brocade cloth."
(عَبْقَرِيٍّ): attributed to ʿAbqar. The Arabs claim that it is the name of the land of the jinn, so they attribute to it every wondrous thing. Al-Qāmūs says: "ʿAbqar is a place with many jinn, and a village whose building is of utmost beauty." Al-ʿabqarī is the perfect of everything. Al-Khalīl said: "The precious among men and others." Quṭrub said: "It is not a relative adjective (mansūb); rather it is in the category of kursī and bukhtī."

* I'rab:
(وَمِنْ دُونِهِما جَنَّتانِ): (من دونهما) is a fronted khabar (predicate) and (جنتان) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. below those two aforementioned gardens are two gardens in rank and beauty of appearance. This is according to the opinion of those who made the first two better than the latter two; it is also said the reverse, and al-Zamakhsharī preferred this. Al-Kisāʾī said: "(ومن دونهما), i.e. in front of them and before them," so that there is no superior and no inferior there.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(مُدْهامَّتانِ): a naʿt (adjective) of (جنتان).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(فِيهِما عَيْنانِ نَضَّاخَتانِ): [Translator's note: the source text here is run together and damaged, «تقدم إعرابهاِيهِما عَيْنانِ نَضَّاخَتانِ)».] The clause is a second adjective of (جنتان); (فيهما) is a fronted predicate, (عينان) a delayed subject, and (نضاختان) an adjective of (عينان).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(فِيهِما فاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ): "fīhā" [Translator's note: so in the source, «فيها»; the verse has (فيهما)] is a fronted predicate and (فاكهة) a delayed subject; (نخل) is conjoined to (فاكهة) and (رمان) to (نخل). The meaning of the specification will come in the Rhetoric section.
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(فِيهِنَّ خَيْراتٌ حِسانٌ): (فيهنّ) is a fronted predicate, (خيرات) a delayed subject, and (حسان) an adjective.
