(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(حُورٌ مَقْصُوراتٌ فِي الْخِيامِ): (حور) is a badal (substitute) of (خيرات). For (خيرات) there are two views: one, that it is the plural of khayra, of the pattern faʿla with a quiescent middle radical — one says "imraʾa khayra" (a good woman) and another "sharra" (a bad one); the second, that it is the plural of khayra lightened from khayyira with the doubled [yāʾ], which is indicated by the reading "khayyirāt" with a doubled yāʾ. You may also parse (حورا) as the predicate of an implied subject, i.e. "they are ḥūr", or as a subject whose predicate is omitted, i.e. "so among them are ḥūr". [Translator's note: the source writes «حورا» in the accusative form here, though the verse has (حور).] (مقصورات) is an adjective of (حور), and (في الخيام) is attached to (مقصورات).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلا جَانٌّ فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded earlier.
(مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ وَعَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسانٍ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) whose governor is omitted, i.e. "they enjoy bliss"; or accusative by way of praise — al-Zamakhsharī confined himself to this. It refers to (من خاف مقام ربه). (على رفرف) is attached to (متكئين); (خضر) is an adjective; (عبقري) is conjoined to (رفرف); and (حسان) is an adjective of (رفرف خضر وعبقري).
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ): its i'rab has preceded.
(تَبارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي الْجَلالِ وَالْإِكْرامِ): (تبارك) is a past verb and (اسم ربك) its fāʿil (agent); (ذي) is an adjective of (رب), (الجلال) a muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct), and (الإكرام) conjoined to (الجلال). It is also said that (اسم) is redundant (ṣila), the meaning being "Blessed is your Lord". Labīd said:
إلى الحول ثم اسم السلام عليكما ... ومن يبك حولا كاملا فقد اعتذر
(For a year; then the name of peace be upon you both — and whoever weeps a full year has discharged his excuse.)

* Rhetoric:
In His words (فيهما فاكهة ونخل ورمان), He separated them with the wāw only to single them out for their distinctions and merit. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "If you say: why did He conjoin the date-palms and pomegranates to the fruit, when they are part of it? I say: to single them out and make clear their merit, for it is as though, through their distinction, they were two further kinds, as in the words of the Exalted (وجبريل وميكائيل); or because the date-palm's produce is both fruit and food, and the pomegranate is fruit and medicine, so they are not purely for enjoyment as fruit. Hence Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: if someone swears not to eat fruit and then eats a pomegranate or fresh dates, he has not broken his oath; his two companions disagreed with him." Al-Zajjāj reported from Yūnus the grammarian — one of the early grammarians — that the date-palm and pomegranate are among the best of fruits, and they were separated by the wāw only because of their merit. Al-Azharī said: "I do not know of any of the Arabs who said of the date-palm and pomegranate and their produce that they are not fruit; only someone said that because of his little knowledge of the speech of the Arabs and of the interpretation of the clear Arabic Qur'an. The Arabs mention things all together and then single out one of them by name, to draw attention to a merit in it." Al-Karkhī's wording: "They are of the fruit; this was the view of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, and most scholars, so whoever swears not to eat fruit breaks his oath by eating either of them. In that case conjoining them to it is conjoining the particular to the general, by way of detail. It is also said that they are not of the fruit; Abū Ḥanīfa held this, saying: whoever swears not to eat fruit does not break his oath by eating dates and pomegranates." And is it conjoining the particular to the general, or conjoining what the first included? The apparent sense is that the verse is not conjoining the particular to the general, because an indefinite noun in an affirmative context does not have comprehensive (shumūlī) generality.

farraa:5-5.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿بِحُسْبَانٍ﴾. A reckoning and stations [188/ب] for the sun and the moon, which they do not exceed.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلنَّجْمُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ﴾. «النجم» is what sprouts (najama), such as grass, herbs and the like; and «الشجر» is what stands on a trunk. Then He said «يسجدان» (the two prostrate); their prostration is that they face the sun when it rises, then incline with it until the shade turns. When the Arabs combine two plural (collective) nouns of things other than people, such as lote-trees and palm trees, they make their verb singular, saying: «الشاء والنعم قد أقبل» (the sheep and the cattle have come), and «النخل والسدر قد ارتوى» (the palms and the lote-trees have been watered). This is most of their speech, and putting it in the dual is permissible.
Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say: «مرت بنا غنمان سودان» and «سود» (two black flocks passed by us).
Al-Farrāʾ said: «سود» is better than «سودان», because it is an adjective that applies to the two. When one of the two is feminine, such as sheep and camels, they say: «الشاء والإبل مقبلة» (the sheep and the camels are coming), because «الشاء» is masculine and «الإبل» feminine. Had you said «مقبلان» it would be permissible; and had you said «مقبلتان», taking «الشاء» as feminine along with the feminine of «الإبل», it would be correct; but the singular is more frequent and better.
When you say «هؤلاء قومك وإبلهم قد أقبلوا» (these are your people and their camels, they have come), the verb is taken to refer to the people specifically, because the action is theirs, and they are the ones who bring the camels. Had you meant the coming of both these and those, «قد أقبلوا» would (still) be permissible, because when people are mixed with some animals, their action becomes like the action of people, as He said: ﴿وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ المَاءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, and the she-camel became like people.
Of this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِى عَلَى بَطْنِهِ﴾; «مَنْ» is only used for people, but when He detailed them, having gathered them together in His saying ﴿وَاللهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ دَابّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾, He detailed them in the manner used for people.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا...﴾ above the earth; ﴿وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ﴾: in the earth, and it is justice.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «وخَفْض الميزان»; «الخفض» (lowering) and «الوضع» (setting down) are close in meaning.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ تَطْغَوْاْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «لا تطغوا» without «أن», «فى الوزن وأقيموا اللسان».
And His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ تَطْغَوْاْ﴾: if you wish, you make it jussive (majzūm) with the intent of prohibition; and if you wish, you make it accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», as Allah said: ﴿إِنِّى أمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلا تَكونَنَّ﴾. That (تطغوا) should be in the position of a jussive is dearer to me, because after it comes an imperative.

farraa:9-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾.
﴿وَٱلأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلأَنَامِ﴾: for all creatures.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْحَبُّ ذُو ٱلْعَصْفِ وَٱلرَّيْحَانُ﴾. Al-Aʿmash read it in the genitive, and the people read it in the nominative.
Whoever read it in the genitive meant: «ذو العصف وذو الريحان» (possessing husk and possessing fragrance/sustenance); whoever read «الريحان» in the nominative made it follow «ذو». «العصف», according to what they mentioned, is the green leaf of the crop; for the Arabs say «خرجنا نعصف الزرع» (we went out to cut the crop) when they cut some of it before it ripens; that is «العصف». «الريحان» is its sustenance, and «الحب» is what is eaten of it. «الريحان» in the speech of the Arabs means sustenance; they say «خرجنا نطلب ريحان الله» (we went out seeking Allah's rayḥān), sustenance in their usage. Some of them said: «ذو العصف» is what is eaten of the grain, and «الريحان» is the sound part that has not been eaten.
Had a reader read: "والحبّ ذا العصف والريحانَ", it would have been permissible, that is: He created this and this. In the codices of the people of Syria it is «والحبّ ذا العصف», but we have not heard any reader read it so; just as in some codices of the people of Kufa there is ﴿والجار ذا القربى﴾ [189/ا] and no one has read it so. Sometimes a word is written in one way while it is read in (various) ways.
It has reached me that the letter of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, was written: «هذا كتاب من على بن أبو طالب» — its scribes wrote «أبو» in all cases — and it is declined in speech when it is read aloud.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلاۤءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾. At the beginning of the passage He only mentioned «الإنسان» (man); there are two explanations of this. The first: the Arabs address (a single person) with the dual form of the verb; one says: «ارحلاها، ازجراها يا غلام» (saddle her, drive her on, boy!).
The other explanation: the mention was intended of mankind and the jinn, so it runs for both of them from the beginning of the sura to its end.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿خَلَقَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مِن صَلْصَالٍ كَٱلْفَخَّارِ﴾.
It is clay mixed with sand, which rings (ṣalṣala) as pottery rings. It is also said: from stinking «صلصال», by which they mean «صلّ» (it went putrid); then «صلصال» is said, just as one says «صرّ الباب» (the door creaked) when closing, and «صرصر». The Arabs repeat (in place of) the lām (the third radical) in the doubled (verb), so it is said «كركرت الرجلَ», meaning «كررْته» (I turned him back), and «كبكبته», meaning «كببته» (I threw him on his face).
I heard one of the Arabs say: «أتيت فلانا فبشبش بى» (I came to so-and-so and he welcomed me), from «البشاشة» (cheerfulness). They only did this out of dislike for three letters of one kind coming together.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿مِن مَّارِجٍ مِّن نَّارٍ﴾.
«المارج» is a fire below the veil — according to what al-Kalbī mentioned — from which these thunderbolts come, and the skin of the sky is seen from it.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَغْرِبَيْنِ﴾.
The readers agreed on its nominative; had it been put in the genitive — that is, in its inflection — following His saying «فبأى آلاء ربكما»: «ربِّ المشرقين», it would have been correct.
The two easts are the rising-place of winter and the rising-place of summer; likewise the two wests.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾. He is saying: He let them loose, then they meet afterwards.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ﴾.
A barrier; «لا يبغيان»: the fresh does not encroach on the salt so that both become fresh, and the salt does not encroach on the fresh so that both become salt.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا الُّلؤْلُؤُ وَالمَرْجَانُ﴾.
It only comes out of the salt, not the fresh. «اللؤلؤ» is the large (pearls), and «المرجان» is the small pearls.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلْجَوَارِ ٱلْمُنشَئَاتُ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read (المنشِئات) with a kasra on the shīn, making them the ones that come and go (of themselves). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd it is (المنشآت), and so read al-Ḥasan and the people of the Ḥijāz, with a fatḥa on the shīn, making them acted upon: they are made to come and made to go.
And His saying: ﴿كَٱلأَعْلاَمِ﴾.
Like mountains: He likened the ship to a mountain; and every mountain, when it is tall, is a «عَلَم».

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلْجَلاَلِ﴾.
This one, and the one at the end of it with «ذى» — both of them in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh are «ذى» — are genitive in inflection, because they are part of the description of «ربك», Blessed and Exalted. In our reading it is: ﴿وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلْجَلاَلِ وَٱلإِكْرَامِ﴾, [ذو] being part of the description of «وجه» of our Lord, Blessed and Exalted.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ﴾, without hamza.
He said: I asked al-Farrāʾ [189/ب] about (شان), and he said: I pronounce it with hamza throughout the Qurʾān except in Sūrat al-Raḥmān, because it is among verses that are without hamza. His affair (shaʾn) every day is that He causes one to die and one to be born, enriches this one and impoverishes that one, among countless deeds.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ ٱلثَّقَلاَنِ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Abū Isrāʾīl told me: I heard Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read: "سَيَفْرغُ لكم", and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb likewise; and the readers after that: "سَنَفْرُغُ لكم"; and some of them read "سيُفرغ لكم".
This is a threat from Allah, for He, Mighty and Majestic, is not distracted by one thing from another. You say to a man who has no occupation: «قد فرغت لى، قد فرغت لشتمى» (you have made yourself free for me, for insulting me), that is: you have set about it and turned to it.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰمَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنسِ إِنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَن تَنفُذُواْ﴾.
He did not say «إن استطعتما» (dual); had it been so, it would have been correct, just as He said (يُرسل عليكما) and did not say «عليكم»: «شُواظ من نار ونحاس فلا تنتصران». He used the dual in «عليكما» and «تنتصران» according to the wording, and the plural according to the meaning. «النحاس» is nominative; had it been genitive it would have been correct, meaning: of fire and of «نحاس».
«الشواظ» is pure fire, and «النحاس» is smoke. One of them recited to me:
يضىء كضوء سراج السلي * ط لم يجعل الله منه نحاسا
(It shines like the light of a lamp of salīṭ, from which Allah made no smoke.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: a Bedouin of Banū Sulaym told me: «السليط» is the fat of the camel's hump, and it gives no smoke when used in a lamp.
And I heard that it is «الخَلّ», which is sesame oil; and I heard that it is olive oil. Olive oil is more correct, in my view.
Al-Ḥasan read (شِواظ) with a kasra on the shīn, just as one says of a herd of wild cattle «صِوار» and «صُوَار».

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا ٱنشَقَّتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَكَانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَٱلدِّهَانِ﴾.
By «الوردة» He meant the (bay) horse: the bay mare in spring is a bay inclining to yellow; when the cold becomes severe she is a red bay; and after that she is a bay inclining to dust-colour. So He likened the changing colour of the sky to the changing colour of the bay among horses, and the bay in the variety of its colours was likened to oil (duhn) and the variety of its colours.
And it is said that «الدهان» is red leather.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لاَّ يُسْأَلُ عَن ذَنبِهِ إِنسٌ وَلاَ جَآنٌّ﴾.
The meaning is: no human will be asked about his sin, nor jinn about his sin, because they will be known by their marks, as Allah described: the disbeliever will be known by the blackness of his face and the blueness of his eye, and the believer will be radiant on the forehead and limbs from the traces of his ablution.
«[Translator's note: «رزقة» is as printed, evidently for «زرقة» (blueness).]»

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذِهِ جَهَنَّمُ ٱلَّتِي يُكَذِّبُ بِهَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: «هذه جهنم التى كنتما بها تكذبان، تَصليانها لا تموتان فيها ولا تحييان تطوفان» (This is Hell which you two used to deny; you two will burn in it, neither dying nor living in it, going round).

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَهَا﴾.
Between the punishment of Hell and the boiling water when they are thirsty. «الآنى» is that whose heat has reached its utmost intensity.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتَانِ﴾.
The exegetes mentioned that they are two orchards among the orchards of Paradise. It may also be, in Arabic, a single garden which the Arabs put in the dual in their poetry. One of them recited to me:
ومَهْمَين قَذَفَين مَرْتَين * قطعته [بالأََمِّ] لا بالسَّمْتين
(Many a pair of far, bare, waterless deserts I have crossed by the straight course, not by the two tracks.)
He means a single desert and a single track. Another recited to me:
يسعى بكيداء ولهذمين * قد جعل الأرطاة جنتين
(He hastens with a bow and two arrowheads; he has made the arṭā shrub into two gardens.)
That is because poetry has rhymes which addition and reduction set right, so it tolerates what (ordinary) speech does not tolerate.
Al-Farrāʾ said: «الكيداء» is the bow. One says «لهذِم» and «لهذَم», two dialectal forms; it is the arrow(head).

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى فُرُشٍ بَطَآئِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾. «الإستبرق» is the thick kind of brocade. The lining (biṭāna) may be the outer side (ẓihāra), and the outer side the lining, in the speech of the Arabs; that is because each of them [190/ا] may be a face. The Arabs say «this is the back (ẓahr) of the sky» and «this is the belly (baṭn) of the sky» for its outer side that you see.
He said: one of the eloquent ḥadīth transmitters told me, from Ibn al-Zubayr, who was censuring the killers of ʿUthmān, may Allah have mercy on him, and said: they came out against him like thieves from behind the village; so Allah killed them every kind of killing, and those of them who escaped escaped beneath the bellies of the stars.
He means: they fled by night. So he made the backs of the stars their bellies; and that is permissible according to what I have told you.

farraa:56-56.t:
His saying: ﴿لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ [إِنسٌ]﴾.
All the readers read «يطمثهن» with a kasra on the mīm. Al-Farrāʾ told us: a man told me, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I used to pray behind the companions of ʿAlī and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, and I heard them read (لم يطمُثهن) with a ḍamma on the mīm. Al-Kisāʾī used to read one (occurrence) with a ḍamma on the mīm and the other with a kasra on the mīm, so as not to depart from these two reports. «لم يطمِثهن» means: they have not deflowered them. (He said: «طمثها» means: he had intercourse with her; and that is because of the blood.)

farraa:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿مُدْهَآمَّتَانِ﴾: He is saying: green inclining to black, from (abundant) watering.

farraa:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿فِيهِمَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ﴾.
Some of the exegetes say: neither pomegranates nor palms are fruit. They have taken a position, but the Arabs count those as fruit.
If you ask: then how are palms and pomegranates mentioned again if they are among the fruit? I say: that is like His saying: ﴿حَافِظُوا على الصَّلواتِ والصلاةِ الوُسْطَى﴾. He commanded them to guard all the prayers, then mentioned the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr) again to emphasise it. Likewise palms and pomegranates were mentioned again to make the people of Paradise desire them. Similar is His saying in al-Ḥajj: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَنْ فِى السَّمَاواتِ وَمَنْ فِى الأَرْضِ﴾, then He said: ﴿وكَثيرٌ مِّن الناسِ، وكثيرٌ حَقَّ عليه الْعَذابُ﴾, though He had mentioned them at the beginning of the statement in His saying ﴿مَنْ فِى السّماواتِ ومَن فِى الأرضِ﴾. Some of the exegetes said: by His saying ﴿مَنْ فِى السماواتِ ومن فى الأرضِ﴾ He only meant the angels, then He mentioned people after them.

farraa:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿فِيهِنَّ خَيْرَاتٌ حِسَانٌ﴾.
It refers back to the four gardens — two gardens and two gardens — so He said «فيهن». The Arabs say: «أعطنى الخَيْرَة منهن», «الخِيرة منهن» and «الخيّرة منهن» (give me the best of them). Had a reader read «الخَيراتُ» or «الخيرات», both would have been correct.
«[Translator's note: the two variants are printed without distinguishing vowels; presumably «خَيْرات» and «خَيِّرات» are meant.]»

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿حُورٌ مَّقْصُورَاتٌ﴾.
They are restricted to their husbands, that is, kept (for them), so that they want no others and do not look to anyone else. The Arabs call the curtained bridal canopy «المقصورة» and «القصورة», and they call a secluded woman «قصورة». The poet said:
لعمرى لقد حببِت كلَّ قَصورة * إلىّ وما تدرى بذاك القصائر
عَنَيْتُ قصوراتِ الحجال ولم أرِد * قصارَ الخُطا، شرُّ النساء البحاتر
(By my life, you have made every secluded woman dear to me, though the secluded ones do not know it. I meant those secluded in canopies, not the short-stepped; the worst of women are the stumpy.)
«البحاتر» and «البهاتر» both mean the short (women); a man is called «بحتر», «بحترى», «بحترة» and «بحترية».

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَىٰ رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ﴾.
They mentioned that these are the meadows of Paradise; and some of them said: they are cushions. ﴿وَعَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسَانٍ﴾: thick carpets.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Muʿādh ibn Muslim ibn Abī Sāda told me: Your neighbour [190/ب] Zuhayr al-Qurqubī used to read: «متكئين على رفارف خضر وعباقرى حسان».
He said: «الرفارف» may be correct; but «العباقرى» not, because the alif of the (broken) plural is not followed by four letters, nor by three sound letters.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: (الرحمن) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is the clause {عَلَّمَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «خلق» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «علَّمه» is a third khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: (الشمس والقمر بحسبان) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «السماء» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it; the clause of the implied verb is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «علَّمه البيان», and the clause «رفعها» is explicative. The clause «ووضع» is conjoined to the implied clause «رفع».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: (ألا تطغوا في الميزان) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «أن» is maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative by removal of the preposition lām.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «وأقيموا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «تطغوا»; the preposition «بالقسط» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «الأرض» is the object of an omitted verb explained by what follows it, and the clause of the implied verb is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «وضع الميزان» in verse (7).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «فيها فاكهة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأرض»; «ذات» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «الحب» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «النخل»; «ذو» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The fāʾ connects (rābiṭa) to the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition, i.e. "if the matter is so"; «بأي» is an interrogative noun, genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تكذبان».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The preposition «من نار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «مارج».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «رب» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is the Lord", and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «يلتقيان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «البحرين».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «بينهما برزخ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «البحرين», as is the clause «لا يبغيان».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «وله الجوار» is resumptive; «الجوار» is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ, which is omitted for lightness. «المنشآت» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الجوار»; the preposition «في البحر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «الجوار»; the preposition «كالأعلام» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «المنشآت».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «من» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «فان» is the khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ).

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «كل» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the notion of being (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached, and the clause «هو في شأن» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «سنفرغ» is resumptive, as is the clause «أيها الثقلان»; «الثقلان» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The conditional clause is the response to the vocative, resumptive; the clause «لا تنفذون» is resumptive; the preposition «بسلطان» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «تنفذون».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «يُرْسَل» is resumptive; the preposition «من نار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «شواظ»; and the clause «فلا تنتصران» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يُرْسَل».

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the clause «فكانت» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «انشقت»; the preposition «كالدهان» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «وردة»; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "you would see a great terror".

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The fāʾ is conjunctive; «يوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يسأل»; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the tanwīn is for compensation; the clause «لا يسأل» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preceding implied apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «يعرف» is resumptive; the preposition «بسيماهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المجرمون»; the clause «فيؤخذ» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يعرف»; the preposition «بالنواصي» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause «يطوفون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جهنم»; «آن» is a naʿt (adjective) of «حميم», genitive (majrūr) with an implied (muqaddar) kasra on the omitted yāʾ, because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ).

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The clause «ولمن خاف جنتان» is resumptive; «جنتان» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition «لمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «فيهما عينان» is a naʿt (adjective) of {جَنَّتَانِ}, and the clause «تجريان» is a naʿt of «عينان».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The clause «فيهما زوجان» is a naʿt (adjective) of {جَنَّتَانِ}; the preposition «من كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «زوجان».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: «متكئين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw that is implied together with its verb, i.e. "they enjoy bliss, reclining". The preposition «على فرش» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متكئين»; the clause «بطائنها من إستبرق» is a naʿt (adjective) of «فرش»; and the clause «وجنى الجنتين دان» is a ḥāl. «جنى» is mubtadaʾ (subject); «دان» is the khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «فيهن قاصرات» is resumptive; the clause «لم يطمثهن إنس» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قاصرات», because its annexation is verbal (lafẓiyya) [Translator's note: i.e. «قاصرات الطرف» remains indefinite, so a clause can describe it].

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: The clause «كأنهن الياقوت والمرجان» is a naʿt (adjective) of {قَاصِرَاتُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «الإحسان» is the khabar (predicate) of «جزاء»; and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The clause «ومن دونهما جنتان» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: «مدهامَّتان» is a naʿt (adjective) of {جَنَّتَانِ}, and what lies between the adjective and the noun it qualifies is a parenthetical clause.

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: The clause «فيهما عينان» is a naʿt (adjective) of {جَنَّتَانِ}, and «نضاختان» is a naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: The clause «فيهما فاكهة» is a third naʿt (adjective) of {جَنَّتَانِ}.

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: The clause «فيهن خيرات حسان» is a fourth naʿt (adjective) of {جَنَّتَانِ}.

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: «حور» is a badal (substitute) from {خَيْرَاتٌ}; the preposition «في الخيام» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مقصورات».

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: The clause «لم يطمثهن» is a naʿt (adjective) of «حور»; the adverb «قبلهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: «متكئين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw that is implied together with its verb, i.e. "they enjoy bliss, reclining"; the preposition «على رفرف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ḥāl.

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: The clause «تبارك» is resumptive; «ذي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ربك».

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying الشَّمْس وَالْقَمَر بحسبان: الشمس is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "the sun and the moon run by a reckoning" (الشمس والقمر يجريان بحسبان), i.e. by calculation. It is also said that بحسبان is the khabar.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying أَلا تطغوا: أن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition (accusative by removal of the preposition), its implied form being "so that you do not transgress" (لئلا تطغوا), and تطغوا is in the position of the accusative by أن. It is also said that أن means أي (explicative "that is"), having no grammatical position; on this view تطغوا is jussive by لا.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying وَالْحب ذُو العصف وَالريحَان: Ibn ʿĀmir read it in the accusative, conjoining it to الأرض, because His saying والأرض وضعها للأنام means "He created it", so والحب is conjoined to that, i.e. "and He created the grain and the fragrant plant". Whoever reads it in the nominative conjoins it to فاكهة, and فاكهة is a mubtadaʾ (subject) with فيها as the khabar (predicate). Whoever reads الريحان in the genitive conjoins it to العصف and makes الريحان mean sustenance.
His saying رب المشرقين: رب is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "He is the Lord of the two easts" (هو رب المشرقين). It is also said that it is a badal (substitute) of the latent pronoun in خلق. In ordinary speech the genitive is permissible as a badal of ربكما.
His saying وَالريحَان: its origin is رَيْوِحان; then they substituted a yāʾ for the wāw and the yāʾ was assimilated, as in ميّت and هيّن; then the yāʾ was lightened, as you say مَيْت, هَيْن and لَيْن. The lightening became obligatory in ريحان because of its length and because of the two augments attached at its end, namely the alif and the nūn. So its pattern is فَيْعَلان. Had its pattern been فَعْلان, you would say رَوْحان, because it is from الرَّوْح, and the substitution of yāʾ for wāw would not be possible, since there is no cause requiring that. Since the yāʾ in it is agreed upon, it is known that it has an origin from which it was lightened, namely what we mentioned. Some have permitted it to be فَعْلان, with the yāʾ a substitute for a wāw, just as they substituted a wāw for a yāʾ in أشاوى, whose origin is أشايا.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying يخرج مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤ: i.e. from one of them; then the muḍāf, namely أحد, was omitted and the pronoun was attached to من, as He said على رجل من القريتين, i.e. from one of the two towns; then the muḍāf was omitted. The omission of the muḍāf is permissible, frequent and widespread in the speech of the Arabs, as in His saying واسأل القرية and His saying التي أخرجتك.
His saying كالأعلام: the كاف is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in المنشآت.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying من نَار ونحاس: whoever reads النحاس in the nominative conjoins it to الشواظ, and this is more correct in meaning, because الشواظ is flame in which there is no smoke, and النحاس is smoke, and both arise from fire. As for whoever reads ونحاسٍ in the genitive, he conjoins it to النار, and there is remoteness in it, because the meaning becomes that the flame arises from the smoke, and it is not so; it only arises from fire. It has been related from Abū ʿAmr that he said: الشواظ only comes from fire and something else with it, meaning it arises from two things, from fire and smoke; and the like is related from al-Akhfash. On this basis the genitive of النحاس is sound. It has also been said that the implied form is "there will be sent against you a flame of fire and something of smoke" (يرسل عليكما شواظ من نار وشيء من نحاس); then شيء was omitted and من نار — which is its adjective — was set up in its place, and the preposition was omitted because it had been mentioned before; so the meaning is like the reading of whoever reads نحاس in the nominative.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t:
His saying فَيُؤْخَذ بالنواصي: there is no pronoun in يؤخذ, and بالنواصي stands in place of the fāʿil (agent) [i.e. it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]; its implied form is "they will be seized by their forelocks" (فيؤخذ بنواصيهم). It is also said that the implied form is "they will be seized by the forelocks among them" (فيؤخذ بالنواصي منهم). It is not permissible for يؤخذ to contain a pronoun referring back to المجرمين, because He would then have to say فيؤخذون, and أخذ would have to be made transitive to two objects, one of them with the بـ, and that is not permissible. One only says أخذت الناصية and أخذت بالناصية ("I seized the forelock"); if you said أخذت الدابة بالناصية ("I seized the beast by the forelock") it would not be permissible. It is related from the Arabs: أخذت الخطام and أخذت بالخطام ("I took the halter") with the same meaning.
It has also been said that its meaning is "each one will be seized by the forelocks", and that is not correct, because it does not become transitive to two objects one of them with the بـ, as we mentioned. It may become transitive to two objects, one of them with a preposition other than the بـ, as in أخذت ثوبا من زيد ("I took a garment from Zayd"); but this meaning is other than the first. So another object is not good with the بـ unless you make it mean "on account of", in which case you may say أخذت زيدا بعمرو, i.e. on his account and for his sin. So take note of it.

mekki-muskil:48-48.t: His saying ذواتا أفنان: ذواتا is the dual of ذات according to the origin, because the origin of ذات is ذوات, but the wāw was omitted for lightness and to distinguish between the singular and the plural; and the dual, with the return of the wāw in it, indicates the origin of the singular. أفنان is the plural of فَنَن according to whoever makes أفنان mean "branches"; whoever makes it mean "kinds and varieties", the singular is فنّ, and its right would be to have the plural فنون.

mekki-muskil:54-54.t:
His saying وجنى الجنتين دَان: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and دان, like قاض and غاز, has a weak final radical (muʿtall al-lām).
His saying متكئين على فرش: a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the governing word in it is implied, its implied form being "they enjoy bliss, reclining" (ينعمون متكئين); what indicates that is that the verses are describing bliss. It is also said that it is a ḥāl of من in His saying ولمن خاف.

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying كأنهن الْيَاقُوت: كأنهن is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of قاصرات الطرف, as if He said "in them are maidens restraining their glances, resembling rubies". Al-Naḥḥās mentioned that the كاف is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); that is far-fetched and has no justification.

mekki-muskil:70-70.t: His saying فِيهِنَّ خيرات: the origin of خيرات is on the pattern فَيْعِلات, but it was lightened, like ميْت, هيْن and هيّن. [خيرات is] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and فيهن the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:76-76.t: His saying على رَفْرَف خضر: رفرف is a collective noun (ism jamʿ); therefore it is described with خضر, which is the plural of أخضر, so it is like your saying رهط كرام ("a noble band") and قوم لئام ("a base people"). It is also said that it is a plural whose singular is رفرفة. Like it is وعبقري: it is said that its singular is عبقرية, and it is also said that عبقري is a singular indicating the plural, a relative adjective (nisba) to عبقر, which is a place.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of eloquence, pointing to an omitted condition); «بأي» is a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تكذبان»; «آلاء» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «ربكما» is muḍāf ilayhi; «تكذبان» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent). The address is to the two weighty kinds (al-thaqalān), mankind and the jinn.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿هذه جهنم التي يكذب بها المجرمون﴾: «هذه» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «جهنم» is the khabar (predicate), «التي» is a ṣifa (adjective), and the clause «يكذب بها المجرمون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t: ﴿يطوفون بينها وبين حميم آن﴾: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «المجرمين», or resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. «يطوفون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يطوفون»; «بين» is conjoined to the first adverb; «آنٍ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «حميم», and it is a manqūṣ noun (ending in a defective yāʾ), so the kasra is implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ that has been dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «لمن» is a fronted khabar (predicate); the clause «خاف» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «من», a clause with no grammatical position. «مقام» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is a noun of place, or a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun with prefixed mīm); «ربه»: «رب» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and is itself muḍāf, and the hāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; «جنتان» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:48-48.t: ﴿ذواتا أفنان﴾: «ذواتا» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «جنتان», and «أفنان» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:50-50.t: ﴿فيهما عينان تجريان﴾: «فيهما» is a fronted khabar (predicate), «عينان» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «تجريان» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عينان».

muyesser-irab:52-52.t: ﴿فيهما من كل فاكهة زوجان﴾: «فيهما» is a fronted khabar (predicate); «من كل فاكهة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a ṣifa (adjective) of «زوجان»; «زوجان» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:54-54.t: ﴿متكئين على فرش بطائنها من إستبرق وجنى الجنتين دان﴾: «متكئين» is accusative (manṣūb) as praise (ʿalā al-madḥ) by an omitted verb, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from His saying «ولمن خاف»; and it has been said: the governing word is omitted, i.e. «يتنعمون متكئين» (they enjoy bliss, reclining). «على فرش» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متكئين»; «بطائنها» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «من إستبرق» is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ṣifa (adjective) of «فرش». The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction; «جنى» is a mubtadaʾ, «الجنتين» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and «دانٍ» is the khabar, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ that has been dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

muyesser-irab:56-56.t: ﴿فيهن قاصرات الطرف لم يطمثهن إنس قبلهم ولا جان﴾: «فيهن» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «قاصرات الطرف» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive; «يطمثهن» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم». The clause «يطمثهن» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «قاصرات الطرف», because the annexation is a verbal (lafẓiyya) one and so it does not become definite; or it is ḥāl (circumstantial), because the indefinite noun has been specified by the annexation. «إنس» is the fāʿil (agent); «قبلهم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يطمثهن»; and «ولا جان» is conjoined to «إنس».

muyesser-irab:58-58.t: ﴿كأنهن الياقوت والمرجان﴾: the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «قاصرات الطرف», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it. «كأن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «هن» is its noun, «الياقوت» is its khabar (predicate), and «المرجان» is conjoined to «الياقوت».

muyesser-irab:60-60.t: ﴿هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان﴾: «هل» is an interrogative particle whose meaning is denial and negation; «جزاء» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «الإحسان» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and «الإحسان» is the khabar (predicate) of «جزاء».

muyesser-irab:62-62.t: ﴿ومن دونهما جنتان﴾: «من دونهما» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «جنتان» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:66-66.t: ﴿فيهما عينان نضاختان﴾: the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of «جنتان»; «فيهما» is a fronted khabar (predicate), «عينان» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and «نضاختان» is a naʿt of «عينان».

muyesser-irab:68-68.t: ﴿فيهما فاكهة ونخل ورمان﴾: «فيهما» is a fronted khabar (predicate), «فاكهة» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), «نخل» is conjoined to «فاكهة», and «رمان» is conjoined to «نخل».

muyesser-irab:70-70.t: ﴿فيهن خيرات حسان﴾: «فيهن» is a fronted khabar (predicate), «خيرات» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and «حسان» is a ṣifa (adjective).

muyesser-irab:72-72.t: ﴿حور مقصورات في الخيام﴾: «حور» is a badal (substitute) of «خيرات», or the khabar (predicate) of an implied (muḍmar) mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هن حور», or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar has been omitted, i.e. «فهن حور»; «مقصورات» is a naʿt (adjective) of «حور», and «في الخيام» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مقصورات». [Translator's note: the source's two implied forms «هن حور» and «فهن حور» both supply the pronoun as mubtadaʾ, although the second alternative calls «حور» the mubtadaʾ; translated as written.]

muyesser-irab:74-74.t: ﴿لم يطمثهن إنس قبلهم ولا جان﴾: «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive; «يطمثهن» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم»; «إنس» is the fāʿil (agent); «قبلهم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يطمثهن»; and «ولا جان» is conjoined to «إنس».

muyesser-irab:76-76.t: ﴿متكئين على رفرف خضر وعبقري حسان﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) whose governing word has been omitted, i.e. «يتنعمون» (they enjoy bliss), or accusative as praise (ʿalā al-madḥ). «على رفرف» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متكئين»; «خضر» is a naʿt (adjective); «عبقري» is conjoined to «رفرف»; and «حسان» is a naʿt of «رفرف خضر» and «عبقري».

muyesser-irab:78-78.t:
﴿تبارك﴾: a past verb.
﴿اسم﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿ربك﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ذي﴾: a ṣifa (adjective) of «رب».
﴿الجلال﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿والإكرام﴾: conjoined to «الجلال».

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿الرحمن﴾: الرحمن is a mubtadaʾ (subject); and it has been said: الرحمن is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: الله الرحمن (Allah is the All-Merciful); or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e.: الرحمن ربنا (the All-Merciful is our Lord).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿علم القرآن﴾: the clause علم القرآن is the khabar (predicate); علم is transitive to two objects, the first of which is omitted because of its comprehensiveness, i.e.: He taught whoever learns; and this is preferable to restricting the omitted first object to one specific person.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿خلق الإنسان﴾: a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the alif and lām in الإنسان are for the genus (al-jins).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿علمه البيان﴾: a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and its two objects.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿الشمس والقمر بحسبان﴾: الشمس is a mubtadaʾ (subject); القمر is conjoined to it; and بحسبان is the khabar (predicate) of الشمس.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿والنجم والشجر يسجدان﴾: conjoined to what preceded; and the clause يسجدان is the khabar (predicate) of النجم.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t: ﴿والسماء رفعها ووضع الميزان﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; السماء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb indicated by the one mentioned. The clause رفعها is explicative, with no grammatical position. ﴿ووضع الميزان﴾: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿ألا تطغوا في الميزان﴾: ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); لا is negating; تطغوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the maṣdar-forming أن; أن with what follows it is construed as (a maṣdar) made genitive [Translator's note: the source has «منصوب» (accusative) here, evidently for «مجرور» (genitive)] by an implied lām of cause, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وضع﴾. The clause ﴿لا تطغوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it is explicative, with no grammatical position; لا is then the prohibitive lā; and تطغوا is jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أقيموا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); الوزن is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وبالقسط is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: do it upright, with justice; the wāw is a conjunction; لا is the prohibitive lā; تخسروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and الميزان is a mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t: ﴿والأرض وضعها للأنام﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. والأرض: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it. The clause ﴿وضعها﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position. وللأنام: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وضعها﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فيها فاكهة والنخل ذات الأكمام﴾: فيها is a fronted khabar (predicate); فاكهة is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); النخل is conjoined to فاكهة; ذات الأكمام is a naʿt (adjective) of النخل; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأرض.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t: ﴿والحب ذو العصف والريحان﴾: الحب is conjoined to فاكهة, nominative (marfūʿ); ذو is a naʿt (adjective) of الحب, nominative with the wāw because it is one of the six nouns (al-asmāʾ al-sitta); العصف is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and الريحان is conjoined to فاكهة, nominative.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿خلق الإنسان من صلصال كالفخار﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; خلق is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring back to Allah the Exalted; الإنسان is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ومن صلصال is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلق; ﴿كالفخار﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of صلصال; and ﴿الفخار﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وخلق الجان من مارج من نار﴾: conjoined to what preceded; ومن مارج is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلق, and من is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); ومن نار is a naʿt (adjective) of مارج, and من is explicative (li-l-bayān) or partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ).

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿رب المشرقين ورب المغربين﴾: رب المشرقين is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هو رب المشرقين (He is the Lord of the two easts); and رب المغربين is conjoined to it.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t: ﴿مرج البحرين يلتقيان﴾: مرج البحرين is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause يلتقيان is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿بينهما برزخ لا يبغيان﴾: the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); برزخ is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); لا is negating; يبغيان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of برزخ; and the whole clause is resumptive with no grammatical position, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يلتقيان.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان﴾: the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position, or a second ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يلتقيان; ومنهما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يخرج; اللؤلؤ is the fāʿil (agent) of يخرج; and المرجان is conjoined to اللؤلؤ.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t: ﴿وله الجوار المنشآت في البحر كالأعلام﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; وله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); الجوار is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); المنشآت is a naʿt (adjective) of الجوار; وفي البحر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to المنشآت; ﴿كالأعلام﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الجوار, or from the pronoun in المنشآت; and ﴿الأعلام﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿كل من عليها فان﴾: كل is a mubtadaʾ (subject); من is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by annexation to كل; وعليها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. فان is the khabar (predicate) of كل, and the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; يبقى is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); وجه ربك is its fāʿil (agent); ذو الجلال is a naʿt (adjective) of وجه; and الإكرام is conjoined to الجلال.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿يسأله من في السماوات والأرض كل يوم هو في شأن﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; and you may make the clause a ḥāl (circumstantial) from وجه, what governs it being يبقى, i.e.: He remains while being asked by the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth; يسأله is an imperfect verb and its fronted object (mafʿūl); من is a relative, the fāʿil (agent) of يسأله; وفي السماوات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. What is asked for is omitted: the inhabitants of the heavens ask Him for forgiveness, and the inhabitants of the earth ask Him for forgiveness and provision. كل يوم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to the (notion of) being-established (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) of هو is attached; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject); and في شأن is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t: ﴿سنفرغ لكم أيها الثقلان﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; the sīn is a particle of the future; نفرغ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being نحن (We); ولكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نفرغ; ﴿أي﴾ الثقلان: (أي) is the one addressed (munādā), a specifically intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), from which the vocative particle has been omitted; and الثقلان is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أي﴾.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿يا معشر الجن والإنس إن استطعتم أن تنفذوا من أقطار السماوات والأرض فانفذوا﴾: يا is a vocative particle; معشر الجن is the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf); الإنس is conjoined to الجن; إن is conditional; استطعتم is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; تنفذوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; أن with what falls in its scope is in the position of the accusative as the object of استطعتم; ومن أقطار السماوات والأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تنفذوا﴾; فانفذوا: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because the apodosis is a request; and انفذوا is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿لا تنفذون إلا بسلطان﴾: لا is negating; تنفذون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and وبسلطان is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تنفذون﴾.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿يرسل عليكما شواظ من نار ونحاس﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; يرسل is an imperfect verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named); وعليكما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يرسل; شواظ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ومن نار is a naʿt (adjective) of شواظ; نحاس is conjoined to شواظ; and it was also read with the genitive, conjoined to نار.
﴿فلا تنتصران﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; لا is negating; تنتصران is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the alif is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:36-36.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t: ﴿فإذا انشقت السماء فكانت وردة كالدهان﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, containing the meaning of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its apodosis; ﴿انشقت السماء﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; فكانت is conjoined to انشقت; the noun of kānat is latent (mustatir), referring back to السماء; وردة is its khabar (predicate); and وكالدهان is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of وردة, or a second khabar of kānat, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the noun of kānat.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t: ﴿فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان﴾: the fāʾ links the answer of إذا; it has been said: the answer of إذا is omitted, i.e.: so when the heaven is split you will see a tremendous matter, and the fāʾ is conjunctive, conjoining to it; but there is no need for this strained interpretation. ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: an adverb (ẓarf) of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the negated verb ﴿يسأل﴾; and إذٍ: a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: يوم إذ انشقت السماء (the day when the heaven is split); لا is negating; يسأل is an imperfect verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named); وعن ذنبه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يسأل; إنس is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ولا جان is conjoined to إنس; and الجان and الإنس are each a generic noun (ism jins).

muyesser-irab:40-40.t: ﴿فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); وبأي is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبان﴾; آلاء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ربكما is muḍāf ilayhi; تكذبان is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil (agent); and the address is to the two weighty races (al-thaqalān), mankind and jinn.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم﴾: يعرف is an imperfect verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named); المجرمون is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and وبسيماهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يعرف﴾.
﴿فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; يؤخذ is an imperfect verb, passive; وبالنواصي is the nāʾib fāʿil; يؤخذ is transitive (by itself), yet it has been made transitive with the bāʾ because it has been made to include the meaning of يُسحب (is dragged).

nahhas-irab:1-2.t: الرَّحْمنُ (1): nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ (2), i.e. out of His mercy He taught the Qur'an, and by it He made clear His good pleasure, which brings one near to Him, and His displeasure, which drives one away from Him and from His mercy.

nahhas-irab:3-4.t: So it is a khabar (predicate) after a khabar.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject). It was said: the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. they both run بِحُسْبانٍ. And it was said: the khabar is بِحُسْبانٍ.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: النجم is whatever crops spread out over the ground, meaning herbs and the like; he said: and الشجر is whatever stands on a stem. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the best of what has been said about its meaning, i.e. everything prostrates to Him, i.e. submits to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَالسَّماءَ رَفَعَها: You put it in the accusative by an implied verb, conjoining what a verb governed onto its like. وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزانَ: al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. justice. Someone else said: it is the balance with which things are weighed.

nahhas-irab:8-9.t: أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزانِ (8): «أن» is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is "so that you do not transgress" (بأن لا تطغوا); تَطْغَوْا is in the position of the accusative by أن. It is also possible for «أن» to have the meaning of أي (i.e. explicative), in which case it has no grammatical position, and تطغوا is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is preferable, because after it comes وَأَقِيمُوا الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ وَلا تُخْسِرُوا الْمِيزانَ (9). Bilāl ibn Abī Burda read وَلا تُخْسِرُوا with fatḥa on the tāʾ [i.e. تَخسَروا]; it is a well-known dialect.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: الأرض is in the accusative by an implied verb.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: فِيها فاكِهَةٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject). وَالنَّخْلُ ذاتُ الْأَكْمامِ: conjoined to it. The singular is كمّ, which is whatever surrounds it [the fruit] of fibre, palm fronds and other things.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: وَالْحَبُّ: nominative as being conjoined to فاكهة, i.e. "and in it are grains." ذُو الْعَصْفِ: a naʿt (adjective) of it. وَالرَّيْحانُ: also conjoined. The reading of al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī is ذُو الْعَصْفِ وَالرَّيْحانُ in the genitive [i.e. والريحانِ], in the sense of "and possessing fragrant herbs" (وذو الريحان).

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: [it means] "So which of the blessings of your Lord [will you both deny]?" Abū Jaʿfar said: If it is said: only man has been mentioned before, so how does the address come to be to two things? There is more than one answer to this. Among them: الأنام includes the jinn and mankind, so they were addressed on that basis. It was also said: when He, Majestic and Mighty, said وَالْجَانَّ خَلَقْناهُ [al-Ḥijr: 27], and man had been mentioned before, all were addressed. al-Farrāʾ permitted that it be an address to a single person using the verb of two, and he reported that from the Arabs.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: الصّلصال is dry clay. On this view the meaning is: He created man from dry clay that makes a sound as clay sounds when fire has touched it, and that is earthenware (al-fakhkhār). It was also said: الصلصال means "stinking", of the pattern faʿlāl, from صلّ اللحم when meat becomes putrid; one also says أصلّ.

nahhas-irab:15-16.t: It was said: المارج is derived from مرج الشيء when a thing becomes mixed; المارج is from between yellow, green and red, and so is the tongue of fire. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās on مِنْ مارِجٍ مِنْ نارٍ; he said: it is from the pure [part] of fire.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: Nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); it may be a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in «خلق». The genitive is permissible, meaning: "So which of the blessings of your Lord, Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests…", and the accusative is permissible in the sense of "I mean" (أعني).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: It is not repetition, because it only comes after blessings other than those that preceded.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: مرج means "He released." The scholars disagreed about the meaning of "the two seas" here. al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: they are the sea of the Byzantines (the Mediterranean) and the sea of Persia. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn Abzā said: they are the sea of the sky and the sea of the earth; the like is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, except that he said: they meet every year. The view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn Abzā is the one Muḥammad ibn Jarīr adopts, for a reason that made it necessary in his view, which we will mention after this.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t: Some of the people of tafsīr said: they do not transgress against people. Some of them said: neither of them transgresses against the other. The apparent sense of the verse indicates generality.

nahhas-irab:22-23.t:
The reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza is يَخْرُجُ [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variant has been lost in the printed text; the reading meant is with ḍamma on the yāʾ, i.e. يُخرَج, "is brought out", as the next sentence shows], and the ḍamma is clearer, because it only comes out when it is brought out.

The scholars discussed the meaning of يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ. The position of al-Farrāʾ is that it only comes out of one of them, and he treated it as figurative. The remoteness in taking «منهما» to mean "from one of them" is not hidden from anyone with understanding. It was also said: يخرج is only for the future, so he says: it will come out of both of them after this. It was also said: it comes out of both of them literally, not figuratively, because it only comes out of the places where the salt water and the fresh water meet. A fourth view is the one Muḥammad ibn Jarīr chose. What led him to it was the tafsīr: someone whose word is taken as proof had said about His saying, Majestic and Mighty, مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيانِ that they are the sea of the sky and the sea of the earth, and pearls and coral are only found in shells when rain falls on them. What shows you this is the ḥadīth from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: "When the sky rains, the shells open their mouths."

nahhas-irab:24-25.t:
الجواري is in the position of the nominative; the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness. Dropping the yāʾ [in writing/pronunciation] is far-fetched; whoever drops the yāʾ says the kasra indicates it, and it used to be dropped before the alif and lām were added.

The reading of the Kufans, except al-Kisāʾī, is وَلَهُ الْجَوارِ الْمُنْشِئاتُ [i.e. with kasra on the shīn], making them [the ships] the agents; «المنشأات» [with fatḥa] is the reading of the people of Medina and of Abū ʿAmr, and it is clearer. As for what is related from ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī, that he read المنشيّات, it is not reliably preserved, because if he replaced the hamza he would say المنشيات, and if he lightened it he would make it between alif and hamza and say المنشاءات, and this is what is preserved of his reading. كالأعلام is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). [Translator's note: the printed text has «كالأعلم».]

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
The pronoun refers back to the earth, which He placed [Translator's note: i.e. mentioned earlier in وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَها]; i.e. everyone on the earth passes away and perishes.
The origin is فاني; the vowel on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy, so it was made vowelless, then it was dropped because of its vowellessness and the vowellessness of the tanwīn after it.

nahhas-irab:27-28.t: ذُو is a naʿt (adjective) of وجه, because the meaning is "and your Lord remains," as you say: "this is the face of the earth." In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd [it is] ويبقى وجه ربك ذي الجلال والإكرام, as a naʿt of ربّك.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: يَسْئَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: The position of Qatāda — not in his exact words — is: the people of the heavens and the people of the earth turn to Him in their needs; they cannot do without Him. كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ: i.e. concerned with their affairs, their well-being and the management of their matters.

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: There are five readings of it. Abū ʿUbayd mentioned two of them, each of which was read by five readers: they are (سنفرغ) and (سيفرغ). The first was read by Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read (سيفرغ) — Abū ʿUbayd did not mention Ṭalḥa. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj and Qatāda read (سنفرغ لكم) with fatḥa on the nūn and the rāʾ. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read (سنفرغ) with kasra on the nūn and fatḥa on the rāʾ, and al-Farrāʾ mentioned that it is read (سيفرغ) with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first two readings have one meaning. Abū ʿUbayd reported that the dialect of the people of the Hijaz and Tihāma is فرغ يفرغ and that the dialect of the people of Najd is فرغ يفرغ [Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing the two dialects has been lost in the printed text; presumably faragha yafrughu versus fariġa/faragha yafragu], and that he knew of no one among the readers who read according to it. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned who read according to it. Whoever says فرغ يفرغ [with fatḥa in the imperfect] brings it according to the original pattern, because it contains one of the guttural letters — the guttural letters are hamza, ʿayn, ghayn, ḥāʾ, khāʾ and hāʾ — and from the guttural letters the pattern faʿala yafʿalu comes frequently, such as ذهب يذهب and صنع يصنع; and there come [verbs] with two dialects, such as صبغ يصبغ and يصبغ, and رعف يرعف and يرعف; and from them there come [verbs] that are hardly ever given fatḥa, such as نحت ينحت. In this one only goes back to [actual] usage.

nahhas-irab:33-34.t: يا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ: a vocative in construct. إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا مِنْ أَقْطارِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا: According to the position of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, the meaning is: "We shall attend to you, O you two weighty ones," and it will be said to you: "O company of jinn and men." He mentioned that this is on the Day of Resurrection: the angels of the seven heavens will descend and surround the regions of the earth, then the Highest King, Majestic and Mighty, will come. al-Ḍaḥḥāk recited: وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا [al-Fajr: 22]. Then Hell will be brought, and when people see it they will flee, while the angels have lined up along the regions of the earth in seven rows. al-Ḍaḥḥāk recited: يَوْمَ التَّنادِ يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ [Ghāfir: 32, 33], and recited: إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا مِنْ أَقْطارِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا. It is related from him that he said: "If you are able to flee from death." It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "If you are able to know what is in the heavens and what is in the earth." لا تَنْفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطانٍ: ʿIkrima said: i.e. by a proof; he said: every سلطان in the Qur'an means a proof. Qatāda said: بسلطان, i.e. by dominion.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُما شُواظٌ مِنْ نارٍ: This is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. Ibn Kathīr and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read — and it is related from al-Ḥasan — (شواظ) with kasra on the shīn. al-Farrāʾ holds that they are two dialects with one meaning, as one says صوار and صوار [i.e. ṣuwār and ṣiwār]. (ونحاس) is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ and the Kufans in the nominative; Ibn Kathīr, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Abū ʿAmr read (ونحاس) in the genitive; Mujāhid read (ونحاس) with kasra on the nūn and the sīn [i.e. ونِحاسٍ]; and Muslim ibn Jundab read (ونحس) without alif and in the nominative.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The nominative in «ونحاس» is clearer in Arabic, because there is no difficulty in it: it is conjoined to «شواظ». If you put it in the genitive, you conjoin it to نار, and you need a contrivance. That is because most of the people of tafsīr, among them Ibn ʿAbbās, say: الشّواظ is the flame and النحاس is the smoke. So if you put it in the genitive, the implied form is "a flame of fire and of smoke," and a flame is not of smoke, just as a blaze is not of smoke, except by a contrivance and an excuse. The contrivance in that — and it is the view of Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] — is that since the flame and the smoke are both from the fire, each of them comprises the other. He recited [a verse] of al-Farazdaq: [ṭawīl metre] 447-
فبتّ أقدّ الزاد بيني وبينه ... على ضوء نار مرّة ودخان
(I spent the night cutting the provisions between me and him [the wolf], by the light of a fire at times, and of smoke.)
So he conjoined ودخان to نار, though smoke has no light, because light and smoke [both] come from the fire; and if you conjoin ودخان to ضوء you do not need a contrivance. Someone else recited on exactly this point: [rajaz metre] 448-
شراب ألبان وتمر وأقط
(A drinker of milk, and dates, and dried curd.)
Only the milk is drunk, but the throat comprises these things. Another said similarly: [majzūʾ al-kāmil metre] 449-
يا ليت زوجك قد غدا ... متقلّدا سيفا ورمحا
(Would that your husband had gone out in the morning girded with a sword and a spear.)
— because both are carried. al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Qatāda said about His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَنُحاسٌ: the copper (al-nuḥās) will be melted and poured on their heads. فَلا تَنْتَصِرانِ: i.e. against whoever punishes you both with that, nor will you gain help from Him [Translator's note: or "against Him"].

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: i.e. So which of the blessings of your Lord — who made the ruling one and the same in preventing [anyone] from passing through, and did not single out anyone in it to the exclusion of another — [will you deny]? [Translator's note: the printed text has «النقود» (coins), apparently for «النفوذ» (passing through); translated according to the context.]

nahhas-irab:37-38.t: فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ: and that is the Day of Resurrection. فَكانَتْ وَرْدَةً: Qatāda said: today it is green, and on the Day of Resurrection red. Someone else added: and it is of iron. كَالدِّهانِ: The soundest thing said about it — and it is the view of Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk — is that it is the plural of دهن (oil), i.e. clear and smooth.

nahhas-irab:39-42.t: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ: the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا. لا يُسْئَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إِنْسٌ وَلا جَانٌّ: The view of Ibn ʿAbbās: they are not asked a question for finding out, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has kept a record of their deeds against them. The view of Qatāda: they are known by the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes; what indicates this is that after it comes يُعْرَفُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيماهُمْ. السيما and السيمياء mean a mark. فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّواصِي وَالْأَقْدامِ: بالنواصي may be in the position of the nominative as the noun whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), and it may be implied [i.e. the deputy agent is an implied pronoun].

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: i.e. it will be said to them: this is Hell, which they used to deny in the world.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَها: i.e. between its layers. وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb reported from Ibn Zayd; he said: الآني means "present." Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās on بَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ; he said: He is saying: its heat has reached its extreme. Abū Jaʿfar said: It is so in the speech of the Arabs; al-Nābigha said: [wāfir metre] 450-
وتخضب لحية غدرت وخانت ... بأحمر من نجيع الجوف ان
(And she dyes a beard that was treacherous and betrayed, with a red [flow] of the belly's blood, at its utmost heat.)

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: i.e. So which of the blessings of your Lord, which He bestowed on you — for He punished none of you but the criminals, and gave them a mark by which they are known so that others are not mixed up with them — [will you deny]?

nahhas-irab:46-47.t: Nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and by an implied verb meaning "is due" or "is established." The implied construction is: "and for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, so performs His obligations and avoids disobeying Him out of fear of the standing at which Allah the Exalted will make him stand for the reckoning." What makes this clear is His saying: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوى فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوى [al-Nāziʿāt: 40]; and one who plunges into acts of disobedience is not called "fearful." Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās on وَلِمَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتانِ; he said: Allah has promised the believers who performed His obligations the Garden.

nahhas-irab:48-49.t: A naʿt (adjective) of the two gardens. al-janna among the Arabs is the orchard. Abū Jaʿfar said: The singular of الأفنان is فنن according to whoever says they are the branches; whoever says they are the kinds — the kinds of fruit — [says] its singular, in their view, is فن. The first is more likely to be correct, because فنّ is mostly pluralised as فنون, so its plural of multitude suffices, just as one says شسع and شسوع. From it is taken [the expression] "so-and-so went into various kinds (funūn) of talk."

nahhas-irab:50-51.t: i.e. among them are two flowing rivers.

nahhas-irab:52-53.t: i.e. of every kind of fruit there are two varieties.

nahhas-irab:54-55.t: مُتَّكِئِينَ is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is among the obscure points of grammar. Abū Jaʿfar said: I know of no one among the grammarians who mentioned it, except something Muḥammad ibn Jarīr mentioned; he said: it is construed according to the meaning, i.e. they enjoy themselves reclining, and he made what precedes it indicate the omitted [verb]. Abū Jaʿfar said: It may be without any omission, referring back to His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَلِمَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتانِ, as you say: لفلان تجارة حاضرا ("so-and-so has trade while present"), i.e. in this state. مُتَّكِئِينَ is according to the meaning of «من»; had it been according to the wording it would have been متّكئا. وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); دانٍ is its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:56-57.t: فِيهِنَّ: Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned this pronoun and to whom it refers; there is a difficulty in it, which we have explained. The implied construction is: in them are ḥūr. قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلا جَانٌّ; and the reading of Ṭalḥa is لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ [Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing Ṭalḥa's variant has been lost in the printed text; presumably يطمُثهنّ with ḍamma on the mīm]; they are two well-known dialects.

nahhas-irab:58-59.t: أن is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the kāf is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being omitted. «هنّ» is in the position of the accusative as the noun of «أنّ», and it was doubled because it is equivalent to two letters in the masculine [i.e. هم]. الْياقُوتُ is the khabar, and وَالْمَرْجانُ is conjoined to it. [Translator's note: the printed text has «عطل» for «عطف».]
