nahhas-irab:60-61.t: A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); i.e. [what is] the reward of one who did good in the world, except that good be done to him in the Hereafter?

nahhas-irab:62-63.t: There are two views on its meaning. One of them: "and below them two" in rank (degrees). This is the position of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he interpreted these two gardens [the first two] as being the ones about which Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ ما أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ [al-Sajda: 17]. The other view is: "and below them two" in excellence; this is the position of Ibn Zayd; he said: and they are for the Companions of the Right.

nahhas-irab:64-65.t: Abū Ḥātim said: مدهمّتان is permissible in ordinary speech, because one says ادهمّ and ادهامّ. مدهامتان is a naʿt (adjective) of the two gardens.

nahhas-irab:66-67.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās on [نَ]ضَّاخَتانِ [Translator's note: the printed text has «ضَّاخَتانِ» with the initial nūn missing]; he said: "overflowing." al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "full." Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: gushing with water and fruit. Abū Jaʿfar said: What is known in the language is that they [gush] with water.

nahhas-irab:68-69.t: There are three views about it. Among them: it was said that palm trees and pomegranates are not among the fruits, since in this verse they are set apart from them. It was also said: they are among them, but they were mentioned again in praise of them, because of their excellence. It was also said: the Arabs repeat a thing with the wāw of conjunction for amplitude, not for preference, and the Qur'an came down in their language. The evidence for that is أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ [al-Ḥajj: 18], then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ; and He, exalted be His praise, said: حافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَواتِ وَالصَّلاةِ الْوُسْطى [al-Baqara: 238]. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is clear; there is no ambiguity in it.

nahhas-irab:70-71.t: al-Farrāʾ reported خيّرات and خيرات. As for the Basrans, they said: خيرة has the meaning of خيّرة, and it was lightened, just as one says ميّت and ميت. «فيهن» refers back to the four gardens.

nahhas-irab:72-73.t: حُورٌ: a badal (substitute), or if you wish, a naʿt (adjective). مَقْصُوراتٌ: Mujāhid said: they have restricted their glances and themselves to their husbands, and do not want others. Abū al-ʿĀliya said: «مقصورات» means confined. al-Ḥasan said: مقصورات means confined, not going about in the streets. Abū Jaʿfar said: What is correct in this is to say: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, described them as مقصورات and made it general, so we make it general as He, Majestic and Mighty, made it general, and say: they have restricted their glances and themselves to their husbands, so they do not see others, and they are confined in the pavilions and guarded.

nahhas-irab:74-75.t: So by this He indicated that the jinn have intercourse.

nahhas-irab:76-77.t:
مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ: خضر is the plural of أخضر, and رفرف is singular in form, but it has been described with a plural because it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), as one says: مررت برهط كرام وقوم لئام ("I passed by a noble band and a base people"), and likewise هذه إبل حسان وغنم صغار ("these are fine camels and small sheep"). وَعَبْقَرِيٍّ is like it, except that it may be the plural of عبقرية. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read متكئين على رفارف خضر وعباقريّ حسان, and some related this reading from ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī from Abū Bakra from the Prophet ﷺ, but its isnad (chain of transmission) is not sound. Abū ʿUbayd claimed that if it were sound it would be وعباقريَّ without full declension (ijrāʾ), and claimed that this is what Arabic requires.

Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear error in the view of all the grammarians, because they have all agreed that one says رجل مدائنيّ ("a man of al-Madāʾin") with full declension; he only imagined that it is a plural. There is in the speech of the Arabs no plural having four letters after its alif. There is no disagreement among them that if you pluralised عبقر you would say عباقر, and, far-fetchedly, عباقير, and عباقرة is permissible. As for عباقريّ as a plural, it is impossible. The reason why عباقريّ cannot be permitted is that it must either be a relative adjective (nisba) of عبقر, in which case one says عبقريّ, or a relative adjective of عباقر, in which case it is returned to the singular and one also says عبقريّ — as all the grammarians laid down regarding the nisba of a plural, that you form the nisba from its singular, so you say for the nisba of المساجد: مسجديّ, of العلوم: علميّ, and of الفرائض: فرضيّ. If someone says: what prevents عباقر from being the name of a place to which the nisba is then formed, as one says معافريّ? It is said to him: the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is not construed according to what is not known, while abandoning the proof of consensus.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t:
تَبارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ: i.e. blessing is in His name, Majestic and Mighty. Blessing (al-baraka) in the language is the permanence and firmness of a favour.
So by this He urged them to mention His name, Majestic and Mighty, often, and to call upon Him, and to mention Him with reverence and glorification of Him, so He said: ذي الجلل والإكرام [Translator's note: so in the printed text, for ذِي الْجَلالِ], i.e. the Majestic, the Noble. In the ḥadīth: «ألظّوا بيا ذا الجلال والإكرام» ("Hold fast to [saying] 'O Possessor of Majesty and Honour'").

safi-cedvel:7-13.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (السماء) is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of an omitted verb that is explained by the verb mentioned after it.
The clause «(رفع) السماء ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause «علّمه البيان» [Note: in verse (4) of this sūra]. The clause «رفعها ...» has no grammatical position, being explicative. The clause «وضع ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause (رفع), which is implied.
8- (أن) is a particle of the verbal noun (maṣdar) and of the accusative; (لا) is a negation. [Note: it is possible that (أن) is explicative (mufassira) and (لا) is prohibitive ... because the setting of the balance calls for the command to act justly, and this is the statement ...]. (في الميزان) is attached to (تطغوا). The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تطغوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted lām, attached to (وضع), i.e. "so that you do not transgress ...".
The clause «تطغوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle (أن) which forms a maṣdar.
9- (الواو) is parenthetical. (بالقسط) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of أقيموا. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is prohibitive and jussive ...
The clause «أقيموا ...» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical. The clause «لا تخسروا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the parenthetical clause.
10- 13- (الواو) is a conjunction in the four places. (الأرض) is a direct object of an omitted verb that is explained by the verb mentioned after it. (للأنام) is attached to (وضعها). (فيها) is attached to a fronted predicate (khabar) of the subject (mubtadaʾ) (فاكهة). (الفاء) is the connecting particle for the apodosis of an implied condition. (بأي) is attached to (تكذّبان). [Note: this verse is mentioned thirty-one times. Eight of them come after verses that enumerate the wonders of Allah's creation and the marvels of His handiwork; then seven after verses mentioning the Fire and its terrors; then eight verses describing the two gardens; and another eight describing the two gardens below the first two ... The repetition came for emphasis and reminder.]
The clause «(وضع) الأرض ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause «وضع الميزان» [Note: in verse (7) of the sūra].
The clause «وضعها ...» has no grammatical position, being explicative. The clause «فيها فاكهة ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from الأرض. The clause «بأي ... تكذبان» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the matter is as has been detailed, then which of the favours ...".

* Morphology:
(الميزان): the first means justice (al-ʿadl), the second means the instrument for measuring weight, and the third means what is weighed ... See verse (152) of Sūrat al-Anʿām.
(12) العصف: an inert noun (ism jāmid) for the leaf of every plant from which grain comes out; its pattern (wazn) is فعل with a fatḥa and then a sukūn. (الريحان): it is originally a maṣdar, then was applied to a well-known fragrant plant, and it also means provision (rizq). According to al-Farrāʾ it is the leaf of the crop, and its pattern is فعلان with a fatḥa on the first letter.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (al-takrīr): in the saying of the Exalted فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ.
It is repeated many times in this sūra, and this repetition, when repeated, is sweeter than sugar. It is fitting only as an affirmation of the various, enumerated blessings: whenever He, glory be to Him, mentions a blessing He has bestowed, He rebukes the denial of it, just as a man says to another: "Did I not do you good by granting you wealth? Did I not do you good by doing such and such for you?" Repetition is fitting here because of the difference in what is being affirmed, and it is frequent in the speech of the Arabs.

safi-cedvel:14-16.t:
* I'rab:
(من صلصال) is attached to (خلق). (كالفخّار) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (صلصال). (من مارج) is attached to the second (خلق). (من نار) is attached to an adjective of (مارج) [Note: (من) is explanatory or partitive ... and if المارج means fire, then it is a substitute (badal) with repetition of the preposition]. (فبأي ... تكذّبان) is like the first [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra], in its words and clauses. The clause «خلق الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «خلق الجانّ ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(الفخّار): a name for what has been baked from clay; its pattern is فعّال with a fatḥa on the first letter. (مارج): a name for what is mixed of red, green and yellow; it was also said that it means the pure, and also said that it is the flickering flame; its pattern is فاعل with a kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:17-18.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject, its implied form being "he" (هو). (فبأي ... ) is like the first, in its words and clauses «1». The clause «(هو) ربّ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:19-23.t:
* I'rab:
The agent (fāʿil) of (مرج) is a pronoun referring to Allah. (بينهما) is accusative, attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (برزخ). (لا) is a negation ... (فبأي ... ) is like the first in both places «2», in its words and clauses. (منهما) is attached to (يخرج) ...
The clause «مرج ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «يلتقيان ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from البحرين. The clause «بينهما برزخ ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from البحرين or from the agent of يلتقيان. The clause «لا يبغيان ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from البحرين [Note: or from the agent of يلتقيان, or from the pronoun in (بينهما) .. and it carries the sense of giving a reason, i.e. "so that they do not transgress"]. The clause «يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(22) المرجان: a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for one of the precious stones; its pattern is فعلان with a fatḥa on the first letter, and its singular is مرجانة. It is red veins like the fingers of the hand; it was also said that it is small pearls.

* Rhetoric:
The art of broadening (fann al-ittisāʿ): in the saying of the Exalted يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ.
He said "from both of them" and did not say "from one of them", because when the two met and became like one thing, it was permissible to say that they come out of both of them, as one says "they come out of the sea" although they do not come out of the whole sea but out of a part of it. You also say "I left the town" when you have left only one quarter of its quarters, indeed one house of its houses.

safi-cedvel:24-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (له) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (الجواري); it is nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, for the sake of agreement with the reading in connected recitation (waṣl). (في البحر) is attached to (الجواري). (كالأعلام) is attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in المنشئات. (فبأي ... ) is like the first [Note: in verse (13) of the sūra], in its words and clauses ...
The clause «له الجواري ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(المنشآت): plural of المنشأة, the feminine of المنشأ, a passive participle of the quadriliteral (أنشأ); its pattern is مفعل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
The unrestricted simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in the saying of the Exalted وَلَهُ الْجَوارِ الْمُنْشَآتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلامِ.
Here He, glory be to Him, the Exalted, likened the ships, as they cleave the swell of the sea, going and coming, to towering mountains.

safi-cedvel:26-28.t:
* I'rab:
(من) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi. (عليها) is attached to an omitted ṣila of (من). (فان) is the predicate of the subject, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ). (ذو) is an adjective of وجه, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw. (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra.] The clause «كلّ من عليها فان» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «يبقي وجه ربّك ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(26) فان: an active participle of the triliteral (فني), its pattern is فاع, with an elision weakening (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters, the quiescence of the yāʾ and the tanwīn.
(27) الجلال: an auditory maṣdar (maṣdar samāʿī) of the triliteral verb جلّ; its pattern is فعال with a fatḥa on the first letter. (الإكرام): a regular maṣdar (maṣdar qiyāsī) of the quadriliteral verb أكرم; its pattern is إفعال ...

* Rhetoric:
1- The unrestricted figurative usage (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of the Exalted وَيَبْقى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ.
That is, His Essence, mighty and majestic, and what is meant is He Himself, glory be to Him, the Exalted. The annexation is explanatory (bayāniyya). The literal meaning of "face" in the observable world is the bodily member, and using it for the Essence is an unrestricted figurative usage, like the use of "hands" for "selves".
2- The art of variation (fann al-iftinān): in the saying of the Exalted كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْها فانٍ وَيَبْقى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلالِ وَالْإِكْرامِ.
This art is that the speaker varies, bringing in his speech two kinds, either opposed, or different, or agreeing. Here He, glory be to Him, combined consolation and boasting: He consoled all creatures, and praised Himself for being alone in remaining after the passing away of all that exists, while describing His Essence, after His being alone in remaining, with majesty and honour.

safi-cedvel:29-30.t:
* I'rab:
(في السموات) is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun (من). (كلّ) is a noun indicating time that stands in for the adverb "day" (yawm); it is accusative, attached to the settledness (al-istiqrār) which is the predicate of the subject (هو). (في شأن) is attached to the predicate of the subject (هو). (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses «1». The clause «يسأله من في السموات» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «هو في شأن» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:31-32.t:
* I'rab:
(لكم) is attached to (سنفرغ). (أيّها) is an indefinite specific vocative (munādā nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable, in the position of the accusative. (فبأي ... ) is like the first «2». The clause «سنفرغ لكم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «أيّها الثقلان ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(الثقلان): the dual of ثقل (with two fatḥas), its pattern is فعل; a collective noun for mankind or the jinn, either in the sense of "one who weighs down" (muthqil, with kasra on the qāf), i.e. who weighs down the earth, or in the sense of "one who is burdened" (mathqūl, with fatḥa on the ʿayn), i.e. loaded with obligations and wearied by them.

* Benefits:
The letter hāʾ..
In this verse occurs the saying of the Exalted: سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ الثَّقَلانِ. Here (إلها) is an alerting particle (ḥarf tanbīh). We will set out the cases of this letter, in order to clarify what is connected with it. It occurs in five ways: 1- It comes as a pronoun for the third person, and is in the position of the genitive or the accusative, as in the saying of the Exalted: قالَ لَهُ صاحِبُهُ وَهُوَ يُحاوِرُهُ. [Translator's note: the source repeats the verse in the text as "تعالى: قالَ لَهُ صاحِبُهُ وَهُوَ يُحاوِرُهُ" twice; the repetition is a slip in the source.]
The hāʾ of له and of صاحبه is in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the hāʾ of يحاوره is in the position of the accusative, a direct object.
2- It comes as a particle of the third person: this is the hāʾ in (إيّاه). The verified view is that it is a particle with merely the meaning of the third person, and that the pronoun is «إيّا» alone.
3- The hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt): this is the one attached to clarify a vowel or a letter, as in (ماهية), and (هاهناه) and (وا زيداه), and the saying of the Exalted: ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ. هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ.
4- The one substituted for the hamza of interrogation, as in the verse:
وأتى صواحبها فقلن: هذا الذي ... منح المودة غيرنا وجفانا
(Her companions came and said: "Is this the one who granted affection to others than us and shunned us?") 
The verified view is that this one should not be counted, because it is not original; moreover some claimed that the original is «هذا» and the alif was dropped.
5- The hāʾ of the feminine, as in (رحمه) in pausal form. This is the opinion of the Kufans. The verified view is that it should not be counted, because it is part of a word, not a word.
As for (ها), it occurs in three ways:
1- A verbal noun (ism fiʿl) meaning (خذ) "take"; its alif may be lengthened, and both are used with the kāf of address and without it. In the lengthened form it is permissible to dispense with the kāf by inflecting its hamza as the kāf is inflected, so one says (هاء) for the masculine, (هاء) for the feminine with a kasra on the hamza, and (هاؤما), (هاؤنّ), (هاؤم); from this is the saying of the Exalted: هاؤُمُ اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ.
2- It is a pronoun for the feminine, used in the position of the genitive and the accusative, as in the saying of the Exalted: فَأَلْهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْواها; in the first it is in the position of the accusative, and in the other two in the position of the genitive.
3- It is for alerting, and enters upon four things:
1- The demonstrative not specific to the far, as in: (هذا). As for (هنا), the hāʾ is original and is not for alerting.
2- The nominative pronoun about which a demonstrative noun gives information, as in the saying of the Exalted: ها أَنْتُمْ أُولاءِ.
3- The adjective of (أي) in the vocative, as in: (يا أيها الرجل). In the dialect of Banū Asad it is permissible to drop its alif and to give its hāʾ a ḍamma by assimilation, and on this is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir (أيّه المؤمنون) (أيّه الثقلان).
4- The name of Allah the Exalted in an oath when the particle is omitted: one says «ها الله», with the hamza pronounced as a cutting or a connecting hamza, both with the alif of (ها) retained and dropped.

safi-cedvel:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(استطعتم) is a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of the jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (أن) is a particle of the verbal noun (maṣdar) and of the accusative. (من أقطار) is attached to (تنفذوا). (الفاء) is the connecting particle for the apodosis. (لا) is a negation. (إلّا) is for restriction. (بسلطان) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of تنفذون [Note: or attached to (تنفذون)]. (فبأي ... ) is like the first [Note: in verse (13) of the sūra]. The interpreted maṣdar (أن تنفذوا ...) is in the position of the accusative, a direct object.
The clause of the vocative «يا معشر ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «إن استطعتم ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative. The clause «تنفذوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle (أن) which forms a maṣdar. The clause «انفذوا ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ. The clause «لا تنفذون ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you pass through, you will not pass through"].

safi-cedvel:35-36.t:
* I'rab:
(عليكما) is attached to (يرسل). (من نار) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (شواظ). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لا) is a negation. (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra.] The clause «يرسل عليكما شواظ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «لا تنتصران ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يرسل.

* Morphology:
(شواظ): a name for pure flame, or flame with smoke in it; its pattern is فعال with a ḍamma on the first letter.
(نحاس): a name for the well-known metal, or meaning smoke with no flame in it; its pattern is فعال with a ḍamma on the first letter.

safi-cedvel:37-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive and the second is a conjunction. (إذا) is an adverb of future time, in the position of the accusative, attached to the content of the implied apodosis. (كالدهان) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (وردة) [Note: it may be a second predicate]. (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses. (الفاء) is a conjunction [Note: or resumptive, or the connecting particle for the preceding apodosis, in which case the clause بأي آلاء ... is parenthetical]. (يومئذ) is an adverb, accusative - or indeclinable on the fatḥa - attached to the negated (يسأل). (لا) is a negation. (عن ذنبه) is attached to (يسأل). (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation. (فبأي ... ) is like the first [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra.] in its words and clauses ...
The clause «انشقّت السماء ...» is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «كانت ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause انشقت ... The apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "you would see a terrible thing". The clause «لا يسأل ... إنس» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the implied apodosis [Note: or has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of إذا, with what is between them parenthetical].
41- 42- (بسيماهم) is attached to a ḥāl from (المجرمون), the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (بالنواصي) is the deputy agent [Note: Abū Ḥayyān said: "to take" (يؤخذ) is transitive, yet it is made transitive here with the bāʾ because it is given the meaning of "to drag". Another said: one says "I took the forelock" and "I took by the forelock". It is related from the Arabs: "I took the rein" and "I took by the rein", with the same meaning.]. (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses. The clause «يعرف المجرمون ...» has no grammatical position, being a justification of what precedes. The clause «يؤخذ بالنواصي ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يعرف المجرمون.

* Morphology:
(الدهان): a noun meaning red leather, or what is used for anointing; its pattern is فعال with a kasra on the first letter. (وردة): the singular of الورد, which is a generic collective noun (ism jamʿ jinsī); its pattern is فعلة with a fatḥa and then a sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): in the saying of the Exalted: فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَالدِّهانِ.
By "rose" (warda) He meant a reddish hue: in spring the rose leans toward yellow; when the cold intensifies it is a red rose; and after that it is a rose leaning toward dusky grey. So the changing colours of the sky when it splits are likened to the rose, and the rose, in the variety of its colours, is likened to oil and the variety of its colours. The thing likened and that to which it is likened are both sensory, that is, of the type of likening the perceptible to the perceptible. [Translator's note: the source says "الغرس" (planting) for what is meant by "warda"; this seems to be a slip in the source, possibly for "الحمرة" (redness); translated as "reddish hue" from the context of the colours that follow.]

safi-cedvel:43-45.t:
* I'rab:
(التي) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, an adjective (naʿt) of جهنّم. (بها) is attached to (يكذّب). (بينها) is an adverb, accusative, attached to (يطوفون), and likewise the adverb conjoined to it. (آن) is an adjective of حميم, genitive like it, and the sign of the genitive is the implied kasra on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ). (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra.] The clause «هذه جهنّم ...» is in the position of the accusative, the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl), of an implied saying. The clause «يكذّب بها المجرمون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (التي). The clause «يطوفون ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from جهنّم, the operator in it being the demonstrative.

* Morphology:
(آن): an active participle from the triliteral أني, of the pattern of ضرب, meaning that its heat became intense; its pattern is فاع; it has an elision weakening (iʿlāl) due to the meeting of two quiescent letters.

safi-cedvel:46-61.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (لمن) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (جنّتان). (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses [Note: in verse (13) of this sūra.] in the following eight verses. (ذواتا) is an adjective of (جنّتان), nominative [Note: or the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being "they two" (هما), and the clause is an adjective of (جنّتان) with what is between them parenthetical (3, 4); or it has no grammatical position, being resumptive]. (فيهما) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (عينان), and the second (فيهما) is the predicate of the subject (زوجان). (من كلّ) is attached to a ḥāl from (زوجان) ..
The clause «لمن خاف ... جنّتان» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «خاف ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من). The clause «فيهما عينان ...» is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (جنّتان) «3». The clause «تجريان ...» is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (عينان). The clause «فيهما من كلّ ...» is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (جنّتان) «4».
54- 55- (متكئين) is an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun of the agent of an omitted verb, and the pronoun refers to those who fear in His saying: لمن خاف, i.e. "they enjoy themselves reclining". (على فرش) is attached to (متّكئين). (من إستبرق) is attached to the predicate of the subject (بطائنها). (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (جني) is a subject (mubtadaʾ), nominative, its predicate being (دان), nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun.
The clause «(يتنعّمون) متّكئين» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «بطائنها من إستبرق ...» is in the position of the genitive, an adjective of فرش. The clause «جني الجنّتين دان» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl [Note: or conjoined to the clause: فيهما من كلّ فاكهة زوجان].
56- 61- (فيهنّ) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (قاصرات). (قبلهم) is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يطمثهنّ). (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is redundant, to emphasise the negation. (جان) is conjoined to أنس, nominative. (هل) is a particle of interrogation carrying the meaning of negation. (إلّا) is for restriction.
The clause «فيهنّ قاصرات ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). The clause «لم يطمثهنّ إنس ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from قاصرات الطرف, the operator in it being the settledness (al-istiqrār). The clause «كأنّهنّ الياقوت ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl from قاصرات الطرف. The clause «هل جزاء ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(48) ذواتا: dual of ذوات - which is originally a singular without dropping the wāw - and the lām of ذوات is a yāʾ, its ʿayn a wāw, and its fāʾ a dhāl, because the original is ذوي - with a yāʾ at the end - in which there is an iʿlāl, because the yāʾ was vowelled and what precedes it had a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif, giving ذوا; then a tāʾ was added at its end. (أفنان): plural of فنن, a name for the branch; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas, and the pattern of أفنان is أفعال. (54) جنى: a name for fruit, or for what is gathered of honey or gold; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas, and it has an iʿlāl by substitution, its original being جني: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and turned into an alif.
(58) الياقوت: a name for the precious red-coloured gem; its pattern is فاعول.

* Rhetoric:
The unrestricted, summarised simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal al-mujmal): in the saying of the Exalted كَأَنَّهُنَّ الْياقُوتُ وَالْمَرْجانُ.
He likened them to the ruby (yāqūt) in the redness of the face, and to the coral (marjān), that is small pearls, in the whiteness of the skin and its clarity; the specifying of the small ones is because they are more intensely white than the large.
Al-Bayhaqī related in al-Baʿth on the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, who said: "The woman among the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr ʿīn) will have the marrow of her shin seen from behind the flesh and bone, from beneath seventy garments, as red wine is seen in a white glass."

safi-cedvel:62-78.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (من دونهما) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (جنّتان). (فبأي ... ) is like the first in its words and clauses [Note: in verse (13) of the sūra] in the following eight places. (مدهامّتان) is an adjective of (جنّتان), nominative, and what is between the adjective and the qualified noun is parenthetical ...
The clause «من دونهما جنّتان ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
66- 70- (فيهما) is attached to a fronted predicate of the subject (عينان), and the second (فيهما) is the predicate of (فاكهة), and (فيهنّ) is the predicate of خيرات ...
The clause «فيهما عينان ...» is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (جنّتان), with what is between them parenthetical. The clause «فيهما فاكهة ...» is in the position of the nominative, a third adjective of (جنّتان), with what is between them parenthetical. The clause «فيهنّ خيرات ...» is in the position of the nominative, a fourth adjective of (جنّتان), with what is between them parenthetical.
72- 78- (حور) is a substitute (badal) for خيرات, nominative. (مقصورات) is an adjective of حور, nominative. (في الخيام) is attached to (مقصورات). (لم يطمثهنّ ... ولا جانّ): its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (56) of the sūra]. (متّكئين على رفرف) is like متكئين على فرش [Note: in verse (54) of the sūra]. (ذي) is an adjective of ربّك, genitive ...
The clause «لم يطمثهنّ إنس ...» is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of حور. The clause «(يتنعّمون) متّكئين» has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: the pronoun in the verb refers to the spouses (al-azwāj) understood from the context of the verses]. The clause «تبارك اسم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(64) مدهامّتان: dual of مدهامة, the feminine of مدهامّ ... It is an active participle of the sextiliteral verb ادهامّ - or a passive participle of it - and both meanings suit the noble verse; its pattern is افعالّ.
(66) نضّاختان: dual of نضّاخة, the feminine of نضّاخ, an intensive form of the active participle, from the triliteral نضخ; its pattern is فعّال with a fatḥa on the first letter. (70) خيرات: plural of خيرة, of the pattern فعلة with a fatḥa and then a sukūn, or plural of خيرة with a fatḥa and a kasra, which is a lightened form of خيّرة with shadda; both words are an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral خار يخير, and they are two adjectives of an omitted qualified noun, by which are meant the women of Paradise, the wide-eyed maidens (al-ḥūr al-ʿīn). (حسان): a broken plural of حسناء, an assimilated adjective from the triliteral حسن of the pattern of كرم; its pattern is فعال with a kasra on the first letter. (72) مقصورات: plural of مقصورة, the feminine of مقصور, a passive participle from the triliteral قصر, meaning "to screen"; its pattern is مفعول. One says "a woman is qaṣīra, qaṣūra and maqṣūra", i.e. veiled in seclusion. (الخيام): plural of خيم, which is a plural of خيمة, that is, it is a plural of a plural; the pattern of خيمة is فعلة with a fatḥa and then a sukūn, the pattern of خيم is فعل with a kasra and then a fatḥa, and the pattern of خيام is فعال with a kasra on the first letter. (76) رفرف: a collective noun (ism jamʿ), whose singular is رفرفة, or a collective generic noun (ism jins jamʿī); it is what hangs down from the couches of precious cloths; its pattern is فعلل, and the collective noun is فعلل with a fatḥa and then a sukūn in each of them. (عبقري): a collective noun whose singular is عبقريّة, or a collective generic noun; the ʿabqarī is the perfect of everything ... Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad said: it is the eminent and precious among men. It was also said: ʿabqarī is related to ʿAbqar, which the Arabs claim is the name of a land of the jinn, so they relate to it everything wondrous ... Quṭrub said: it is not a relative adjective but is in the position of al-kursī, so the doubled yāʾ is not the yāʾ of relation (nisba).

* Rhetoric:
Specification (al-ikhtiṣāṣ): in the saying of the Exalted: فِيهِما فاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ.
He conjoined the date-palm and the pomegranate to "fruit", although they are part of it, as a specification of them and a clarification of their excellence, as if, because of their distinction, they were two other kinds. From this is the saying of Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him: if a man swears not to eat fruit and then eats a pomegranate or fresh dates, he does not break his oath, and his two companions differed from him.

* Benefits:
- Writing the hamza..
In this verse occurs the saying of the Exalted: مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ. In the word (متكئين) the hamza is written on a "seat" (nabra, the tooth of the yāʾ). We shall clarify below the most important matters connected with that rule:
1- The hamza at the beginning of a word is written on an alif; it is above the alif if it has a fatḥa or a ḍamma, such as (أمن) (أصول), and below the alif if it has a kasra, such as (إسلام).
2- The hamza in the middle of a word: we compare its vowel with the vowel of the letter before it and write it on the letter that suits the stronger of the two vowels. The strongest of the vowels is the kasra, followed by the ḍamma, followed by the fatḥa. The kasra is suited by the nabra, the ḍamma by the wāw, and the fatḥa by the alif.
In the word (متكئين) the hamza has a kasra and what precedes it has a kasra, so it is written on a nabra. In the word (ينأون) the hamza has a fatḥa and what precedes it is quiescent, and the fatḥa is stronger and is suited by the alif. And so on ...
- Exceptions to the rule for writing the medial hamza.
1- The hamza with a fatḥa preceded by a quiescent alif is written on the line: عباءة - إضاءة - إساءة.
2- The hamza with a fatḥa or a ḍamma preceded by a quiescent wāw is written on the line, such as سموءل - موءودة.
3- The hamza with a fatḥa, a ḍamma or a kasra preceded by a quiescent yāʾ is written on a nabra, such as: ييئس - سرّني مجّيئك - سررت بمجيئك.
3- [Translator's note: the source numbers this item "3" a second time; it is evidently item 4 of the list] The hamza at the end of a word: if it is preceded by a vowelled letter it is written on a letter that suits the vowel of what precedes it, such as: (ناشئ) تباطؤ - ملجأ. If it is preceded by a quiescent letter it is written on the line if it has a ḍamma or a kasra, such as: عبء or عبء, بطء or بطء. If it has a tanwīn of fatḥa, it is written on a nabra if it can be connected to the letter before it, such as:
عبئا - بطئا. If it cannot be connected, it is written on the line, with the tanwīn drawn after it on the alif, such as: جزءا - ردءا, except when it is preceded by a quiescent alif, in which case the tanwīn is drawn above the hamza, such as: رداء - جزاء.

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(القرآن) is a second direct object, and the first object is omitted, its implied form being "whomever He willed" [Note: or Jibrīl, or Muḥammad, peace be upon him, or the human being, as indicated by «خلق الإنسان»] ...
Clause: «الرحمن علّم القرآن ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause. And the clause: «علّم ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الرحمن). And the clause: «خلق ... » is in the position of the nominative, a second khabar. And the clause: «علّمه البيان ... » is in the position of the nominative, a third khabar.

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(بحسبان) is attached to an omitted element, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they run by a reckoning" [Note: which is a specific being (kawn khāṣṣ), or attached to a general being (kawn ʿāmm), with an omitted muḍāf in the mubtadaʾ: "the running of the sun and the moon.."]. Clause: «الشمس ... بحسبان» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical [Note: because the implied clause (رفع) السماء is conjoined to the clause علّمه البيان]. And the clause: «النجم ... يسجدان» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the parenthetical clause. And the clause: «يسجدان» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (النجم ...).

* Morphology:
(النجم) is the name of the plant that has no stem; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa and then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit derivative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-tabaʿiyya): in His words, Exalted is He, وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدانِ.
What is meant by their prostration is their submission to Him, Exalted is He, in what He wills of them by their natural disposition; their running according to what their nature requires is likened to the submission of one prostrating to his Creator and his glorifying Him. Then the name of the thing likened to was used for the thing likened. So there is here an explicit derivative metaphor.
2- The art of tawhīm (suggestion of a misleading sense): in His words, Exalted is He, وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدانِ.
This art is the speaker's bringing a word that makes the rest of the speech, before it or after it, suggest that the speaker intended a shared word with another, or intended its mis-writing or alteration, or a difference in its i'rab, or in its meaning, or some other kind of difference, whereas the matter is the opposite. Mention of the sun and the moon suggests to the hearer that النجم is one of the stars of the sky, whereas what is meant is the plant that has no stem.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {الجوار}: the majority read it with kasra on the rāʾ, because it is a manqūṣ noun (one ending in a defective yāʾ) on the pattern mafāʿil, and the yāʾ is dropped in pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ʿAbd Allāh and al-Ḥasan read — and it is also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr — «الجَوارُ» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, as if the omitted letter were forgotten; from this is:
4173 - لها ثنايا أربعٌ حِسانُ ... وأربعٌ فثَغْرُها ثَمانُ (She has four fine front teeth, and four more, so her mouth [has] eight.) This is like their saying «هذا شاكٌ». The explanation of this has already been given in al-Aʿrāf at His saying: {وَمِن فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٍ} [al-Aʿrāf: 41].
His saying: {المنشئات}: Ḥamza and Abū Bakr — with a disagreement in what is transmitted from him — read it with kasra on the shīn, meaning that they produce the waves by their running, or produce the voyage, coming and going, or [they are] those that have raised their shuruʿ, i.e. their sails. The shirāʿ is the sail (al-qilʿ). From Mujāhid: whenever it raises its sail it is among the munshiʾāt, otherwise it is not among them. Attributing the raising to them is figurative (majāz), as one says: «أنْشَأتِ السحابةُ المطرَ» (the cloud produced the rain). The rest read it with fatḥa, and it is a passive participle (ism mafʿūl), i.e. Allah or people produced them, or raised their sails. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «المُنَشَّآت» with a doubled shīn, for intensiveness. Al-Ḥasan read «المُنْشات» in the singular, with the hamza changed into an alif and with a drawn-out tāʾ (tāʾ majdhūba) in the writing; he made the adjective singular, relying on the noun described to convey the plurality, as in His saying: {أَزْوَاجٌ مُّطَهَّرَةٌ} [al-Baqara: 25]. As for his changing the hamza into an alif, although its regular treatment would be bayna bayna (a sound between hamza and the long vowel), that is an exaggeration in lightening, as in his saying:
4174 - إنَّ السِّباعَ لَتَهْدَا في مَرابِضِها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (The beasts of prey are indeed at rest in their lairs …)
i.e. «لتهدَأ». As for writing it with the drawn-out tāʾ, that follows its pronunciation in continuous speech (waṣl). And «في البحر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «المُنْشِئات» or «المنشَآت». Its being written with a yāʾ after the shīn in the codices of Iraq strengthens the reading with kasra, and its being written without it strengthens the reading with fatḥa; they omitted the alif as it is omitted in all sound feminine plurals. And «كالأَعْلام» is a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from the latent (mustatir) pronoun concealed in «المُنْشَآت», or from «الجوار»; both amount to the same meaning. Al-aʿlām are mountains, the plural of ʿalam. He said:
4175 - رُبَّما أَوْفَيْتُ في عَلَم ... تَرْفَعَنْ ثوبي شَمالاتُ (Many a time I have climbed up on a mountain-top, north winds lifting my garment.)

semin-durr:26-26.t: And His saying: {كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ}: He gave precedence to those endowed with reason over others, while all of them are meant. The pronoun in «عليها» refers to the earth. Some of them said: "even though it has not been mentioned, as in His saying: {حتى تَوَارَتْ بالحجاب} [Ṣād: 32]." This speaker has been refuted, and they said: rather, it was mentioned before, in His saying: {والأرض وَضَعَهَا} [al-Raḥmān: 10].

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {ذُو الجلال}: the majority read «ذو» with wāw, as an adjective (naʿt) of «الوجه». Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read «ذي» with yāʾ, as an adjective of «ربِّك». There will come a disagreement among the Seven [readers] at the end of the sūra, if Allah the Exalted wills.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {يَسْأَلُهُ مَن فِي السماوات}: there are two views on it. The first: it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «وَجْه», and what governs it is «يَبْقَى», i.e. it remains being asked by the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth.
His saying: {كُلَّ يَوْمٍ}: accusative (manṣūb) by the [verbal notion of] settledness (istiqrār) contained in the khabar (predicate), which is His saying «في شَأْنٍ». Al-shaʾn: the affair.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {سَنَفْرُغُ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «سَيَفْرُغُ» with yāʾ, i.e. Allah the Exalted will attend. The rest of the Seven read it with the nūn of majesty. The rāʾ has ḍamma in both readings, and this is the most eloquent dialect, the dialect of the Ḥijāz. Al-Aʿraj read it with fatḥa on the rāʾ together with the nūn, and it admits two explanations. The first: that it is from «فَرَغَ» with fatḥa on the rāʾ in the past tense, and it was given fatḥa in the imperfect because of the guttural letter. The second: that «فَرِغَ» with kasra on the ʿayn [of the root] has been heard, so this would be its imperfect; this is the dialect of Tamīm. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Abū al-Sammāl read «سَنِفْرَغُ» with kasra on the imperfect prefix and fatḥa on the rāʾ; its justification is clear from what was said earlier in al-Fātiḥa. Abū Ḥātim said: "It is the dialect of lower Muḍar." Al-Aʿmash, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibrāhīm read «سَنِفْرَغُ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ [with two dots] below, as a passive. [Translator's note: the text as printed writes «سَنِفْرَغُ» here, while describing a reading with a ḍamma on a yāʾ, i.e. «سَيُفْرَغُ»; translated as written.] ʿĪsā also read with fatḥa on the nūn of majesty and kasra on the rāʾ. Al-Aʿraj also read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and on the rāʾ, and it is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr. The reading of «أيها» has already been discussed in al-Nūr. "Attending" (al-farāgh) here is a metaphor (istiʿāra). It has also been said: it means "directing oneself towards (al-qaṣd)". A verse of Jarīr was cited:
4176 - ألانَ وقد فَرَغْتُ إلى نُمَيْرٍ ... فهذا حينَ كُنْتُ لهمُ عَذاباً (Now that I have turned to [deal with] Numayr, this is the time I have become a torment to them.) And al-Zajjāj cited:
4177 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فَرَغْتُ إلى العبدِ المقيَّدِ في الحِجْلِ (… I turned to the slave fettered in the shackle.)
This is supported by the reading of Ubayy «سَنَفْرُغُ إليكم», i.e. "We shall direct Ourselves to you." Al-thaqalān are the jinn and mankind, because they are the two weighty burdens (thaqal) of the earth. It has also been said: because of their being weighed down by sins. It has also been said: al-thaqal is mankind, for their nobility, and the jinn were called thus figuratively, by contiguity. Al-thaqal is something great and noble. In the hadith: «إني تاركٌ فيكم ثَقَلَيْن كتابَ الله وعِتْرتي» ("I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my family").

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {فانفذوا}: an imperative expressing incapacity (amr taʿjīz). Al-nufūdh is going out quickly. It has been mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara that what has nūn as its first radical and fāʾ as its second indicates going out, like «نَفَق» and «نَفَرَ». And «إلاَّ بسُلْطان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إنْ اسْتَطَعْتما» as addressed to the two thaqal [jinn and mankind]; by right he should have kept to one course and read «أنْ تَنْفَذا، لا تنفُذان». The majority treated it like His saying: {وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ المؤمنين اقتتلوا} [al-Ḥujurāt: 9], since under each of the two there are many individuals. The wording of the dual is observed in His saying afterwards: «يُرْسَلُ عليكما», so Zayd's reading is not far-fetched.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {شُوَاظٌ}: Ibn Kathīr read it with kasra on the shīn, and the rest with ḍamma; they are two dialectal forms with one meaning. Al-shuwāẓ: it has been said: a flame with smoke. It has also been said: rather, it is pure flame. It has also been said: the red flame. It has also been said: it is the smoke coming out of the flame. Ruʾba said:
4178 - ونارَ حَرْبٍ تُسْعِرُ الشُّواظا ... (And a fire of war kindling the flames.) And Ḥassān said:
4179 - هَجَوتُكَ فاخْتَضَعْتَ لها بذُلٍّ ... بقافِيَة تَأَجَّجُ كالشُّواظِ (I lampooned you, and you bowed to it in humiliation, with a rhyme blazing like flames.)
And «يُرْسَلُ» is passive; this is the reading of the majority. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «نُرْسِلُ» with nūn, and «شواظاً ونُحاساً» in the accusative. And «مِنْ نار» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «شواظ», or attached to «يُرْسَلُ».
His saying: «ونُحاس»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it in the genitive, conjoined to «نارٍ», and the rest in the nominative, conjoined to «شُواظ». Al-nuḥās: it has been said it is the well-known brass, which Allah the Exalted melts and torments them with. It has also been said: smoke that has no flame with it. Al-Khalīl said: it is well known in the speech of the Arabs, and he cited for al-Aʿshā:
4180 - يُضيْءُ كضَوْءِ سراجِ السَّلِيْ ... طِ لم يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ فيه نُحاسا (It shines like the light of an oil lamp in which Allah has put no smoke.)
Its nūn may take ḍamma or kasra; Mujāhid, Ṭalḥa and al-Kalbī read it with kasra. Ibn Jundub read «ونَحْسٌ», as in His saying: {فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ} [al-Qamar: 19]. Ibn Abī Bakra and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «ونَحُسُّ» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and the sīn doubled, from His saying: {إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 152], i.e. "and We kill with the punishment". Ibn Abī Isḥāq also read «ونَحَُِسٍ» with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra on the ḥāʾ, and the sīn in the genitive. And al-Ḥasan and al-Qāḍī [read]
«ونُحُسٍ» with two ḍammas and the sīn in the genitive. Zayd's reading «ونُحاساً» in the accusative has already been mentioned, being conjoined to «شواظاً» in his reading.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {فَإِذَا انشقت}: its apodosis (jawāb) is implied (muqaddar), i.e. "you would see a great terror", or "what happened would happen".
His saying: {وَرْدَةً}, i.e. like a rose. It has been said: it is the well-known flower that is smelled; He likened it to it in redness. And [a verse] was cited:
4181 - فلو كُنْتُ وَرْداً لَوْنُه لعَشِقْنَني ... ولكنَّ ربي شانَني بسَواديا (Had I been rose-coloured, they would have loved me; but my Lord marred me with my blackness.)
It has also been said: it is from the colour of the bay horse (al-faras al-ward), and it was made feminine because the sky is feminine. Al-Farrāʾ said: "He meant the colour of the bay horse, which in spring tends to yellow, in winter to red, and in the severity of the cold to dust-colour; so He likened the changing colours of the sky to the changing colours of the bay among horses." ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read «وَرْدَةٌ» in the nominative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the sense: 'and there came to be a rose sky'; it is of the kind of speech called tajrīd (abstraction), as in his saying:
4182 - فَلَئِنْ بَقِيْتُ لأَرْحَلَنَّ بِغَزْوةٍ ... تَحْوِي الغنائمَ أو يموتَُ كريمُ (If I remain alive, I shall set out on a raid that gathers spoils, or a noble man dies.)" His saying: {كالدهان}: it may be a second khabar (predicate), or an adjective (naʿt) of «وردة», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the noun (ism) of «كانت». Concerning «الدِّهان» there are two views. The first: it is the plural of «دُهْن», like «قُرْط» and «قِراط», and «رُمْح» and «رِماح»; and it is in the sense of His saying: {يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السمآء كالمهل} [al-Maʿārij: 8].
That is the dregs of oil. The second: it is a singular noun. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "the name of what one anoints with, like «الجِزام» and «الإِدام»", and he cited:
4183 - كأنَّهما مَزادَتا مُتَعَجِّلٍ ... فَرِيَّانِ لَمَّا تُدْهَنا بدِهان (As if they were the two water-skins of a hasty man, new, not yet treated with oil.)
Someone else said: it is red leather, and he cited for al-Aʿshā:
4184 - وأَجْرَدَ مِنْ كِرامِ الخَيْلِ طِرْفٍ ... كأنَّ على شَواكِله دِهانا (And a short-haired, noble steed of the best horses, as if there were red leather on its flanks.)
i.e. red leather. This may possibly be a plural. It is supported by what Mundhir ibn Saʿīd cited: 4185 - يَبِعْنَ الدِّهانَ الحُمْرَ كلَّ عَشِيَّةٍ ... بموسِمِ بَدْرٍ أو بسُوْقِ عُكاظِ (They sell the red hides every evening at the season of Badr or in the market of ʿUkāẓ.)
His saying «الحُمْرَ» supports its being a plural; though it may be said that it is like their saying: «أهلك الناسَ الدينارُ الحُمْرُ والدرهمُ البِيْضُ» (the red dinar and the white dirham have ruined people), except that this goes against the basic rule. It has also been said: it was likened to oil (al-dihān), i.e. olive oil, for its melting and swirling; and it has also been said: for its gleam.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {فَيَوْمَئِذٍ}: the tanwīn is a substitute for the clause, i.e. "on the day when the sky is split". The fāʾ in «فيومئذٍ» is [the fāʾ of] the apodosis of the condition (jawāb al-sharṭ). It has also been said: [the apodosis] is omitted, i.e. "when the sky is split, you will see a terrifying matter", and the like. The hāʾ in «ذَنْبه» [refers to one of the two mentioned], and the pronoun of the other is implied, i.e. "nor will a jinn be asked about his sin" either. What puts the adverb in the accusative is «لا يُسأَلُ», and «لا» does not prevent [this]. The disagreement of people about it has already been given in al-Fātiḥa. The reading «جأَنّ» with hamza has also been given there.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān read «بسِيْمائِهم» with the long vowel (madd). The discussion of this has already been given at the end of al-Baqara.
His saying: {فَيُؤْخَذُ بالنواصي}: «يُؤْخَذُ» is transitive, yet it is made transitive with the bāʾ, because it has been made to include the meaning of «يُسْحَبُ» (is dragged); al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said this. But «سحب» is only made transitive with «على»; the Exalted said: {يُسْحَبُونَ فِي النار على وُجُوهِهِمْ} [al-Qamar: 48]. So he ought to have said: it has been made to include the meaning of «يُدَعُّوْن», i.e. "they are shoved". Makkī said: "One only says «أَخَذْتُ الناصِيةَ» and «أخَذْتُ بالناصية». If you said «أَخَذْتُ الدابَّةَ بالناصيةِ», it would not be permissible. It is reported from the Arabs: «أَخَذْتُ الخِطامَ» and «أَخَذْتُ بالخِطام» with the same meaning. It has been said that its implied form is: 'so each one will be seized by the forelocks'; this is not correct, because it is not made transitive to two objects, one of them with the bāʾ, for the reason we mentioned. It may be made transitive to two objects, one of them with a preposition other than the bāʾ, as in «أَخَذْتُ ثوباً من زيد» (I took a garment from Zayd).
This meaning is other than the first, so another object does not sit well with the bāʾ, unless you make it mean 'because of', in which case you may say «أَخَذْتُ زيداً بعمروٍ», i.e. because of him and for his offence." End of quotation. What he said is open to objection (fīhi naẓar), because you say «أَخَذْتُ الثوبَ بدرهمٍ» (I took the garment for a dirham), so it has been made transitive with something other than «مِنْ» as well, in a meaning other than the one he mentioned.
The al- in «النواصي» and «الأقدام» is not a substitute for a pronoun according to the Basrans, so the implied form is "by the forelocks [belonging] to them"; according to the Kufans it is a substitute [for the pronoun]. Al-nāṣiya is the front of the head; this has been treated fully in Hūd. In the hadith of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: «ما لكم لا تَنْصُون مَيِّتكم» ("Why do you not comb out your dead person?"), i.e. you do not stretch out his forelock. Al-naṣiyy is a good pasture. Their saying «فلانٌ ناصيةُ القوم» (so-and-so is the forelock of the people) may be from this, meaning that he is good and beneficial, or like their saying: "he is the head of the people".

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {هذه جَهَنَّمُ}: i.e. it will be said to them. And «آن» means hot, at the extreme of heat. It is a manqūṣ noun like «قاضٍ»: one says «أنى يَأْني فهو آن», like «قَضى يَقْضي فهو قاضٍ». It has already been discussed in al-Aḥzāb. The majority read «يَطوفون», from «طاف». ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «يُطافُون» as a passive, from «أطافهم غيرُهم» (others made them go round). Al-Aʿmash, Ṭalḥa and Ibn Miqsam read «يُطَوِّفُون» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the ṭāʾ and kasra on the doubled wāw, i.e. they make themselves go round. A group read «يَطَّوَّون» with the ṭāʾ and the wāw doubled; the original form is «يتطَوَّفون». [Translator's note: the printed text has «يَطَّوَّون»; the stated original «يتطَوَّفون» implies «يَطَّوَّفون». Translated as written.]

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ}: it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), or it may be [a noun of] place. If it is a maṣdar, it may be annexed to its agent, i.e. his Lord's standing over him and His keeping record of his deeds, from His saying: {أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَآئِمٌ على كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ} [al-Raʿd: 33] — this meaning is reported from Mujāhid; or it may be annexed to its object, the meaning being: standing up for the rights of Allah so that he does not neglect them. If it is [a noun of] place, the annexation is by the slightest connection, since people stand before Allah the Exalted for the reckoning in the open plains of the Resurrection; it has been said: in it is the station of Allah. The apparent meaning is that the two gardens are for one person who fears. It has also been said: one garden for the one who fears among mankind, and another for the one who fears among the jinn, so it is of the type of distribution (tawzīʿ). It has also been said that «مَقام» here is intrusive (muqḥam), the implied form being "and for him who fears his Lord", and [a verse] was cited:
4186 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ونَفَيْتُ عنه ... مَقامَ الذِّئْبِ كالرَّجُلِ اللعينِ (… and I drove away from it the wolf['s station], like the accursed man.)
i.e. I drove away the wolf. This is not good, because the addition of a noun is not an easy matter.

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {ذَوَاتَآ}: an adjective (ṣifa) of «جَنَّتان», or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are possessors of". In the dual of «ذات» there are two usages: returning to the original form, for its original form is «ذَوْيَة», the second radical being wāw and the third yāʾ, since it is the feminine of «ذو»; and the second: forming the dual on the surface form, so one says «ذاتا».
Al-afnān: there are two views on it. The first: it is the plural of «فَنَن», like «طَلَل», which is the branch. Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:
4187 - بكاءَ حمامةٍ تَدْعو هَدِيلاً ... مُفَجَّعةٍ على فَنَنٍ تُغَنِّي (Like the weeping of a bereaved dove calling for its mate, singing on a branch.)
Another said:
4188 - رُبَّ وَرْقاءَ هَتُوفٍ بالضُّحى ... ذاتِ شَجْوٍ صَدَحَتْ في فَنَنِ (Many a grey, cooing dove in the forenoon, full of grief, has sung out on a branch.) Another said:
4189 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... على كلِّ أفنانِ العِضاهِ تَرُوْقُ (… pleasing on every branch of the thorn-trees.)
The second: it is the plural of «فَنّ», like «دَنّ», and Ibn ʿAbbās pointed to this. The meaning is: possessing kinds and varieties. They cited:
4190 - ومِنْ كلِّ أفنانِ اللَّذاذَةِ والصِّبا ... لَهَوْتُ به والعيشُ أخضرُ ناضِرُ (In every kind of pleasure and youthful play I have amused myself, while life was green and fresh.)
Except that the usual plural of «فَنّ» is «فُنون».

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {مُتَّكِئِينَ}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَنْ» in His saying «ولِمَنْ خافَ»; it was only put in the plural following the meaning of «مَنْ», after the singular following its wording. It has also been said: a ḥāl whose governor is omitted, i.e. "they enjoy themselves, reclining". It has also been said: accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). The majority read «فُرُش» with two ḍammas, and Abū Ḥaywa with a ḍamma and a sukūn, which is a lightened form of it.
His saying: {بَطَآئِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ}: this clause may be resumptive; the apparent view is that it is an adjective (ṣifa) of «فُرُش». As for «مِنْ إستبرق», the discussion of «الاستبرق» and what has been said about it has already been given in Sūrat al-Kahf. Abū al-Baqāʾ said here: "The original of the word is a verb on the pattern «اسْتَفْعَلَ»; when it was used as a name, its hamza was made a hamzat qaṭʿ (disjunctive hamza). It has also been said: it is foreign. It has been read with the hamza dropped and kasra on the nūn, and this is a mistake, because that does not occur in nouns, but only in verbal nouns and verbs." End of quotation. As for his saying "and this is a mistake, because that does not occur" to the end — he means that dropping the hamza in continuous speech occurs only in verbs and verbal nouns, whereas in nouns their hamzas are not dropped because they are disjunctive hamzas. This statement is more deserving of being called a mistake: firstly, we do not concede that this reading is a case of dropping the disjunctive hamza by treating it like the connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl); rather, it is a case of transferring the vowel of the hamza to the quiescent letter before it. The vowel of the hamza was a kasra, so the vowel of the nūn is a transferred vowel, not a vowel for the meeting of two quiescent letters. Then his saying "only in verbs and verbal nouns" — this restriction is not correct, by agreement, since that occurs in ten nouns which are not verbal nouns; I mentioned them at the beginning of this work.
His saying: {وَجَنَى الجنتين دَانٍ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The original of «دانٍ» is «دانِوٌ», like «غازٍ», and it underwent the same weakening as it. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «وجَنِيَ» with kasra on the nūn. Its justification: he inclined (imāla) the fatḥa because of the alif, then dropped the alif because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and kept the inclination of the nūn, so it was thought to be a kasra. It has also been read «وجِنَى» with kasra on the jīm, and it is a dialectal form. Al-janā is the fruit that is picked; it is [on the pattern] faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle), like «القَبَض» and «النَقَص».

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {فِيهِنَّ قَاصِرَاتُ}: there is disagreement about this pronoun. It has been said: it refers to the gardens. Then it may be asked: how can a dual precede and then a plural pronoun be brought?
The answer: either [one says] that the minimum plural is two, according to one view, and it has supporting evidence, most of which has been given before; or one says: it refers to the gardens indicated by «الجنتين»; or one says: every single individual has two gardens, so it is correct that they are many gardens; or that the garden contains sitting places, palaces and dwellings, so each one of them was called a garden. It has also been said: it refers to the couches (al-furush). This is a good view with little strain.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«فيهِنَّ»: in these enumerated blessings: the two gardens, the two springs, the fruit, the couches and the fruit within reach." Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "There is far-fetchedness in it", and he had approved the view before it. This is open to objection (fīhi naẓar), because the usage is to say "on the couch is such-and-such", and one does not say "in the couch is such-and-such" except with strain; for this reason al-Zamakhsharī combined other things with the couches so that it would be correct for him to say «فيهن» with the preposition of containment; and because the reality is that a person is on the couches, since he is above them, whereas his being in them can only be said figuratively. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Every place in Paradise is a garden, so it is correct to say «فيهِنَّ»." Al-qāṣirāt are those who restrain their glance, i.e. their eyes, from anyone other than their husbands. Its meaning: they confine their glances to their husbands. Imruʾ al-Qays said: 4191 - مِن القاصِراتِ الطَّرْفِ لو دَبَّ مُحْوِلٌ ... من الذَّرِّ فوق الإِتْبِ منها لأَثَّرا (Of those who restrain their glance; were a year-old young ant to creep over her shift, it would leave a mark.)
«وقاصراتُ الطرفِ» is a case of annexing the active participle to its accusative [object] for lightness, since one says «قَصَرَ طَرْفَه على كذا». What the restraining is attached to is omitted because it is known, i.e. "to their husbands", as explained before. It has also been said: the meaning is that they restrain others' glance to themselves, i.e. when someone sees them, his glance does not pass on to anyone else.
His saying: {لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ}: this clause may be an adjective (naʿt) of «قاصِرات», because its annexation is a verbal (lafẓī, non-defining) annexation, as in His saying: {هذا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا} [al-Aḥqāf: 24] and [his saying]:
4192 - يا رُبَّ غابطِنا لو كان يَطْلُبُكمْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (Many a one who envies us, had he sought you …)
Or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the indefinite noun is specified by the annexation. There is disagreement about this word and the one after it as transmitted from al-Kisāʾī: it is reported from him that he let the reader choose to give ḍamma to whichever of the two he wished; al-Dūrī reported from him ḍamma in the first only, and Abū al-Ḥārith reported from him ḍamma in the second only. They are two dialectal forms: one says «طَمَثَها يَطْمِثُها ويَطْمُثُها» when he has intercourse with her. The origin of al-ṭamth is intercourse leading to the flow of a virgin's blood; then every intercourse came to be called ṭamth, even if there is no blood with it. It has also been said: al-ṭamth is menstrual blood or the blood of intercourse. It has also been said: al-ṭamth is a particular touching. Al-Jaḥdarī read «يَطْمَثْهُنَّ» with fatḥa on the mīm in both words, and it is anomalous (shādhdh), since neither its second nor its third radical is a guttural letter. The pronoun in «قبلَهُمْ» refers to the husbands, indicated by His saying «قاصراتُ الطَّرْفِ», or indicated by «مُتَّكئين».

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {كَأَنَّهُنَّ الياقوت}: this clause may be an adjective (naʿt) of «قاصِرات», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it; Makkī mentioned nothing else. What al-marjān is has already been given. Al-yāqūt is a precious gem; it is said that fire does not affect it, and for that reason al-Ḥarīrī said:
4193 - وطالما أُصْلِيَ اليقاوتُ جَمْرَ غَضَا ... ثم انْطفا الجمرُ والياقوتُ ياقوتُ (How often has the ruby been exposed to the embers of ghaḍā wood; then the embers die out and the ruby is still ruby.)
i.e. it remains as it was, unaffected by it. The point of the simile, as al-Ḥasan said, is the clarity of the ruby and the whiteness of the marjān; this is on the view that it is white, which has been given before. It has also been said: the point lies in … and their preciousness; for that reason they named [women] Marjāna, Durra and the like. [Translator's note: there is a gap («. . .») in the source text here.]

semin-durr:60-60.t: Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «إلاَّ الحِسانُ», i.e. "except the beautiful houris".

semin-durr:62-62.t: His saying: {وَمِن دُونِهِمَا}: i.e. below those two previously mentioned gardens are two gardens, in rank and beauty of appearance. This is according to the apparent view that the first two are superior to the other two. The opposite has also been said, and al-Zamakhsharī preferred it.

semin-durr:66-66.t: Al-naḍkh is more than al-naḍḥ with ḥāʾ, because al-naḍḥ with ḥāʾ is sprinkling and seeping, while al-naḍkh with khāʾ is the gushing of water. Al-idhīmām is blackness and intense greenness; they were made «مُدْهامَّتيْن» (dark green) because of how well-watered they are, and this is observable to the eye; for that reason they said "the blackness of Iraq" (sawād al-ʿIrāq) because of its many trees and crops.

semin-durr:68-68.t: His saying: {وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ}: some have used it as evidence that these two are not among fruit, since conjunction requires difference; so if someone swore "he will not eat fruit", he would not break his oath by eating them. Others say: it is a case of mentioning the specific after the general, by way of detailing it, as in His saying {وملائكته} [al-Baqara: 98] then saying «وجبريلَ وميكَال». This is a loose usage, because «فاكهة» is not general (ʿāmm), since it is an indefinite noun in an affirmative context; it is only unrestricted (muṭlaq). But since it applies truly to palms and pomegranates, this was said about it. [Translator's note: the source cites the verse as al-Baqara: 97; «وملائكته … وجبريل وميكال» is al-Baqara: 98.]

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying: {خَيْرَاتٌ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is the plural of «خَيْرَة» on the pattern faʿla with a sukūn on the second radical; one says: «امرأةٌ خَيْرَةٌ» (a good woman) and another «شَرَّةٌ» (a bad one). The second: it is the plural of «خَيْرة», lightened from «خَيِّرة»; this is indicated by the reading of Ibn Miqsam, al-Yazīdī and Bakr ibn Ḥabīb «خَيِّرات» with a doubled yāʾ. Abū ʿAmr read «خَيَرات» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, plural of «خَيْرَة»; it is anomalous (shādhdh), because the second radical is weak, except that the Banū Hudhayl treat it like a sound letter and say «جَوَزات» and «بَيَضات», and [a verse] was cited:
4194 - أخو بَيَضاتٍ رائِحٌ مُتَأَوِّبُ ... رفيقٌ بمَسْحِ المَنْكِبَيْنِ سَبُوْحُ (The keeper of eggs [an ostrich], going out in the evening and returning by night, gentle in the motion of its shoulders, a swift runner.)

semin-durr:72-72.t:
And «مَقْصورات», i.e. kept secluded. From it is «القَصْر» (the palace), because it keeps in whoever is in it; and from it is the grammarians' term «المقصور», because it is withheld from the long vowel (madd), or withheld from case-inflection (iʿrāb), or the inflection is withheld in it. Women are praised for keeping to their houses, as [Abū] Qays ibn al-Aslat said:
4195 - وتَكْسَلُ عن جيرانِها فيَزُرْنَها ... وتَعْتَلُّ عن إتْيانِهِنَّ فتُعْذَرُ (She is too languid to visit her neighbours, so they visit her; she excuses herself from going to them, and is excused.)
One says «امرأةٌ مَقْصورة» and «قَصيرة» and «قَصورة» with one meaning. Kuthayyir ʿAzza said:
4196 - وأنتِ التي حَبَّبْتِ كلَّ قصيرةٍ ... إليَّ ولم تَعْلَمْ بذاك القَصائرُ
عَنَيْتُ قصيراتِ الحِجالِ ولم أُرِدْ ... قِصارَ الخُطا شَرُّ النساءِ البَحاتِرُ (You are the one who made every secluded woman dear to me, though the secluded women do not know it. I meant those kept within the curtained alcoves; I did not mean those short of step — the worst of women are the dumpy ones.)
Al-khiyām is the plural of «خَيْمة», which is made of thumām grass and other herbage; if it is made of hair it is not called khayma but bayt. Jarīr said:
4197 - متى كان الخيامُ بذي طُلوحٍ ... سُقِيْتِ الغَيْثَ أيتها الخيامُ (When were the tents at Dhū Ṭulūḥ? May you be watered with rain, O tents!)

semin-durr:76-76.t:
His saying: {رَفْرَفٍ}: «الرَّفْرَفُ» is the plural of «رَفْرَفَة», so it is a generic noun (ism jins). It has also been said: rather, it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ); Makkī reported both. It is the fine cloth that hangs down from couches. Al-Jawharī said: "Green cloths from which sitting places are made; the singular is rafrafa." Its derivation is from «رَفَّ الطائرُ», i.e. it rose in the air; and «رَفْرَفَ بجناحَيْه» when it spread them to fly; and the rafraf of clouds is their blowing [along]. Its being a plural is indicated by its being described with a plural. Al-Rāghib said: "The rafīf of trees is the spreading of their branches. «رَفَّ الطائرُ»: it spread its wing, yariffu with kasra. «رَفَّ فَرْخَه يَرُفُّه» with ḍamma: it tended its chick; then it was borrowed for tending. From it: «ماله حافٌّ ولا رافٌّ», i.e. he has no one to surround him and look after him. Al-rafraf is the spread-out [mass] of leaves. And His saying {على رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ}: a kind of cloth likened to meadows. It has also been said: al-rafraf is the edge of the large tent and the pavilion that falls on the ground, short of the ropes and pegs. Al-Ḥasan mentioned that it is cushions." End of quotation. Ibn Jubayr said: "The meadows of Paradise, from «رَفَّ البيتُ» when it is comfortable and fine." From Ibn ʿUyayna: they are carpets. It is described here with «خُضْر» because a generic noun may be described with a plural, as in His saying: {والنخل بَاسِقَاتٍ} [Qāf: 10], and with a singular; its being put in the plural here was made fitting by the plural «حِسان». The majority read «رَفْرَفٍ». ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, ʿĀṣim, al-Jaḥdarī, al-Farqabī and others read «رَفارِفَ خُضْرٍ» in the plural, with a sukūn on the ḍād. From them also «خُضُرٍ» with ḍamma on the ḍād, which is assimilation (itbāʿ) to the khāʾ. It has also been said: it is a dialectal form in the plural of the adjective on the pattern afʿal. A verse of Ṭarafa was cited:
4198 - أيها الفتيانُ في مَجْلِسِنا ... جَرِّدُوا منها وِراداً وشُقُرْ (O young men in our gathering, pick out from them bay horses and chestnuts.)
Another said:
4199 - وما انْتَمَيْتُ إلى خُوْرٍ ولا كُسُف ... ولا لئامٍ غداةَ الرَّوْع أَوْزاعِ (I have never claimed kinship with weaklings, nor with the gloomy-faced, nor with base men scattered on the morning of terror.)
They read «عباقِرِيَّ» with kasra or fatḥa on the qāf and with the yāʾ doubled and with fatḥa, as a diptote. This is problematic, since there is nothing preventing tanwīn on [a word with] the two yāʾs of relation (nisba); it is as if this reader imagined it to be on the pattern mafāʿil and so made it a diptote. Ibn Khālawayh reported from the Prophet ﷺ and a group «وعباقِرِيٍّ» with tanwīn, and «رَفارِفٍ» with full declension is reported from ʿĀṣim. It may be said concerning the one who made «عباقِرِيَّ» a diptote: since it came next to «رفارِفَ», which is a diptote, it was made a diptote for congruence (mushākala); and concerning the one who gave full declension to «رفارِفَ»: since it came next to «عباقريّاً», which is fully declined, he declined it for harmony, as in {سَلاسلاً وأَغْلالاً} [al-Insān: 4], as will come.
Abū Muḥammad al-Marwazī — and he was a grammarian — read «خَضَّارٍ», like «ضَرَّاب», with doubling. [A form] afʿal [paired with] faʿʿāl is not known.
The majority [read] «وعَبْقِرِيٍّ», related to ʿAbqar, which the Arabs claim is the land of the jinn; so everything they considered great and marvelled at they called «عَبْقريٌّ». In the hadith: «فلم أرَ عَبْقَريَّاً يَفْري فَرِيَّه» ("I have not seen a genius doing the work he does"). What is meant by it here, it has been said, is spread carpets with images and figures in them. It has also been said: carpets (al-zarābiyy). It has also been said: rugs (al-ṭanāfis). It has also been said: brocade. And «عَبْقريّ» is the plural of «عَبْقَريَّة», i.e. so it is a generic noun, as was said about «رَفْرف». It has also been said: it is a singular indicating the plural, and for that reason it is described with «حسان».

semin-durr:78-78.t: His saying: {ذِي الجلال}: Ibn ʿĀmir read «ذو الجَلال» with wāw, making it follow the noun [«اسم»]; and thus it is written in the codex of the people of Syria. The rest [read] with yāʾ, as an adjective of «الرَّبِّ», since He is the one described with that. They agreed on the wāw in the first [occurrence], except those I mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {الرحمن}: there are three views on it. One: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "Allah is al-Raḥmān". Two: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied, that is: "al-Raḥmān is our Lord". These two views are held by those who regard «الرحمن» together with this implied element as a verse, for they counted «الرحمن» as a verse, and that cannot be conceived except by joining a khabar or a subject to it, since a verse must be informative; this will come at His saying «مُدْهامَّتان». Three: that it is not a verse, and that it forms one utterance with what follows it, being a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «عَلَّم القرآنَ».

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {عَلَّمَ القرآن}: there are two views on it. The more apparent: that it is ʿallama taking two objects, that is: "he made known", from taʿlīm (teaching); on this the first object is omitted, and it was said that its implied form is "He taught Jibrīl the Qurʾān"; it was also said "He taught Muḥammad"; it was also said "He taught man", and this is preferable because of its generality, and because His saying «خلق الإِنسانَ» points to it. The second: that it is from ʿalāma (sign), so the meaning is: He made it a sign and a verse to be taken care of.
These clauses were brought without a conjunction because they were put forward to enumerate a favour, as you say: "So-and-so did good to so-and-so: he honoured him, he spread his fame, he raised his rank"; because of the closeness of the connection he left out the conjunction. The apparent sense is that they are reports. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«خَلَق الإِنسان» is resumptive, and likewise «عَلَّمه» may be an anticipated ḥāl from al-insān, with «قد» intended with it." End of quotation. This is not apparent; rather the apparent sense is what I gave earlier, and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned no other. If it is asked: why did He put the teaching of the Qurʾān to man before his creation when it comes after it in existence? It is said: because teaching is the cause of his being brought into existence and created.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {بِحُسْبَانٍ}: there are three views on it. One: that «الشمس» is a mubtadaʾ and «بحُسْبان» is its khabar, with an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being: "the course of the sun and the moon is by a reckoning", that is: existing, or established, or was established, by a reckoning. Two: that the khabar is omitted and this prepositional phrase is attached to it, its implied form being: "they run by a reckoning". On these two views, two views are allowed for al-ḥusbān: one, that it is a single maṣdar, meaning al-ḥisāb, so it is like al-shukrān and al-kufrān; the second, that it is a plural of ḥisāb, like shihāb and shuhbān. Three: that al-ḥusbān is its khabar and the bāʾ is locative, meaning "in", that is: "existing in a ḥusbān"; and ḥusbān on this view is a singular noun, a name for the revolving sphere, likened to the ḥusbān of the mill, by whose revolving the mill turns; Mujāhid said this. [Translator's note: the source repeats «وحُسْبان» three times at this point.]

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {والسمآء رَفَعَهَا}: the majority read with the accusative, by ishtighāl, taking into account the end of the sentence, which the grammarians call "the sentence with two faces" (dhāt al-wajhayn). In it is evidence for Sībawayh, who allows the accusative even if the ishtighāl clause contains no pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ contained in the sentence with two faces. Al-Akhfash says: a pronoun is necessary; an example is «هند قامَتْ وعمراً أكرمْتُه لأجلها». He said: "because you took the khabar into account and conjoined to it, and what is conjoined to the khabar is a khabar, so what is required of it is required of this." The majority did not require that, and this is their evidence. Al-Farrāʾ said: "All of them made it accusative without a link, except those among them who were irregular." This was given in full in sūrat Yā Sīn at His saying the Exalted {والقمر قَدَّرْنَاهُ} [Yā Sīn: 39], where the seven differed over its accusative and nominative, and praise be to Allah.
His saying: {وَوَضَعَ الميزان}: the majority read «وَضَع» as a past verb, and «الميزانَ» is accusative as direct object. Ibrāhīm read «ووَضْعَ الميزانِ» with sukūn on the ḍād and genitive «الميزانِ». Its explanation: that it is conjoined to the object of «رَفَعَها», that is: "and He raised the placing of the balance", that is: He gave it standing and elevation for the taking of rights by it; and this is among the wonders of wording, as the implied form becomes: "and He raised the placing of the balance".
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how did He omit the conjunction in the first clauses and bring it afterwards? I say: He rebuked with the first clauses, coming in the manner of enumeration, those who denied al-Raḥmān and His favours, just as one who denies the benefactions of a benefactor is rebuked among people by their being enumerated to him in the example I gave earlier; then He returned the speech to its course after the rebuke, in joining by the conjunction what should be joined, for proportion and nearness. If you ask: what proportion is there between these two clauses that He put the conjunction between them?
