I say: the sun and moon are heavenly, and the star (al-najm) and the tree are earthly, so there is proportion between them from the aspect of contrast; and the sky and earth are always paired; and the course of the sun and moon by reckoning is of the kind of submission to Allah's command, so it suits the prostration of the star and the tree."

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {أَلاَّ تَطْغَوْاْ}: there are two views about this «أنْ». One: that it is the subjunctive particle, with «لا» after it negative, and «تَطْغَوْا» made accusative by «أنْ», and before it an implied lām of cause, attached to His saying «ووَضَع الميزانَ»; the implied form is: "so that you do not transgress", and this is clear. Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed that it be the explicative («أنْ» al-mufassira), and on this «لا» is prohibitive and the verb is jussive by it. But the Shaykh rejected it, in that its condition is the preceding of a sentence containing the meaning of saying, and that is not present. I say: Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ took the view that it is explicative; but Abū al-Baqāʾ seemed to notice the objection and said: "«وأَنْ» means «أَيْ», and the saying is implied", thereby making the thing explained by «أَنْ» implied, not pronounced. However, it may be said that his statement "the saying is implied" is not good, because it does not explain an explicit saying, so how can he imply what cannot rightly be explained? The remedy is for him to say: "what has the meaning of saying is implied."

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ تُخْسِرُواْ}: the majority read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the sīn, from akhsara, that is: to diminish, as in His saying {وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَّزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ}. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Bilāl ibn Abī Burda read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and kasra on the sīn, so fa'ala and afʿala are alike in meaning. One says khasira al-mīzān and akhsarahu, with one meaning, like jabara and ajbara. Abū al-Fatḥ and Abū al-Faḍl reported from Bilāl fatḥa on the tāʾ and the sīn. There are two views on it. One: that it is by omission of the preposition, its implied form being: "and do not suffer loss in the balance"; al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. But the Shaykh said: "There is no need for that, because khasira has come transitively. He the Exalted said: {خسروا أَنْفُسَهُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 12] and {خَسِرَ الدنيا والآخرة} [al-Ḥajj: 11]." I say: This is not of that kind. Do you not see that {خَسِروا أنفسَهم} and {وخَسِر الدنيا والآخرةَ} mean that loss has befallen them, and that they are non-existent? This meaning is certainly not intended in the verse; what is intended is: "do not cause loss to what is weighed in the balance". «تَخْسُروا» was also read, with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the sīn. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ولا تَخْسروا» was read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and with ḍamma, kasra and fatḥa on the sīn. One says khasira al-mīzān yakhsiruhu and yakhsuruhu. As for the fatḥa: the original is «في الميزان», so the preposition was dropped and the verb reached it directly." He repeated the word «الميزان» and did not use a pronoun for it in the two clauses after it, to strengthen its importance, and this is like the saying:
4170 - لا أَرى الموتَ يَسْبِقُ الموتَ شيءٌ ... نَغَّصَ الموتُ ذا الغِنى والفقيرا
(I do not see that anything outstrips death; death has spoiled the life of the rich and the poor.)

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {والأرض وَضَعَهَا}: like His saying {والسمآء رَفَعَهَا} [al-Raḥmān: 7]. Abū al-Sammāl read it nominative, as a mubtadaʾ. And «للأَنام» is the reason for the placing. Al-anām: it was said: living creatures; it was said: the children of Ādam specifically; it was said: they are humankind and jinn. Its pattern is faʿāl like qadhāl, so in the plural of paucity it is ānima, like "āthima woman" (pl.), and in the plural of multiplicity unum, like qadhāl, aqdhila and qudhul.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ}: this clause may be a ḥāl from al-arḍ, but it is an anticipated ḥāl. It is also allowed, and this is the best, that the preposition and its genitive noun be the ḥāl, with «فاكهةٌ» nominative as agent; it is indefinite because benefiting from it is less than benefiting from what is mentioned after it, and this is of the type of ascending from the lower to the higher. Al-akmām: plural of kimm with kasra, which is the vessel of the fruit.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {والحب ذُو العصف والريحان}: Ibn ʿĀmir read all three accusative. There are three views on it. Accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ (specification), that is: "and I specify the grain"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. There is something to consider in it, since it was not included in the meaning of fruit and palm-trees so that He would single it out from among them; he only meant the implying of a verb, which is "I specify", so it is not the technical ikhtiṣāṣ. Two: that it is conjoined to al-arḍ. Makkī said: "because His saying «والأرضَ وَضَعَها» means 'He created it', so He conjoined «الحَبَّ» to that." Three: that it is accusative by an implied «خَلَق», that is: "and He created the grain". Makkī said: "or 'and He created the grain'". And he read thus in agreement with the writing of the codices of his land, for the codices of al-Shām have «ذا» with alif. They allowed for «الرَّيْحان» that it be with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "and possessor of the fragrant herb", so the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, like {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82].
The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read the first two nominative and «الرَّيْحان» genitive, conjoined to «العَصْفِ», and this supports the statement of the one who omitted the muḍāf in the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir. The rest read all three nominative, conjoined to «فاكهة», that is: "and in it also are these things". He mentioned first what they enjoy of fruits, second the thing that combines enjoyment and nourishment, which is the fruit of the palm, and third what nourishes only, which is the greatest of them, because it is the sustenance of most people. On this reading «الرَّيْحان» may be conjoined to what precedes it, that is: "and in it is also the fragrant herb", or it may be genitive by annexation in origin, that is: "and possessor of the fragrant herb", and what was said earlier is done to it.
Al-ʿaṣf: the leaves of crops. It was said: straw. Its origin, as al-Rāghib said, is from "al-ʿaṣf and al-ʿaṣīfa, which is what is cut (yuʿṣaf) from crops"; it was said: it is the broken bits of plants. The ʿāṣif wind: the one that breaks what it passes over; this has been given. Al-Rayḥān is in origin a maṣdar, then it came to be applied to provision, as in their saying "subḥān Allāh wa-rayḥānuhu", that is: His providing; it was said: al-rayḥān here is the fragrant plant.
There are two statements on al-rayḥān. One: that it is on the pattern faʿlān like al-layyān, from roots with wāw; the original is rawḥān. Abū ʿAlī said: "The wāw was changed to yāʾ, just as they changed yāʾ to wāw in «أَشاوى»." The second: that its origin is rayūḥān, on the pattern fayʿilān, so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and the yāʾ assimilated into it, then it was lightened by dropping the middle letter of the word, as they said kaynūna and baynūna. The original has a doubled yāʾ, which was lightened as hayyin and mayyit were lightened. Makkī said: "Lightening it was necessary because of its length, with the addition of the two extra letters." Then he rejected al-Fārisī's statement on the ground that there is no requirement to turn it into yāʾ, and then said: "Some people said", and mentioned what I gave earlier from Abū ʿAlī to the end.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَبِأَيِّ}: attached to «تُكذِّبان». The majority add «أيّ» to «الآلاء» by annexation. In the whole sūra «أيّ» was also read with tanwīn, and its explanation is that it cut off ayyan from annexation to an implied thing, then made «آلاء ربِّكما» a badal of it, a badal of a definite from an indefinite. The discussion of «الآلاء» and what its singular is was given in al-Aʿrāf, and praise be to Allah. The address in «رَبِّكما»: it was said to the two weighty ones, humans and jinn, because al-anām includes both according to the well-known view; it was said: to male and female; it was said: it is a dual that is meant for one, as in His saying the Exalted {أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ} [Qāf: 24] and the saying of al-Khabīth al-Thaqafī, «يا حَرَسيُّ اضْربا عُنُقَه» ("O guard, strike (dual) his neck"); what is in it has been given. And «كالفَخَّار» is an adjective of ṣalṣāl, and its explanation was given.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
And al-jānn: it was said: it is a generic noun like al-insān. It was said: it is the father of the jinn, Iblīs. It was said: it is their father but not Iblīs.
His saying: {مِن مَّارِجٍ مِّن نَّارٍ}: the first «مِن» is for the beginning of the limit. As for the second there are two views: one, that it is explicative; the second, that it is partitive. Al-mārij: it was said: what is mixed of red, yellow and green, and this is observable in fire, where the three colours are seen mixed with one another. It was said: the pure. It was said: the red. It was said: the redness at the edge of the fire. It was said: what is mixed with black. It was said: the pure. It was said: the flickering flame. And «مِنْ نار» is an adjective of «مارج». His saying «فبأيِّ» to the end is emphasis and repetition, as was given in His saying {وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا القرآن} [al-Qamar: 21] and as in what will come: {وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ} [al-Mursalāt: 15]. A group, among them Ibn Qutayba, held that the repetition is because of the variety of favours, so He repeated the challenge with each single one.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {رَبُّ المشرقين}: the majority read it nominative. There are two views on it. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «مَرَج البحرَيْن», and what is between them is parenthetical. The second: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "He is the Lord", meaning the one who did these things. The third: that it is a badal of the pronoun in «خَلَق». Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ربِّ» genitive, as a badal or bayān of «ربِّكما». Makkī said: "In speech the genitive is allowed as a badal of «ربِّكما»", as if he had not learned that it is a transmitted reading. As for al-mashriqān, it was said: the east of winter and summer and their two wests. It was said: the two easts of the sun and moon and their two wests. It was said: the two easts of the sun only and its two wests. The Shaykh said: "From ʿAbbās: the sun has an east in summer that is ascending, and an east in winter that is descending; it moves between them ascending and descending." The Shaykh said: "So al-mashriqān and al-maghribān are for the sun." I say: This is the statement that says: the east of summer and the east of winter, for by them he means only the sun's and the moon's rising in them, or the sun's rising alone in them, so it falls necessarily within one of the two statements mentioned.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {يَلْتَقِيَانِ}: a ḥāl from «البحرَيْنِ», and it is close to the anticipated ḥāl. It may, with some stretching, be concurrent. And «بينهما بَرْزَخٌ» may be a resumptive clause, or a ḥāl, or the adverbial alone may be the ḥāl, with al-barzakh as agent of it, and this is best because of its nearness to a single word. As for the owner of the ḥāl there are two views: one, that it is «البحرَيْن»; the second, that it is the agent of «يَلْتقيان». And «لا يَبْغِيان» is another ḥāl like the one before it, that is: "He let them flow, not transgressing", or "they meet, not transgressing", or "between them is a barrier in the state of their not transgressing". This ḥāl is in the force of a reason, since the meaning is: "so that they do not transgress". Some have strained and said: the original of that is "so that they do not transgress", then the particle of reason was dropped, which is regular with «أَنْ» and «أَنَّ», then «أَنْ» was also dropped, which is a regular omission, as in His saying the Exalted {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ} [al-Rūm: 24]; so when «أَنْ» was dropped, the verb became nominative. This is not prohibited, except that omission is repeated in it, and he may say: omission has come more than that in what is more hidden than this, as was given in {قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ} [al-Najm: 9], and as will come in His saying {وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 82].

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {يَخْرُجُ}: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr read «يُخْرَج», passive. The rest read active, figuratively. They said: there is an omitted muḍāf, that is: "from one of them", because that is not taken from the sweet sea, so that they faulted the saying:
4171 - فجاءَ بها ما شِئتَ مِنْ لَطَمِيَّةٍ ... على وَجْهِها ماءُ الفُراتِ يموجُ
(And he brought it, as much as you wish of musk-laden wares, on whose surface the water of the Euphrates surges.)
Makkī said: "as He the Exalted said: {على رَجُلٍ مِّنَ القريتين} [al-Zukhruf: 31], that is: from one of the two towns, and the omission of the muḍāf is frequent and common." It was said: it is like His saying {نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا} [al-Kahf: 61], whereas the one who forgot was his servant (Mūsā's young companion); this is attributed to Abū ʿUbayda. It was said: from one of them comes the pearl, and from the other the coral. It was said: rather, both come out from both, and then they mentioned interpretations, among them: that the two come out of the salt sea at the place where the sweet falls into it, and this is observed by divers and is the view of the majority, so attributing it to both is fitting. Among them is the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās: these things come to be in the sea by the falling of rain, and the oysters open their mouths to the rain, and people have witnessed it. Among them: that the sweet in the salt is like fertilization, as it is said that the child comes out from the male and the female. Among them: that it was said «منهما» in that they are one kind, so the coming out of these things is from both, as the Exalted said {وَجَعَلَ القمر فِيهِنَّ نُوراً} [Nūḥ: 16], though it is in only one of them.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why did He say «منهما» when they come out only from the salt? I say: when the two met and became like one thing, it was allowed to say they come out from both, as it is said 'they come out of the sea' and they do not come out of the whole sea, but from part of it. You say 'I went out of the town', though you went out only from a quarter of its quarters, from one house of its houses. It was also said: they come out only from the meeting-place of the salt and the sweet." End of quotation. Some said: the speech of Allah is more deserving of consideration than the speech of some people, so it is possible that He drives them from the sweet sea to the salt, and it happened that they extracted them only from the salt; and if on land there are things hidden from merchants who go back and forth crossing deserts, how much more what is in the depth of the sea? The answer to this: Allah the Exalted addresses people and reminds them of His favour only with what they are familiar with and witness.
Al-luʾluʾ: it was said: the large gems; and al-marjān its small ones; it was also said the reverse, and they quoted al-Aʿshā's saying:
4172 - مِنْ كلِّ مَرْجانةٍ في البحرِ أَحْرَزها ... تَيَّارُها ووقاها طِيْنَها الصَّدَفُ
(Of every pearl in the sea, which its current secured and whose mud the oyster guarded.)
He meant the large pearl. It was said: al-marjān is a red stone. It was said: a very white stone. Al-marjān is non-Arabic. Ibn Durayd said: "I have not heard a conjugated verb from it. And al-luʾluʾ is a rare pattern; only five words have come on this form: al-luʾluʾ, al-juʾjuʾ, which is the chest, al-duʾduʾ, al-yuʾyuʾ for a bird, and al-buʾbuʾ with two bāʾs, which is the original. Al-luʾluʾ with two ḍammas and hamza is the well-known form, and changing the hamza into wāw is common and eloquent, and this was given earlier."
Ṭalḥa read «اللُّؤْلِىءُ» with kasra on the third lām, and it is a preserved dialect. Abū al-Faḍl reported from him «اللُّؤْلِيْ» with the last hamza changed into a yāʾ with sukūn, as if, when he put kasra on what precedes the hamza, he changed it into yāʾ out of heaviness. Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read «يُخْرِجُ», that is, Allah the Exalted. It is also reported from him and from Ibn Miqsam «نُخْرِجُ» with the nūn of majesty. Al-luʾluʾ and al-marjān are accusative in these two readings.

ukberi-tibyan:10-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ (١٠) فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَالنَّخْلُ ذَاتُ الْأَكْمَامِ (١١))
His saying (لِلْأَنَامِ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to وَضَعَهَا.
It is also said: it is attached to what follows it, i.e. "for mankind «فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ»", so it is either the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), or an explanation (tabyīn).

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْحَبُّ ذُو الْعَصْفِ وَالرَّيْحَانُ (١٢))
His saying (وَالْحَبُّ) is read in the nominative, conjoined to «النَّخْلِ», and (وَالرَّيْحَانُ) likewise. It is also read in the accusative, i.e. "and He created الْحَبَّ ذَا الْعَصْفِ, and He created الرَّيْحَانَ".
It is also read الرَّيْحَانِ, in the genitive, conjoined to الْعَصْفِ.

ukberi-tibyan:14-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ صَلْصَالٍ كَالْفَخَّارِ (١٤) وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ مِنْ مَارِجٍ مِنْ نَارٍ (١٥))
His saying (كَالْفَخَّارِ): it is a naʿt (adjective) of صَلْصَالٍ. And (مِنْ نَارٍ) is a naʿt of مَارِجٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:17-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ (١٧) فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ (١٨) مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ (١٩) بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ لَا يَبْغِيَانِ (٢٠))
His saying (رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ): i.e. "He is the Lord". It is also said: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «مَرَجَ».
And (يَلْتَقِيَانِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَلْتَقِيَانِ».
And (لَا يَبْغِيَانِ) is also a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ (٢٢))
His saying (يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا): they said: the implied meaning is "from one of the two":
«[Translator's note: the source text ends here with a colon; nothing follows in the edition used.]»

ukberi-tibyan:24-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَهُ الْجَوَارِ الْمُنْشَآتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ (٢٤) فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ (٢٥) كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ (٢٦))
His saying (الْمُنْشَآتُ): with fatḥa on the shīn, and this is the proper way. (فِي الْبَحْرِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it.
It is also read with kasra on it, i.e. "they bring about (tunshiʾu) the voyage", and this is figurative.
And (كَالْأَعْلَامِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «الْمُنْشَآتُ». The hāʾ in «عَلَيْهَا» refers to the earth, and its mention has preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَبْقَى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ (٢٧))
His saying (ذُو الْجَلَالِ): in the nominative it is a naʿt (adjective) of الْوَجْه; and in the genitive [ذِي] it is a naʿt of the genitive noun [رَبِّكَ].

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَسْأَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ (٢٩))
His saying (كُلَّ يَوْمٍ): it is an adverb (ẓarf) for what is indicated by «هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ», i.e. "He turns affairs about every day".

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ الثَّقَلَانِ (٣١))
His saying (سَنَفْرُغُ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the rāʾ; it has also been read with fatḥa on it because of the guttural letter, and its past tense is فَرَغَ with fatḥa on the rāʾ.
فَرِغَ with kasra on the rāʾ has also been heard for it, so it takes fatḥa in the imperfect, like نَصِبَ يَنْصَبُ.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا مِنْ أَقْطَارِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا لَا تَنْفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطَانٍ (٣٣))
His saying (لَا تَنْفُذُونَ): لَا is negating, in the sense of «مَا».

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُمَا شُوَاظٌ مِنْ نَارٍ وَنُحَاسٌ فَلَا تَنْتَصِرَانِ (٣٥))
And (شُوَاظٌ) with ḍamma and with kasra are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both. And (مِنْ نَارٍ) is an adjective (ṣifa), or attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb.
(وَنُحَاسٌ) in the nominative is conjoined to شُوَاظٍ, and in the genitive it is conjoined to نَارٍ; the nominative is stronger in meaning, because النُّحَاسُ is smoke, and that is the شُوَاظُ (flame) of the fire.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَالدِّهَانِ (٣٧))
And (الدِّهَانُ) is the plural of دُهْنٍ (oil); it is also said: it is a singular, meaning a leather mat (النِّطْعُ).

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُسْأَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إِنْسٌ وَلَا جَانٌّ (٣٩))
(جَانٌّ) is the fāʿil (agent) [i.e. the deputy agent of the passive verb].
It is also read with a hamza [جَأْنٌّ], because the alif was given a vowel and so changed into a hamza; this was mentioned in al-Fātiḥa.
«[Translator's note: the source calls جَانٌّ a fāʿil although يُسْأَلُ is passive; the bracketed clarification is added.]»

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ (٤٤))
His saying (يَطُوفُونَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْمُجْرِمِينَ», and it may be resumptive.
And (آنٍ) is an active participle (fāʿil-pattern), like قَاضٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَوَاتَا أَفْنَانٍ (٤٨))
His saying (ذَوَاتَا): the alif before the tāʾ is a replacement for a yāʾ; it is also said: for a wāw. It is an adjective (ṣifa) of جَنَّتَانِ, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). And الْأَفْنَانُ is the plural of فَنَنٍ, which is a branch.

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى فُرُشٍ بَطَائِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ دَانٍ (٥٤))
His saying (مُتَّكِئِينَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «خَافَ», and what governs it is the adverbial expression (al-ẓarf).
His saying (مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ): the origin of the word is a verb on the pattern اسْتَفْعَلَ; when it was used as a name, its hamza was made a disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ). It is also said: it is foreign (aʿjamī).
It has also been read with the hamza dropped and kasra on the nūn. This is a mistake, because that does not occur in nouns, but only in maṣdars and verbs.

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فِيهِنَّ قَاصِرَاتُ الطَّرْفِ لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلَا جَانٌّ (٥٦))
His saying (فِيهِنَّ): the pronoun may refer to the dwellings of the two gardens, or to the couches (الْفُرُش), i.e. "upon them". And الطَّرْف was made singular because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).
And (لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ) is a description of قَاصِرَاتِ, because the annexation is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa); and likewise «كَأَنَّهُنَّ الْيَاقُوتُ».
«[Translator's note: the source has الظَّرْفُ ("the adverb") where the context requires الطَّرْفُ ("the glance"); it is translated here as الطَّرْف.]»

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ (٦٠))
And (الْإِحْسَانِ) [i.e. the second الْإِحْسَانُ] is the khabar (predicate) of جَزَاءُ, and إِلَّا entered in accordance with the meaning [the interrogative having the sense of negation].
«[Translator's note: the bracketed clarifications are added.]»

ukberi-tibyan:70-72.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فِيهِنَّ خَيْرَاتٌ حِسَانٌ (٧٠) فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ (٧١) حُورٌ مَقْصُورَاتٌ فِي الْخِيَامِ (٧٢))
His saying (خَيْرَاتٌ): it is the plural of خَيْرَةٍ; one says: امْرَأَةٌ خَيْرَةٌ (a good woman). It has also been read with a doubled yāʾ. And (حُورٌ) is a badal (substitute) from «خَيْرَاتٌ». It is also said: the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "in them are حُورٌ".

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ وَعَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسَانٍ (٧٦))
And (مُتَّكِئِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) is omitted, indicated by the pronoun in «قَبْلَهُمْ».
And (رَفْرَفٍ) has a plural meaning; that is why it is described by «خُضْرٍ». It has also been read رَفْرَافٍ, and likewise «عَبْقَرِيٍّ».

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تَبَارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ (٧٨))
And (ذِي الْجَلَالِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of رَبِّكَ; this is stronger than the nominative, because the name (al-ism) is not so described. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الرَّحْمَنُ (١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الرَّحْمَنُ): some held that it is (by itself) a verse; on this view the implied wording is "Allah is the Most Merciful" (اللَّهُ الرَّحْمَنُ), so that the speech is complete. According to the view of the others, «الرَّحْمَنُ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:3-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ (٣) عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيَانَ (٤)).
And (خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ) is resumptive, and likewise «عَلَّمَهُ». It may also be an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial) from الْإِنْسَان, with «قَدْ» intended with it.

ukberi-tibyan:5-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ (٥) وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ (٦) وَالسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِحُسْبَانٍ), i.e. "they run by a reckoning". (وَالسَّمَاءَ) in the accusative by an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned; this is preferable to the nominative because it is conjoined to a noun that a verb has governed, namely the pronoun in «يَسْجُدَانِ»; or it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الْإِنْسَانَ».

ukberi-tibyan:8-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزَانِ (٨) وَأَقِيمُوا الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ وَلَا تُخْسِرُوا الْمِيزَانَ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ لَا تَطْغَوْا), i.e. "so that you do not transgress" (لِئَلَّا تَطْغَوْا).
It is also said that «لَا» is for prohibition, and أَنْ means "that is" (أَيْ, explicative), the verb of saying being implied. And (تُخْسِرُوا) with ḍamma on the tāʾ, i.e. "and do not diminish what is weighed".
It is also said that the implied wording is "in the balance". It is also read with fatḥa on the sīn and the tāʾ (تَخْسَرُوا), its past tense being خَسِرَ; the first is sounder.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Raḥmān
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ ﴿عَلَّمَ القُرْآنَ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 2]: "اَلرَّحْمَنُ" is one of the names of Allah the Exalted; it is not said of anyone other than Him. It is in the earlier scriptures, and its meaning is: the One abundant in mercy.

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying: ﴿والأرْضَ وضَعَها لِلأنامِ﴾: "اَلْأنامُ" means humans and jinn.

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيها فاكِهَةٌ والنَّخْلُ ذاتُ الأكْمامِ﴾: the meaning of ﴿الأكْمامِ﴾ is: that which covers. Every tree that puts forth something sheathed has akmām (sheaths). The akmām of the palm tree are what cover its heart (jummār) of fronds, fibre and trunk; and everything the palm tree puts forth has sheaths: the spathe's sheath (kumm) is its husk. From this the cap is called "kumma", because it covers the head, and from this come "the two sleeves (kummā) of the shirt", because they cover the hands.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والحَبُّ ذُو العَصْفِ والرَّيْحانُ﴾, and it is also read "والرَّيْحانَ", but the majority reading is ﴿والرَّيْحانُ﴾. Al-ʿaṣf is the leaves of the crop; it is also said that straw is al-ʿaṣf, and one also says al-ʿaṣfa. The poet said:
؎تَسْقِي مَذانِبَ قَدْ مالَتْ عَصِيفَتُها ∗∗∗ آتِيُّها مِن أتِيِّ الماءِ مَطْمُومُ
(It waters channels whose blades of crop have bent over; their inflow is brimming from the inflowing water.)
It is also transmitted "بِأتِيِّ الماءِ". The meaning of ﴿ذُو العَصْفِ والرَّيْحانُ﴾ is: having leaves and provision. The Arabs say "subḥāna llāhi wa-rayḥānahu", and the philologists said its meaning is "and [I seek] His provision". Al-Namir ibn Tawlab said:
؎سَلامُ الإلَهِ ورَيْحانُهُ ∗∗∗ ورَحْمَتُهُ وسَماءٌ دُرَرْ
(The peace of God and His rayḥān, His mercy, and a sky pouring abundantly.)
He said: the meaning of "رَيْحانُهُ" is His provision. Whoever reads "والرَّيْحانِ" «[Translator's note: the source here has the genitive, whereas the variant cited above was written with the accusative, والرَّيْحانَ.]» conjoins it to "اَلْعَصْفِ"; and whoever reads ﴿والرَّيْحانُ﴾ conjoins it to ﴿الحَبِّ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 95] «[Translator's note: so in the printed text; the reference is to الحَبُّ in this verse, al-Raḥmān: 12.]». The meaning would then be: "In them both there is fruit; in them both are grain with husks; and in them both is rayḥān." So "اَلرَّيْحانُ" here would be the fragrant plant that is smelled, and it may also here be provision.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned in this sūra what indicates His oneness: the creation of man, the teaching of clear speech, and the creation of the sun, the moon, the sky and the earth. Then He addressed humans and jinn, saying: "فَبِأيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ", that is: which of the favours of your Lord, among these things mentioned, do you both deny? For all of them are favours bestowed upon you, in their guiding you to His oneness, and in His providing you with what sustains you and is the means to your life. "اَلْآلاءُ": its singular is "ألًى" and "إلًى". And everywhere in the sūra that His saying "فَبِأيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ" occurs, its meaning is as we have explained: So which of the favours of your Lord do you both deny?!

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَلَقَ الإنْسانَ مِن صَلْصالٍ كالفَخّارِ﴾. And He said elsewhere: ﴿إنّا خَلَقْناهم مِن طِينٍ لازِبٍ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 11], and He said: ﴿مِن حَمَإٍ مَسْنُونٍ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 26], and He said: ﴿إنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسى عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرابٍ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 59]. These expressions from which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said that He created man differ in wording, but in meaning they go back to a single origin, for the origin of clay is dust. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He created Adam from dust, which was made into clay, then it changed and became like black mud, then it changed and became ṣalṣāl like pottery — ṣalṣāl being the dry [clay]. All of this has dust as its origin, and there is nothing in it that contradicts any other part. We have explained this only because a group of heretics ask about the like of this in order to confuse the weak. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known from what He created the father of all humans, Adam, peace be upon him, and made known from what He created the origin of the jinn, saying: ﴿وَخَلَقَ الجانَّ مِن مارِجٍ مِن نارٍ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 15]. "اَلْمارِجُ" is the flame mixed with the blackness of the fire.

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبُّ المَشْرِقَيْنِ ورَبُّ المَغْرِبَيْنِ﴾: by this He means the two rising-places of the sun, and likewise the moon, and the two setting-places of the sun and the moon. One of the two rising-places is the rising-place of winter and the other the rising-place of summer, and likewise the two setting-places.

zajjaj:19-19.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَرَجَ البَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيانِ﴾: the meaning of "مَرَجَ" is: He mixed; meaning the salt sea and the fresh sea. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿بَيْنَهُما بَرْزَخٌ لا يَبْغِيانِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 20]: "اَلْبَرْزَخُ" is the barrier, and it is a barrier from the power of Allah. "لا يَبْغِيانِ": the salt does not encroach upon the fresh so as to mix with it, nor the fresh upon the salt so as to mix with it.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying: ﴿عَلَّمَ القُرْآنَ﴾: its meaning is: He made it easy to be remembered.

zajjaj:22-22.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنهُما اللُّؤْلُؤُ والمَرْجانُ﴾: "اَلْمَرْجانُ" is small pearls, and "اَللُّؤْلُؤُ" is a comprehensive name for the beads that come out of the sea. He said ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنهُما﴾ (comes out of them both) although it comes out only of the salt sea, because He had mentioned them both and joined them together; so if it comes out of one of them, it has come out of them both. Similar to this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 15] ﴿وَجَعَلَ القَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِراجًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 16], while the sun is in the lowest heaven; but since He mentioned the seven collectively, what is in one of them is in them. It is also read "يُخْرَجُ مِنهُما" (is brought out of them both), with ḍamma on the yāʾ.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَهُ الجَوارِ المُنْشَآتُ في البَحْرِ كالأعْلامِ﴾: "اَلْجَوارِي" — the pause on it is with the yāʾ; the yāʾ dropped in pronunciation only because of the quiescence of the lām «[Translator's note: i.e. the lām of the following article (al-munshaʾāt), with which the long vowel cannot meet.]», and the preferred way is to pronounce it in connection. If someone pauses on it without the yāʾ, that is permissible though far-fetched, but he should give a faint hint (rawm) of the kasra on the rāʾ to indicate the omission of the yāʾ. It is also read "اَلْمُنْشِئاتُ", with kasra on the shīn, but fatḥa on the shīn is better. The meaning of "اَلْمُنْشَآتُ" is: those whose sails are raised; and "اَلْمُنْشِئاتُ" is in the sense of those that carry and raise the sails. The meaning of "كالأعْلامِ" is: like mountains. The poet said:
؎إذا قَطَعْنَ عَلَمًا بَدا عَلَمْ
(Whenever they cross one mountain, another mountain appears.)
And "اَلْجَوارِي" are the ships.

zajjaj:26-26.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلُّ مَن عَلَيْها فانٍ﴾: its meaning is: on the earth.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿خَلَقَ الإنْسانَ﴾ ﴿عَلَّمَهُ البَيانَ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 4]: it has been said that by "man" here He means the Prophet ﷺ, and "عَلَّمَهُ البَيانَ" means "He taught him the Qurʾān, in which is the clear explanation of everything". And it has been said: "man" here is Adam ﷺ. And it is permissible in the language for "الإنْسانَ" to be a name for the genus of all people; on this meaning "عَلَّمَهُ البَيانَ" means: He made him discerning, so that man became distinct from all the animals.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿الشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ بِحُسْبانٍ﴾: "اَلشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ" are both nominative as subjects (by ibtidāʾ, the mubtadaʾ).
And His saying ﴿بِحُسْبانٍ﴾ indicates the khabar (predicate) of the subject; the meaning is: "The sun and the moon run by reckoning." And the meaning of ﴿بِحُسْبانٍ﴾ may also be that they both indicate the number of the months and years and all times.

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والنَّجْمُ والشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدانِ﴾: the philologists and most of the exegetes said: "اَلنَّجْمُ" is everything that grows on the face of the earth that has no stalk, and "اَلشَّجَرُ" is everything that has a stalk. The meaning of their prostration is the turning of the shade with them, as He said: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إلى ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِن شَيْءٍ يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلالُهُ عَنِ اليَمِينِ والشَّمائِلِ سُجَّدًا لِلَّهِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 48]. It has also been said that by al-najm the stars are meant, and this may be so, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has informed us that the stars prostrate, saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ والشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ والنُّجُومُ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 18]. And it may be that by al-najm here He means both what grows on the face of the earth and what rises of the stars of the sky; of everything that rises (ṭalaʿa) one says "qad najama" (it has appeared).

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿والسَّماءَ رَفَعَها ووَضَعَ المِيزانَ﴾: the meaning is: "He raised it above the earth and held it back from falling onto the earth, and He set up the balance so that people may obtain justice from one another." And it has been said: "اَلْمِيزانُ" here is justice, because equity (al-muʿādala) is the weighing of things against one another.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿ألا تَطْغَوْا في المِيزانِ﴾: that you do not exceed the measure and justice. ﴿ألا تَطْغَوْا﴾ may be in the sense of the lām: "so that you do not transgress"; and ﴿ألا تَطْغَوْا﴾ may be a prohibition, with "أنْ" having the explicative sense (al-tafsīr), so that the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "And He set up the balance", that is: "Do not transgress in the balance." This is indicated by what is conjoined to it, namely His saying: ﴿وَأقِيمُوا الوَزْنَ بِالقِسْطِ ولا تُخْسِرُوا المِيزانَ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 9]. The reading is with ḍamma on the tāʾ. The philologists have transmitted "akhsarta l-mīzāna" and "khasarta" (you made the balance deficient); on "khasarta" it would be "وَلا تَخْسِرُوا". But do not read it so unless a sound transmission from an imam of reading is established. It has been reported that a certain person among the early ones read it so, but he is not one from whom reading was taken, nor does he have a reading (ḥarf) according to which people read.

zajjaj:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿سَنَفْرُغُ لَكم أيُّهَ الثَّقَلانِ﴾: by al-thaqalān (the two weighty ones) He means humans and jinn. "سَنَفْرَغُ لَكُمْ" with fatḥa on the rāʾ is permissible; "سَيَفْرُغُ" with fatḥa on the yāʾ is permissible; and "سَيُفْرَغُ لَكُمْ" with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ is permissible. Its meaning is: We shall turn to your reckoning — and Allah is not distracted by one matter from another. Farāgh in the language is of two kinds: one of them is being free from an occupation, and the other is directing oneself to a thing. You say "qad faraghtu mimmā kuntu fīhi" (I have finished with what I was engaged in), that is: my occupation with it has ceased; and you say "sa-atafarraghu li-fulān" (I shall devote myself to So-and-so), that is: I shall make him my aim.

zajjaj:33-33.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا مَعْشَرَ الجِنِّ والإنْسِ إنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أنْ تَنْفُذُوا مِن أقْطارِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: al-aqṭār are the regions. ﴿لا تَنْفُذُونَ إلا بِسُلْطانٍ﴾, that is: wherever you are, you witness a proof and an authority from Allah indicating that He is One.

zajjaj:35-35.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُما شُواظٌ مِن نارٍ ونُحاسٌ﴾, and it is also read "وَنُحاسٍ", with kasra on the sīn. Al-nuḥās is smoke, and al-shuwāẓ is the flame that has no smoke with it.

zajjaj:37-37.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإذا انْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ ورْدَةً كالدِّهانِ﴾: the meaning of ﴿وَرْدَةً﴾ is: it became like the colour of the rose, and that is on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of ﴿كالدِّهانِ﴾ is: it changes colour from the greatest terror, as the various oils change colour; al-dihān is the plural of "دُهْنٍ" (oil). The evidence for this is His saying ﴿يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّماءُ كالمُهْلِ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 8], that is: like oil that has been boiled. And it has been said: ﴿فَكانَتْ ورْدَةً كالدِّهانِ﴾ means it became like the colour of a ward (bay-red) horse; "al-kumayt" is al-ward, whose colour changes, so that in winter its colour differs from its colour in summer, and in the season [between] its colour is other than its colour in winter and summer «[Translator's note: the bracketed word is added for clarity.]».

zajjaj:39-39.t:
﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُسْألُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إنْسٌ ولا جانٌّ﴾, while He said elsewhere: ﴿وَقِفُوهم إنَّهم مَسْؤُولُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 24]. When that day comes, the mark of the criminals will be blackness of the face and blueness [of the eyes] «[Translator's note: the bracketed words are added for clarity.]». The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿يُعْرَفُ المُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيماهم فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّواصِي والأقْدامِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 41], that is: by this mark of theirs; and the evidence for that is His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 106].
And His saying: ﴿وَنَحْشُرُ المُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 102].

zajjaj:41-41.t: And His saying: ﴿فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّواصِي والأقْدامِ﴾: it has been said: the feet are joined to the forelocks from behind, and they are cast into the Fire; and that is more severe in their punishment and in their disfigurement.

zajjaj:43-44.t: And His saying: ﴿هَذِهِ جَهَنَّمُ الَّتِي يُكَذِّبُ بِها المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ ﴿يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَها وبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ﴾: ﴿آنٍ﴾ is from "qad aniya, yaʾnā, fa-huwa ānin", when something reaches the utmost in cooking and heat. When they cry for relief from the Fire, their relief is made the boiling water (al-ḥamīm al-ānī) which has become like molten metal (al-muhl); so they are taken round, once to the boiling water and once to the Fire — I seek refuge with Allah and His mercy from it. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known what there is for whoever fears Him and is in awe of Him, saying: ﴿وَلِمَن خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتانِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 46]. It has been said: whoever intends a sin, then remembers what he will bear for it, and abandons it out of fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, dread of His punishment and hope for His reward, will have two gardens. Then He described them, saying: ﴿ذَواتا أفْنانٍ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 48]. Al-afnān is the plural of "fann" (kind), that is: he will have in them whatever souls desire and eyes delight in, of every kind; so "al-afnān" means the varieties. And "al-afnān" also means the branches, whose singular is "fanan"; and this is the better of the two views.

zajjaj:52-52.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيهِما مِن كُلِّ فاكِهَةٍ زَوْجانِ﴾: "اَلزَّوْجانِ" means the two kinds.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
And His saying: ﴿فِيهِنَّ قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ﴾: its meaning is: in them are ḥūr who restrain their glances, who have confined their glances to their husbands and do not look at others.
﴿لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إنْسٌ قَبْلَهم ولا جانٌّ﴾: no one has touched them. It is also read "لَمْ يَطْمُثْهُنَّ", but that is rare in reading; in the language one says "ṭamatha, yaṭmithu and yaṭmuthu". In this verse there is evidence that the jinnī has intercourse, just as the human has intercourse.

zajjaj:58-58.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَأنَّهُنَّ الياقُوتُ والمَرْجانُ﴾: the exegetes and the philologists said: they are in the clarity of rubies and the whiteness of marjān; al-marjān is small pearls, and it is whiter.
And His saying: ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 56] — while He mentioned only two gardens — means: in these two gardens and what has been prepared for the person in this account besides these two gardens.

zajjaj:60-60.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلْ جَزاءُ الإحْسانِ إلا الإحْسانُ﴾, that is: the recompense of one who did good in this world is nothing but that good be done to him in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:62-62.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن دُونِهِما جَنَّتانِ﴾, that is: for whoever fears the standing before his Lord there are two gardens, and besides them he has two [more] gardens «[Translator's note: the bracketed word is added for clarity.]». "اَلْجَنَّةُ" in the language of the Arabs is the orchard.

zajjaj:64-64.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُدْهامَّتانِ﴾: meaning that they are both green, their greenness verging on black. With every green plant, the fullness of its greenness and its being well-watered is that it verges on black.

zajjaj:66-66.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيهِما عَيْنانِ نَضّاخَتانِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that they both gush forth every good thing.

zajjaj:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيهِما فاكِهَةٌ ونَخْلٌ ورُمّانٌ﴾: some people said that palm trees and pomegranates are not among fruit. But some of the philologists — among them Yūnus the grammarian, who comes next after al-Khalīl in seniority and skill — said that pomegranates and palms are among the most excellent of fruit, and they were separated by the wāw only because of their excellence. He cited as evidence for that His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿مَن كانَ عَدُوًّا لِلَّهِ ومَلائِكَتِهِ ورُسُلِهِ وجِبْرِيلَ ومِيكالَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 98], and said: because of their excellence they were separated by the wāw.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى فُرُشٍ بَطائِنُها مِن إسْتَبْرَقٍ وجَنى الجَنَّتَيْنِ دانٍ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 54]: it has been said: "اَلْإسْتَبْرَقُ" is very thick brocade, like what is made for the Kaʿba; and "اَلْبَطائِنُ" (the linings) are what is next to the ground.
And His saying: ﴿وَجَنى الجَنَّتَيْنِ دانٍ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 54], that is: what is picked of their fruit, when they want it, comes near to their mouths, so that they take it with their mouths and hands.

zajjaj:70-70.t: And His saying: ﴿فِيهِنَّ خَيْراتٌ حِسانٌ﴾: its origin in the language is "خَيِّراتٌ", and the meaning is that they are good in character and beautiful in form. It has been read so — I mean with a doubled yāʾ.

zajjaj:72-72.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حُورٌ مَقْصُوراتٌ في الخِيامِ﴾: "اَلْخِيامُ" in the language of the Arabs is the plural of khayma (tent). And "al-khiyām" are two things: al-khiyām are the camel-litters (hawādij), and al-khiyām are the dwellings. It has come in the exegesis that each tent of these tents is of a hollowed pearl. The meaning of ﴿مَقْصُوراتٌ﴾ is: secluded, confined to their husbands.

zajjaj:76-76.t:
And His saying: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ وعَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسانٍ﴾, and it has also been read "عَلى رَفارِفَ خُضْرٍ وعَباقِرِيَّ حِسانٍ". The reading is the first one; this reading has no justification in Arabic, because a plural with two letters after its alif, like "مَساجِدُ" and "مَفاتِيحُ", does not admit a form like "عَباقِرِيَّ", since what exceeds three letters is not pluralised with the yāʾ of relation (yāʾ al-nisba). If you pluralised "عَبْقَرِيٌّ", its plural would be "عَباقِرَةٌ", just as if you pluralised "مُهَلَّبِيٌّ" its plural would be "مَهالِبَةٌ" — one does not say "مَهالِبِيُّ".
If someone asks: how then is "عَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسانٍ" permissible, when "عَبْقَرِيٍّ" is singular and "حِسانٌ" is plural? The basis is that its singular is "عَبْقَرِيَّةٌ" and the plural (collective) is "عَبْقَرِيٌّ", as you say "ثَمَرَةٌ" and "ثَمَرٌ", "لَوْزَةٌ" and "لَوْزٌ"; and "عَبْقَرِيٌّ" may also be a generic noun. So the reading is the first one.
As for the explanation of ﴿رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ وعَبْقَرِيٍّ﴾: they said al-rafraf here is the meadows of Paradise; they said al-rafraf is cushions; they said it is maḥābis (covers); and they also said it is the overhanging parts of the covers of the furnishings. As for al-ʿabqarī, they said it is carpets, and they said it is spread-out rugs (ṭanāfis). What indicates this in the Qurʾān is His saying: ﴿وَنَمارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 15] ﴿وَزَرابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 16]: al-namāriq are cushions and al-zarābī are carpets. So the meaning of "رَفْرَفٍ" here and "عَبْقَرِيٍّ" is cushions and carpets; and it indicates — and Allah knows best — that the cushions have fringes (rafraf). The origin of "اَلْعَبْقَرِيُّ" in the language is a description of everything whose description is carried to the extreme. Its origin is that "ʿAbqar" was the name of a land in which carpets and other things were embroidered, so every excellent thing, and everything whose description is carried to the extreme, was attributed to "ʿAbqar". Zuhayr said:
؎بِخَيْلٍ عَلَيْها جِنَّةٌ عَبْقَرِيَّةٌ ∗∗∗ جَدِيرُونَ يَوْمًا أنْ يَنالُوا فَيَسْتَعْلُوا
(With horses bearing riders like the jinn of ʿAbqar, worthy one day to attain [their aim] and prevail.)

zajjaj:77-77.t: And His saying: ﴿فَبِأيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ﴾, that is: which of the favours of your Lord that have been enumerated to you, O company of jinn and humans, do you both deny? Rather, you ought to glorify Allah and extol Him. So He closed the sūra with that by which He, Mighty and Majestic is He, ought to be extolled and glorified, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَبارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي الجَلالِ والإكْرامِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 78].
